Lee Child has handed the Jack Reacher book franchise over to his brother, leaving many readers angry – and he’s now addressed the furious backlash.

Since 1997, the British author has written 30 novels focused on the hulking action hero and co-authored six with his sibling, Andrew Grant, before retiring and giving him full creative control of the best-selling series.

However, despite the books co-written with Grant being a success, Child – real name James Grant – said that long-time Reacher fans have been “funny” about the development.

open image in gallery Jack Reacher author Lee Child has retired from franchise ( PA Archive )

“They believe Reacher is their property and anybody who messes with him is messing with their thing,” he said in a new interview. “So there’s been a bit of grumpiness from some of the readers simply because something has changed. But other than that I think it’s been fairly seamless.”

He told The Times: “Stieg Larsson wrote three books in the Girl with the Dragon Tattoo series before he died. Then a fourth one was ghostwritten from Sweden by David Lagercrantz. I was asked by The New York Times to review that. I became fascinated to what degree does the identity of the author matter? My conclusion was you can get away with it if you’re careful.”

Child’s name appears with his brother’s pen name, Andrew Child, on the book covers after “toying with the idea of having no author’s name on the book at all”, which he said looked too “weird”.

The Reacher franchise was adapted into two Tom Cruise films – Jack Reacher in 2012 and Jack Reacher: Never Go Back in 2016 – and is currently a hit Prime Video series starring Alan Ritchson.

In 2025, Child told The Independent that readers were right to disapprove of Cruise’s casting as the character; many didn’t think the Hollywood star was right for the role due to his height. In Child’s books, Reacher is described as being “extremely tall” (he’s 6ft, 5in), and “extremely broad, long-armed and long-legged”. In real life, Cruise is 5ft, 7in.

Child said that, while he “liked” working with Cruise, “the readers, ultimately, were right” in their views.

open image in gallery Tom Cruise and Alan Ritchson as very different versions of Jack Reacher ( Paramount Pictures / Prime Video )

“I thought the first movie in particular was excellent. It was a really crisp hard-edged thriller. Working with Tom was a pleasure and a privilege – he’s a really smart guy, he’s a smart filmmaker, he’s real fun. But you cannot escape the fact that Reacher is a huge guy.”

He added: “I mean, that is a component in his entire approach to the world and the world’s approach to him. He’s huge, he’s implacable, he’s scary, and for all Tom’s ability in getting the internals of Reacher out, he is not huge and he’s not scary. So the readers were terribly upset about it and I think, ultimately, the readers were right.”

The author thinks they have struck gold with Ritchson, who is returning to play the role in a fourth season based on Child’s 13th Reacher book Gone Tomorrow. According to the author: “Alan was born to play Reacher and I think he knows that.”

Elsewhere in his new interview, Child criticised another book series-turned-action franchise that has been taken over by Amazon: James Bond. He said Amazon’s purchase of 007 was “interesting” because he feels the character is “word out” and “still has distinctly postwar roots”, which he said “needs to move on”.

Recreating the environmental context under which a memory is formed might help it resurface even if it is seemingly forgotten, a new study involving fruit flies suggests.

Memories are notoriously imperfect, with some fading over time while others remain hidden altogether until they are brought back by reminders.

The research suggests that some forgotten memories are not completely erased, but can persist in the brain in a silent form that can later be recovered.

It still remains unclear how the brain accurately recovers some memories and ends up forming false ones.

“The neuronal processes governing true memory recovery and false memory formation remain poorly understood,” write researchers in the study published in the journal Nature Neuroscience.

This fruit fly study now provides fresh clues to how memories work.

open image in gallery A view of an interactive display of the human brain ( AFP via Getty Images )

In the study, Swiss researchers trained the flies to associate an odour with mild electric shocks.

While the flies avoided that odour immediately after training, 24 hours later this learned avoidance had faded, seemingly forgotten.

But when scientists recreated the original training setting and exposed the flies to the same odour, the aversive memory was recovered, and the flies avoided the odour again.

The reminder only worked when the training chamber's original texture and lighting were recreated, hinting that the environmental context helped bring the memory back.

Peering into the flies’ brains, scientists found that the original pattern of nerve activity linked to the memory faded over time.

But a silent trace of the memory remained in different groups of neurons, researchers found.

This trace could be reactivated with a specific reminder, they found.

“From this silent state, reminders recover memory expression by reinstating the original memory trace,” researchers wrote.

open image in gallery The fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster ( Ryszard via Eurekalert )

Scientists also found that the flies formed “false memories” in some cases.

In another experiment, the flies were subject to a second odour that was not paired with a shock.

When scientists later used that harmless odour as the reminder, the flies began avoiding it too.

“Manipulating reminders can distort recovery, leading to false memory formation,” they explained.

open image in gallery All 139,255 brain cells in the brain of an adult fruit fly ( Princeton University via Eurekalert )

Researchers found that the brain pathways involved in forming the false memory were different from those used to recover the true memory.

This suggests, at least in fruit flies, the brain may process recovered and distorted memories through distinct nerve circuits.

While fly memory is not the same as human recollection, the findings offer an example of how remembering can depend on the context of stored information, scientists say.

“Together, these findings suggest that forgotten memories can re-emerge through a reconstructive process,” they concluded.

Immigration and Customs Enforcement is set to equip its officers with body cameras within the next two months, but agency policy grants leadership extensive control over which footage is made public, stipulating that releases must be in its "best interests."

The nationwide rollout, expected to finish by the end of September, follows years of delays and heightened scrutiny following recent fatal officer-involved shootings. Critics warn that the policy allows the ICE director broad discretion to selectively release footage that casts the agency favorably while keeping controversial encounters secret.

Under the policy issued in February 2025, officers must activate cameras during routine enforcement activities, including arrests, search warrants, and emergency responses.

open image in gallery Protesters holding signs and candles line the roadway during a vigil for a Mexican man who was struck and killed by a tractor trailer while running from an encounter with Immigration and Customs Enforcements officers ( AP Photo/Kelly Jordan )

Following serious incidents or shootings, a committee of top officials and attorneys will review footage and make a release recommendation, which can occur within 72 hours.

However, the ICE director retains authority to block or indefinitely delay releases citing "specific and compelling circumstances." Furthermore, the policy mandates redacting identifying features like faces, names, and badge numbers to protect officer privacy.

Federal spending records indicate ICE spent $30.9 million in July to purchase body-worn camera equipment from Axon under an existing contract.

open image in gallery Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents walk to close a gate outside of Delaney Hall detention center, after a Salvadoran immigrant, Edwin Lopez-Cornejo, who was being held inside died ( Reuters )

The purchase came shortly after two fatal shootings by ICE officers in Maine and Houston, neither of which was recorded on body cameras. Congress had previously allocated $20 million for ICE body cameras in an April 30 spending bill.

At least one member of every arrest team will be required to wear a camera. Over half of field officers have received the equipment, with remaining deployments slated for completion by late September—slightly behind earlier estimates provided to lawmakers.

Supporters, including White House border czar Tom Homan, argue the devices provide transparency and frequently exonerate officers. Critics, including criminal justice researchers and former agency officials, contend the policy creates image-management tools that allow selective disclosures rather than true public accountability.

open image in gallery White House border czar Tom Homan said July 19 on CBS News’ "Face the Nation." "And if you look at the data, body cameras actually exonerate agents more than they, you know, provide evidence of wrongdoing." ( Getty )

Homan argued on CBS News’ "Face the Nation" on July 19, "I think the American people need to see what that officer sees and hears. And if you look at the data, body cameras actually exonerate agents more than they, you know, provide evidence of wrongdoing."

However, Schneider anticipates that ICE will selectively release recordings that promote the agency’s mass deportation program, portraying officers as brave and immigrants as dangerous criminals. "Much of what law enforcement does is convince the public that we need them and feel safe and they do all this good stuff for us," he said.

"The more bad stuff the public sees, the more angry the public gets. And this causes problems for the police brand."

open image in gallery A detained woman sits inside a vehicle surrounded by federal agents, as immigration enforcement continues after a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent fatally shot Renee Nicole Good on January 7 ( Reuters )

ICE began testing body cameras in 2021 during President Joe Biden’s administration and distributed 1,400 devices three years later, citing plans for expanded use as funding became available. After returning to office in 2025, Donald Trump rescinded a Biden order that mandated federal law enforcement agencies use body cameras.

ICE did not purchase body cameras even after receiving a historic $75 billion infusion in Donald Trump’s signature policy bill in 2025 and subsequently hiring thousands of new officers. The two July purchases from Axon were made through an existing government contract that began in 2023, records show.

"This is not hard to deploy, but they’ve slow-rolled it," said Jason Houser, who served as ICE chief of staff under Biden and helped implement the agency’s pilot program. Houser contended that the Donald Trump administration should have equipped officers with body cameras when it expanded mass arrests and traffic stops.

He described the current rollout, occurring only after several shootings and congressional pressure, as "clearly a political response" that will not enhance the safety of officers or the public.

"This doesn’t fix the problem of putting officers in a place where they’re not trained or equipped to carry out the style of operations that the administration is asking them to do," he added.

News.title: Best bath towels to make your bathroom feel like a spa, reviewed by a home expert
News.content:
Shopping for the best bath towels may seem low-stakes, but I’d argue they’re almost as important as the fixtures and fittings of the room itself. The right one can make every trip feel like a spa-like experience, which is no mean feat for what is often the busiest room of the house.

A highly absorbent towel not only gets you dry quickly, but prevents water from flooding your floors. A stylish towel can inject colour and texture too, helpful in a space that’s primarily made up of tile, mirror and glass.

So, how to choose? Well, first off, consider your towel’s primary function and whether it’s going to be for everyday use, a guest towel or the gym (fast-drying cotton-polyester blends are best here).

What is GSM in towels? GSM (grams per square metre) is the scale on which towel quality and weightiness is measured. The higher the GSM, the more absorbent and thicker the towel will be. A good rule of thumb? Choose anything that’s 600GSM or above. High GSM towels are usually more expensive and take longer to dry. But if you’re looking for hotel-level softness, these are small thorns to bear.

If you’re looking for a towel to dry your hair without wreaking havoc on fragile wet strands, try microfibre fabric or something crafted from flat-woven smooth cotton like a peshtemal, also known as a hammam towel. And for your face? Muslin cloths, soft cotton, and ultra-fine microfibre are great for removing every last trace of make-up without leaving skin feeling or looking raw. Frankly, it’s easy to see how Monica Gellar got to 11 categories of towel in Friends.

For bath towels, choosing one that’s made of 100 per cent cotton is your best bet. Breathable, absorbent, and plush, it’s hard to settle for anything less.

Ready to dive in? I’ve used, washed and dried a range of the bath towels to find the very best across a range of price points. Keep reading to discover my top picks.

Greg James has hit out at an Instagram troll for making a “deranged” comment about his wife Bella Mackie after the death of their dog Barney.

On Tuesday (4 August), the radio presenter, 40, shared the “horrible news” that he and Mackie’s beloved chocolate labrador was put down the previous night.

James missed that day’s breakfast radio show and returned to the airwaves on Wednesday (5 August), when he shared an emotional tribute to his ”very, very lovely dog”.

Later in the week, How To Kill Your Family author Mackie, who has been married to James since 2018, took to Instagram to share a picture of herself smiling as she received the first review for her new book Claw’s Out.

open image in gallery Mackie offered a blunt response to the comment, with James jumping in to support her

While Mackie, 43, hinted at Barney’s death in the post, calling it “some very welcome good news at a very sad time”, that didn’t stop one commenter from writing that it was “too soon before your pup died”.

While her commenters leapt to defend Mackie following the “s***ty comment”, the writer herself responded with a simple: “F*** you.”

James then left his own comment, writing: “Our grief and how we deal with it is absolutely nothing to do with you. Or more simply put, what Bella just said.”

Hours before, Mackie had shared a video of herself crying days on from Barney’s death, and along with a picture of the ring she’d had engraved with his face.

Reacting to the troll’s comment in a since-expired Instagram comment, she wrote: “Gave me an odd moment of dark comedy actually so thanks for your deranged message I guess?”

open image in gallery James with Barney, who became a regular character on his radio show ( Dr Noel Fitzpatrick/YouTube )

A regular character on James’s radio show and his and his wife’s social media feeds, Barney was adopted by the couple from Battersea Dogs and Cats Home in 2019, one year after James began hosting the Radio 1 breakfast show.

James shared the “horrible news” of his death on Instagram on Tuesday, writing: “I can’t really get my head around it. But he was peaceful, we were with him at home in the garden in the sunshine and I can’t stop crying.”

During his first radio show back the following day, James told listeners that he didn’t “really want to talk about it too much because I will cry”.

“Love that Barney boy so much, my God,” he said. “I guess it’s the whole thing, isn’t it? The price of love is pain, and my pain and my sadness is so much, because I loved him so god damn much. He was so joyful. What a thing.”

News.title: Suspected Ebola case on packed Congo river boat sparks testing rush
News.content:
Congolese health authorities have intercepted and detained a river boat on its way to the capital after a suspected Ebola case onboard.

Authorities have set up a mobile clinic to test more than 200 passengers after one of them disembarked and died earlier on the voyage.

The boat travelling from the northeastern commercial hub of Kisangani was stopped and held in Maluku, some 40 miles from Kinshasa.

Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is dealing with its worst ever outbreak of the viral haemorrhagic fever, which has seen nearly 4,000 cases and killed around 1,801 people according to the latest government figures.

Samuel Roger Kamba, the health minister, said a 32-year-old man had disembarked in Pimu in Mongala province, before developing ‌suspected Ebola symptoms and dying.

“We did not say it was Ebola. We said there was a suspected case for which we are being cautious,” the health minister told a press conference, according to MediaCongo, a local news site.

He said there had been no other reports of deaths among travellers.

The virus has so far spread to five provinces, though more than 90 per cent of cases have been recorded in the north eastern Ituri region.

News.title: El Nino could cause explosion of rabid seals, animal health experts warn
News.content:
This year’s El Nino weather event risks propelling an outbreak of rabid seals around the world, the world’s animal health body has warned.

Countries in South America and Australasia are being urged to look for signs the deadly infectious disease has reached their waters, only two years after it was first confirmed in South Africa.

The 2024 discovery of rabies in South Africa’s Cape fur seals was the first significant outbreak ever found in marine mammals and has been described as a “significant shift in rabies ecology”.

More than 100 cases have been confirmed in South Africa and Namibia since then, raising fears that aggressive rabid seals could infect humans, pets and other wildlife.

Changing patterns in fish stocks caused by the El Nino phenomenon now potentially risk widening the spread, as uninfected seal populations migrate for food and come into contact with rabid colleagues.

Scientists believe warming sea temperatures off Antarctica could send seal populations northwards into Southern African waters, where they could be exposed to rabies.

They could then return to their home waters, taking the virus with them and infecting other seal populations.

News.title: ​Arteta’s ‘dynasty’ dream collides with Arsenal’s harsh reality
News.content:
Arsenal 1 Real Betis 3

Mikel Arteta says he wants to create a “dynasty” at Arsenal as he threw down the gauntlet to his players to retain their Premier League title and reach a “different level”.

Arsenal are on the verge of completing a £75m deal for Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimãraes from Newcastle and have not given up hope of landing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who has been offered an improved contract by the Spanish giants.

The Premier League champions slumped to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night, when they paid the price for individual errors and a lethargic, sloppy defensive display.

But that did little to quell Arteta’s ambitions for the new season. “I’m even more excited [about this season], and we’re going to go and attack every possible title because that’s the ambition that we have,” he said.

“We know that we have the ability. We will go from a strength to a strength as well, whether it’s with the players that we have to take them to a different level, and with the market that is still open to recruit as well, so we are very optimistic about it.

“All the work that we’ve done – that I’ve done through the summer – is to understand what we need to do to win again and to create a dynasty in this football club. That’s the aim.”

Despite Arteta’s bullishness, he conceded Arsenal would have to be a lot better than they were against Betis. When asked about the mood in the dressing room, he said: “Very upset, given a hard time. They are fuming, but this is good. That’s what we need.”

Telegraph Sport analyses some of the talking points from a disappointing evening at the Aviva Stadium.

No Saliba a concern

The importance of goalkeeper David Raya and centre-backs William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães to Arsenal hardly needs overstating. Their title success was built on the foundations provided by that triumvirate at the back.

Raya has yet to report back from holiday after Spain’s World Cup triumph and Saliba is facing an extended spell on the sidelines with a back injury. Gabriel did appear for the second half but, watching this, Arteta is unlikely to have been dissuaded from the belief he needs another top defender to compensate for the loss of Saliba.

It may have been only Arsenal’s second game of pre-season, so a degree of legginess was understandable.

But the ease with which they were cut open and overloaded by the Spanish side, and the volume of individual errors, did not sit comfortably with Arteta with just over a fortnight until they kick off their title defence at home to newly promoted Coventry City.

Only once in 63 matches last season did Arsenal concede three goals in a single game but they were fortunate Betis did not score more. “In the first half there are two different things: to play well and to compete,” said Arteta, who saw his side trail 3-1 at the interval.

News.title: Ebola outbreak outpacing containment effort, WHO chief warns
News.content:
Caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, for which there are no vaccines or treatments, it has been extremely difficult to contain, according to experts on the ground.

“The outbreak is spreading faster than our scale-up of the response, with new cases doubling in some hotspots over the past week alone,” Dr Tedros said on X.

Part of the difficulty is that the virus was circulating undetected for weeks before the outbreak was formally declared in mid-May, leaving health officials even now racing to catch up with the spread.

Prof Placide Mbala, director of research, clinical trials and innovation at Africa CDC, told the Telegraph: “It’s mostly the fact we arrived a bit late. It took us some time before we detected this virus outbreak. And when we detected the outbreak, we already had a total of I can say more than 200 suspected cases. It’s been difficult to catch up. That’s where we are.”

While the DRC has a wealth of experience in tackling haemorrhagic fever outbreaks, the effects of that initial delay are still being felt.

Prof Mbala said: “We have some experience dealing with the cases, the labs, the communication, the infection prevention and control.

“We have some experience... But my observation is that we were very slow, and it’s why we’re in this situation.

“We are slow detecting the people, slow responding, we are slow deploying people, we are slow to recruit the community healthcare workers to improve contact tracing, we are slow to deploy the safe burials.”

DRC’s largest outbreak had previously been from 2018 to 2020, when 3,481 cases were recorded.

The West Africa outbreak recorded 28,616 cases and 11,310 deaths according to the WHO.

Prof Mbala said insecurity was also severely hampering attempts to curb the virus. The outbreak epicentre is in Ituri province, which has been wracked by ethnic strife for decades and is also home to militias competing to control mining.

He said: “There are many, many mining groups controlling most of the mining places. We have a big issue with those places, because they are places where the response team cannot go.”

Medics and aid workers have also been undermined by violent public distrust of their efforts.

Locals in the area have either doubted the existence of the virus, or have accused health teams of deliberately spreading the infection, or somehow benefiting from it.

More than a dozen health facilities have been set alight and several health workers have been killed.

Prof Mbala said: “The local people, they also sometimes are very upset, because they believe that it’s a kind of a business, and people who are coming here, they are getting a lot of money, [so] don’t want this disease to stop.”

He said he hoped that immunity was starting to rise in some areas and this would start to curb transmission.

However there was also a risk that people fleeing the outbreak would spread the virus further afield.

He said: “The second scenario is the fact we are seeing people moving from the affected area to new areas, to run away from the response team because they do not want to go to the treatment centre.

“And in complicity with their family members living in other areas, they are now the ones who are spreading the disease to new areas

“So we’ll see new places affected because people are moving around from the affected zone to the non-affected zone.”

News.title: Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat
News.content:
Chelsea 0 Juventus 1

Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

News.title: The underground lab where ‘princess mosquitoes’ are treated like royalty
News.content:
Beneath the grand Art Deco headquarters of the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine lies a vast labyrinth inhabited by weird and wonderful creatures.

In this maze of subterranean labs, store rooms and corridors live colonies of disease-bearing insects and arachnids from all over the world, from bed bugs, sand flies and microscopic dust mites to the so-called kissing bugs that spread Chagas disease – a sinister condition that can cause its victims to drop dead of heart failure without warning, albeit decades after the first (silent) infection.

Behind a series of doors, contained in stacks of mesh boxes, you can even find the flies that spread trachoma, the Dickensian eye disease that is still a leading cause of blindness around the world. But be warned: entering the room is not for the faint of heart – the flies feed on human excrement and the smell is impossible to forget.

There are also many varieties of mosquito, including several species of the Anopheles genus that spread malaria, Culex and Aedes mosquitoes that are also vectors for human and animal diseases, and even Toxorhynchites, perhaps better known as the elephant mosquito, a friendly giant which doesn’t bite people but preys on other mosquitoes.

These animals have been studied intensely since the insectaries were established in the building’s vaults in the 1960s, underpinning many breakthroughs in the control, surveillance, and understanding of vector-borne diseases in the developing world.

LSHTM researchers are now looking closer to home. They have established the UK’s first laboratory colony of Aedes vexans mosquitoes, a species native to the British isles, to study whether they could harbour diseases like West Nile virus, Rift Valley fever, Zika or Japanese encephalitis.

News.title: What I saw in a week on the front line of Afghanistan’s hunger crisis
News.content:
May 15 and 16, 2026

It is the weekend, a small moment to rest, although there is still a lot of work waiting for me. A week in the field does not mean that work in Kabul stops. I try to catch up on my emails and have a planned online interview for an international staff position – since in Europe, Friday is a normal working day. I also review parts of new proposals for donors and our financial planning.

On Saturday, however, I take a short break. Together with the base management team in Helmand, we visit a historical site called Qala-e-Bost, believed to have been built around 3,000 years ago. It is a rare moment to step away from work, followed by lunch with the team.

May 17, 2026

Sunday morning, the first working day of the week, we visit Basrhan Sub Health Centre, run by one of our local partners. As a nurse and former nurse trainer, I feel very much in my element in these health centres. It allows me to engage easily with the team and discuss their work.

I speak with the outreach officer and the vaccinator. They explain that this facility supports 18 outreach locations, each visited at least once a month. They provide vaccinations, raise awareness, and connect communities to the health centre. These visits often take place in simple settings, like mosques.

Immunisation is now well accepted. In the beginning, there was some resistance, but trust has grown over time. Every child is tracked, and if a child misses a vaccination, community health volunteers follow up at home. For extra polio vaccinations, this is carefully recorded by marking a finger of the child – helping ensure that no child is missed. The goal is clear: a polio-free Afghanistan.

I also speak with a mother. She is wearing a burka, so I cannot see her face. She tells me she is 22 years old and holds her 12-month-old son on her lap. She came because he has a fever, but I see a healthy child – something that stands out after my time in the TFU.

She brings her child regularly for follow-up and growth monitoring and the child has never been in a treatment program for malnutrition. She speaks positively about the services. “We are lucky,” she says. “The staff treat us well, and we have access to care in our community.”

Sports.title: Arsenal star Gabriel Martinelli ‘on Galatasaray’s transfer shortlist’ with Gunners future cast into doubt

Sports.title: Argentina back Gianni Infantino and close in on being handed World Cup 2030 perk in return
Sports.content:
ARGENTINA have given their backing to Fifa president Gianni Infantino amid rising pressure on his position.

Infantino is under massive scrutiny after his failed bid to sell off chunks of the World Cup.



The Swiss chief wanted to create a subsidiary called Fifa Forward Enterprise, which would have overseen football’s biggest tournament and allowed investors to claim a stake in it.

The proposals were widely condemned by a number of federations, including Uefa – who threatened a boycott of Fifa tournaments.



They were joined by Concacaf and the AFC, while the English FA and Welsh FA have revoked their support for Infantino.

The 56-year-old has had some support, including from Qatar and the Mexican FA, which broke rank with Concacaf to pledge allegiance to him.

And now the Argentinian FA have released a statement vowing to stick by Infantino in spite of calls for him to step down.

The federation – who are also hoping to host a full group phase at the 2030 World Cup – admitted Fifa were right to withdraw from their World Cup plan and praised Infantino after he apologised for the debacle.

But they insisted he he had their full backing going forwards.

Their statement read: “On behalf of the Argentine Football Association (AFA), and its Executive Committee, we address you, dear President, and through you to the FIFA board, to express our support for the management carried out during the last 10 years, which had as its main axes the development of football throughout the world and the institutional solidity based on a clear, stable and transparent governance model.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“In this regard, with respect to the recent events that are public knowledge, we must acknowledge the Administration’s decision to withdraw a project that, within the football family and from its inception, generated far more uncertainties than certainties.

“Therefore, it is worth highlighting the acknowledgment of the errors made in that process and the apology expressed in the heartfelt message sent to FIFA’s 211 member associations.

“You are leading a management that has brought about a profound transformation of FIFA; that has opened the doors of the organization to all member associations and confederations, so that through frank and direct dialogue, we can all continue to promote football at all levels and disciplines.”

The AFA went on to say they “believe that the way forward is to continue working under its leadership, in order to continue developing a better and even more inclusive football”.



It comes after Conmebol – which presides over South American football – said it would not back a vote to oust Infantinol.

The next World Cup will be co-hosted by Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay, alongside main hosts Spain, Portugal and Morocco.

The South American sides are currently due to host one game each, but AFA chief Chiqui Tapia wants Argentina to host an entire group phase – especially if the tournament expands to 64 teams.



He told Diario Ole: “If we start thinking that we are half an hour from Uruguay and an hour and a half from Paraguay and we can do a complete phase in our country.”

Decisions over the World Cup will take a back seat for now as Fifa grapples with the Infantino crisis after holding an emergency meeting in Rabat, Morocco.

Infantino has vowed to fight on after admitting mistakes were made after global outcry over the contentious proposals.

He is likely to face stiff opposition ahead of the Fifa presidential elections on March 18, 2027.

Uefa chief Alexander Ceferin is said to be a candidate, as well as PSG chief Nasser Al-Khelaifi, Arsene Wenger and Concacaf chief Victor Montagliani.

Sports.title: Arsenal ‘interested in Tottenham captain Cristian Romero’ in controversial transfer that echoes Sol Campbell’s exit
Sports.content:
ARSENAL are reportedly interested in Tottenham captain Cristian Romero – opening the door to a bombshell transfer across North London.

But Spurs are ready to slam it shut as they do not want to sell Romero to their bitter rivals.



Spurs are still bitter about their star centre-back Sol Campbell leaving them to join the Gunners 25 years on.

Romero treading the same path would be another sickener for Tottenham – even with the Argentine rubbing some fans up the wrong way last season.



The 28-year-old was sent off twice, publicly slammed the club’s board and had to be talked out of a trip to Argentina that would have seen him miss Spurs’ final-day survival showdown.

Tottenham are expected to sell Romero this summer but an overseas buyer is deemed more likely.



The Athletic claim that Inter Milan and Atletico Madrid are both actively pursuing the centre-half.

Inter even have a £34.2million agreement in principle over a transfer fee, but have not yet agreed personal terms with Romero.

Atletico, meanwhile, have a long-standing interest and are now pursuing him again.

Arsenal are ‘admirers’ of Romero, which Spurs are ‘unaware’ of, but a move between the two clubs is considered a ‘non-starter’.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

William Saliba is Mikel Arteta‘s first-choice centre-back alongside Gabriel, but the Frenchman is out for an extended period due to a back injury.

Romero would provide valuable experience but Cristhian Mosquera, Ben White, Piero Hincapie, Jurrien Timber and Riccardo Calafiori can all step into central defence to cover for Saliba.

Spurs paid £42.5m to sign Romero from Atalanta in 2021, with the defender scoring 13 times in 156 appearances.

He previously played for Belgrano and Genoa, and was on the books at Juventus for two years without making a senior appearance.

Arsenal have signed Illan Meslier and Christos Tzolis this summer, as well as making Hincapie’s loan from Bayer Leverkusen permanent.



Bruno Guimaraes will join the imminently after Arsenal and Newcastle agreed a £75m deal.

Sports.title: Premier League gets new Wag in actress Jordyn Jones who sparked romance with Chelsea ace Mykhailo Mudryk during drug ban
Sports.content:
THE PREMIER LEAGUE is welcoming a host of new stars this season, and not just on the pitch.

Chelsea‘s Mykhailo Mudryk has returned to the fold after a successful appeal against a doping ban, which had seen him sidelined since December 2024 after being hit with a four-year ban.



The Ukrainian international had been suspended after meldonium, a prohibited substance, was discovered in a sample provided while on international duty.

With his return the 25-year-old will act like a new signing for Xabi Alonso‘s squad, and was back on the pitch for the Blues in pre-season in a friendly against Juventus on Wednesday.



Despite being away for so long Mudryk has kept himself in shape, and good enough shape to be able to bench press his girlfriend.

Joining the Premier League as a Wag for the first time this season will be gorgeous actress, Jordyn Jones.

Jordyn, 26, initially outed the winger for sliding into her Instagram DMs, even temporarily blocking him after he invited her to a date at Disneyland Paris last September.

However, his persistence paid off and by March of this year Mudryk had won the blonde beauty over, as she posted to her page: “Fast forward six months. I’m glad I unblocked you.”

She has also posted pictures of herself wearing a Chelsea scarf and shirt, while in April a video showed Mudryk bench pressing Jordyn in gym.

With Mudryk tasting his first sweet minutes of football since returning from his suspension, Jordyn – and by extension her 8.7 million Instagram followers – will surely turn out to watch him in action at Stamford Bridge this season.

Sports.title: Man Utd files: Filming for Amazon documentary begins and why JJ Gabriel can’t wear new training kit
Sports.content:
JJ GABRIEL missed out on wearing the new training kit debuted by his team-mates this week.

United players were showing off the club’s new Betway-sponsored training kit since their £20m-per-year deal was announced on Monday.



But Gabriel, at 15 years old, is blocked from wearing betting sponsors on his kit, like every other Under-18 in the Premier League.

The league and clubs have rules that strictly prohibit Under 18s from wearing any kit or clothing—including training kit—that displays gambling or betting sponsor logos.



Gabriel was invited to the Topps Flagship Premier League launch day to pick up his rookie card on Thursday.

The teen was one of 20 Gold Cards announced, with Bruno Fernandes, Harry Kane, Alan Shearer, Declan Rice and Bruno Guimaraes on the same list.

Amazon Prime

It is understandably taking staff some getting used to going about their day jobs with camera lenses ever present.

Sports.title: England star Ivan Toney, 30, charged with assault after brawl outside trendy London nightclub
Sports.content:
IVAN Toney has been charged with assault following an alleged headbutt during a brawl outside a London club.

The England star, 30, who was part of the Three Lions squad during the World Cup, was arrested at a trendy bar in Soho.



Dramatic video revealed by The Sun showed the £40million star being frogmarched out of 100 Wardour St last December.

The striker – who started in England’s third-place play-off victory against France – will appear in court next month.



Toney was due to return to training with Saudi side Al-Ahli tomorrow ahead of the new season, according to reports.

The Met Police today confirmed the ex-Brentford star had been charged with assault causing actual bodily harm.

Issuing a statement, the force said: “A man has been charged with assault following a Met investigation.

“Ivan Toney, 30, of Northampton, was charged on Thursday, 31 July with assault causing actual bodily harm.



“He will appear at Westminster Magistrates’ Court on Thursday, 24 September.

“The charge relates to an assault, which reportedly took place on 6 December 2025 at a nightclub on Wardour Street, W1.”

Witnesses in the club described trouble erupting after a fan grabbed Toney for a selfie.

One reveller, who had been out for a drink with his girlfriend, told The Sun: “He walked past a table of a group of lads.

“One of them recognised him and said, ‘Oh, it’s Ivan Toney’ and tried to put his hands around his neck to get a photo with him.



“And then Toney has said, ‘Get off me, get off me’.”

Officers arrived at the club within half an hour and quickly led the Three Lions forward out the venue.

The onlooker said Toney may have felt threatened by the fan before chaos erupted.

He added: “He’s a superstar — he gets half a million a week in Saudi Arabia.

“He had his jewellery on and he had a real nice watch.



“He might have thought they were trying to attack him to take his chain or watch off him.”

It comes just days after Toney shared snaps from a luxury holiday on Instagram with the caption “down time but we stay up”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

London Ambulance Service confirmed it sent an ambulance and a paramedic at 1.57am to reports of an alleged assault .

A spokesman added: “We assessed three people. We took one patient to a local hospital and discharged the other patients at the scene.”

Sports.title: Inside Bruno Guimaraes' dream Arsenal transfer six years in making for Mikel Arteta
Sports.content:
Bruno Guimaraes endured sleepless nights as he waited patiently by the phone in Curitiba six-and-a-half years ago. After bossing the Athletico Paranaense midfield, he had his heart set on a life-changing transfer to Atletico Madrid.

A £26million agreement was in the works, so much so that Guimaraes fought back the tears as he waved goodbye to the Furacão faithful following a 1-0 home victory over Santos. Christmas slowly passed, the January window formally opened and still the future felt a tad uncertain.

Atletico were dithering, Benfica had tabled an offer and club president Mario Celso Petraglia confirmed there was a new suitor at the table: it was Arsenal.

Gunners technical director Edu had been monitoring Guimaraes' explosive development and his contribution towards four trophies including the Copa do Brasil and Copa Sudamericana.

‌



There was a direct approach to his agents but finances were limited and Lyon muscled in, courtesy of Brazilian icon Juninho Pernambucano.

Tottenham respond as Arsenal consider shock transfer for Spurs skipper Cristian Romero READ MORE :

He presented the hungry 22-year-old with a promise: 'Sign for Lyon and you can become one of the best midfielders in world football'.

Juninho had won titles with Vasco Da Gama prior to joining Lyon and was one of Guimaraes' heroes, therefore his guidance carried significant weight.

Arsenal's new £75million addition is an avid Vasco supporter and actually attended one of their matches, a 1-1 draw with Mirassol, as recently as July 26.

‌



A £17.1m deal soon followed and speaking upon signing a long-term contract in France, the Brazil U23 starlet did not hesitate to take aim at Atletico, stating: "Nobody called me."

View 4 Images Bruno Guimaraes is presented to Lyon fans after signing for the club in January 2020

The Spaniards, having initially led the charge, soon lived to regret abandoning their pursuit of the player.

Two years later, it was somewhat fitting that Guimaraes' Newcastle medical would take place in his homeland while he was away on international duty, underlining his growth in stature.

‌



Again, Arsenal had been sniffing around but incredibly, were not able to compete with the Magpies' financial muscle on the back of signing two midfielders, Martin Odegaard and Albert Sambi Lokonga, the previous summer.

A few months later, they paid a heavy price. Guimaraes netted and starred in Newcastle's 2-0 victory over Arsenal, who lost their grip on Champions League qualification with just one match to spare.

View 4 Images Bruno Guimaraes scored in a 2-0 win for Newcastle over Arsenal in May 2022

Since then, he has persistently taken the fight to the Gunners and got under their skin. In fact, he has won more duels against his new employers (71) than he has against any other Premier League side.

‌



For the entirety of his career, Guimaraes has only ever gone where he's felt wanted. It stems from a series of rejections as a child in Rio de Janeiro.

He loved futsal but failed to make the grade at Fluminense and Botafogo. Father Dick, still heavily involved in his representation, would make the 269-mile drive to Osasco every weekend to watch a fresh-faced Guimaraes play for Audax in Sao Paulo.

It was a sacrifice he was willing to make but there was tough love along the way. If his son had lost, Dick would hand him a ham and cheese sandwich with juice.

If Guimaraes won, he'd be treated to whatever food he craved. He still carries those fond memories with him today, emblazoned across his back.

‌



View 4 Images Bruno Guimaraes with his father Dick Gomez

The No.39, which he is poised to wear for Arsenal, was also the number of his cab-driving dad's Rio taxi - the same vehicle he drove to Guimaraes' youth matches in.

Gunners academy starlet Louie Copley, who suffered a serious knee injury in midweek against Real Betis, has been wearing that number in training and matches in recent weeks.

On the club's website, he's now listed as Arsenal's No.38 - paving the way for a certain Brazilian to own the shirt that means so much to him.

‌



After fluffing the chance to land the all-action maestro on two separate occasions, Mikel Arteta was never going to pass up the opportunity to finally sign his long-standing target.

Negotiations rumbled on, the saga became slightly tedious but there was only ever truly one outcome. Third time's the charm and Guimaraes is a Gunner.

Sports.title: England star Ivan Toney charged with assault at London nightclub
Sports.content:
England star Ivan Toney charged with assault at London nightclub

Ivan Toney, who represented England at this summer's World Cup, has been charged with assault following a police investigation into an incident at a Soho nightclub last year

View Image Ivan Toney has been charged with assault (Image: Javier Garcia/Shutterstock)

Ivan Toney has been charged with assault causing actual bodily harm following an incident at a Soho nightclub in December last year.

The England striker, 30, was charged on July 31 relating to the alleged assault on December 2025 on Wardour Street, London. He is due to appear in court on September 24.

A statement from the Met Police said: "A man has been charged with assault following a Met investigation.

"Ivan Toney, 30 (16.03.1996), of Northampton, was charged on Thursday, 31 July with assault causing actual bodily harm.

"He will appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Thursday, 24 September.

"The charge relates to an assault, which reportedly took place on 6 December 2025 at a nightclub on Wardour Street, W1."

Tottenham respond as Arsenal consider shock transfer for Spurs skipper Cristian Romero READ MORE :

A spokesperson for Toney said: "Ivan acknowledges the charge and although he is naturally shocked, he looks forward to being given the opportunity to clear his name in court."

Toney was part of England's squad at the recent World Cup in the USA, Canada and Mexico. He helped the Three Lions to a third-placed finish, their best performance since 1966.

His selection came as something of a surprise to many and attracted widespread criticism due to Toney playing his football in Saudi Arabia, despite plundering 42 goals last term.

Toney didn't feature until the semi-final defeat by Argentina, where he came on as a late substitute. But he started the third-place playoff win against France, playing 78 minutes.

Toney began his career with hometown club Northampton before signing for Newcastle in 2015. From there, he went out on loan to Barnsley, Shrewsbury, Scunthorpe and Wigan.

It was at Peterborough where his goal-scoring form first caught the eye, leading to a move to Brentford in 2020.

He scored 72 goals in 141 appearance for the Bees before his money-spinning Saudi switch, including 36 in the Premier League, leading to a first England call-up in 2022 and a debut in March 2023.

In all, Toney has played 10 times for his country, scoring once in a friendly against Belgium at Wembley in March 2024.

Sports.content:
Aston Villa stars 'think they know what's happening next' with Arsenal target Ezri Konsa

Arsenal are targeting Aston Villa defender Ezri Konsa in a £60m deal - and his team-mates think they know where he'll end up before the transfer window closes

View 2 Images Arsenal are reportedly keen on signing Aston Villa defender Ezri Konsa this summer. (Image: (Photo by Sarah Stier - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images))

Aston Villa stars are reportedly 'resigned to losing' Ezri Konsa this summer, with Arsenal interested in signing the England international. The Gunners are looking to bounce back from a disappointing setback in their pursuit of Real Madrid star Vinicius Junior.

‌



It's claimed the Gunners are eyeing the Villa star, as they look to bolster their backline following an injury to William Saliba and concerns over Jurrien Timber and Ben White. The Mail says both Arsenal and Liverpool are keen on securing the England international, with his Aston Villa colleagues worried that Konsa will depart the club.

‌



However, the Gunners will need to raise their offer, having already seen a bid much lower than Villa's £60m valuation swiftly rejected earlier this summer. It was claimed earlier this week that the Premier League champions will go back in with an improved offer before the window closes on September 1.

‌



Konsa has been among the main transfer targets for Mikel Arteta's side this summer, behind Bruno Guimaraes and Vinicius Junior, but Arsenal are reluctant to overspend. While Arteta will now look to find an alternative attacking option to Vinicius, signing Konsa would be a huge coup and soften the blow of missing out on the Brazilian.

Vinicius Jr to Arsenal transfer saga reaches conclusion as Real Madrid star strikes agreement READ MORE :

However, Villa have already seen several key players exit this summer, with Morgan Rogers departing for Chelsea and Youri Tielemans joining Manchester United, meaning they are under no financial pressure to cash in.

‌



Defender Lucas Digne is also expected to complete a move to PSG, but there is still said to be some anxiety within the Villa Park dressing room about Konsa's future, with the defender having just two years remaining on his contract.

Guimaraes is on the brink of switching to the Emirates Stadium for a reported £75m transfer from Newcastle United.

View 2 Images Vinicius Junior has made his decision (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

Yet, the Gunners suffered a setback earlier this week, with Vinicius poised to pen a new contract with Real Madrid.

Arsenal had been ready to table a blockbuster contract for the Brazilian winger in a bid to tempt him to the Premier League champions this summer, with the 26-year-old locked in a stalemate with Los Blancos over fresh terms.

Sports.title: Tottenham respond as Arsenal consider shock transfer for Spurs skipper Cristian Romero
Sports.content:
Tottenham respond as Arsenal consider shock transfer for Spurs skipper Cristian Romero

Tottenham are open to selling Cristian Romero before the summer transfer window closes and Arsenal have emerged as surprise suitors amid their search for defensive reinforcements

View 2 Images Cristian Romero's future at Tottenham is uncertain (Image: Robin Jones/Getty Images)

Tottenham will refuse to sell Cristian Romero to Arsenal, who are interested in signing the Spurs captain. Romero, 28, is a shock target for the Gunners, who want to sign a centre-back before the transfer window shuts on September 1.

‌



Atletico Madrid and Inter Milan are also interested, with the latter striking a €40million (£34.2m) deal in principle with Tottenham. Romero, however, is yet to agree personal terms with Inter like he reportedly has with Atletico, who are preparing a bid of their own.

‌



According to The Athletic, Spurs were unaware of Arsenal's interest but would consider any transfer between the North London rivals a non-starter. William Gallas is the last player to move directly between the two clubs, joining Spurs in 2010 after his deal with Arsenal had expired.

‌



Sol Campbell controversially went the other way in 2001, having run down his contract at Tottenham. The transfer remains infamous to this day.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Vinicius Jr to Arsenal transfer saga reaches conclusion as Real Madrid star strikes agreement READ MORE :

Liverpool weigh up hijacking £60m Arsenal transfer to appease desperate Andoni Iraola READ MORE :

Arsenal's search for defensive reinforcements comes after William Saliba succumbed to a back injury at the World Cup. Although Mikel Arteta already has Cristian Mosquera, Ben White and Jurrien Timber as cover, he would like another right-footed centre-back.

‌



Romero was named captain by Spurs last summer following the departure of club legend Son Heung-min. Atletico were eyeing up a move back then and have renewed their interest in recent weeks.

Tottenham have already signed two centre-backs this summer, welcoming ex-Bournemouth star Marcos Senesi on a free before paying £52million for Brighton's Jan Paul van Hecke. Spurs are also close to tying Micky van de Ven down to a new contract which would extneded his stay until 2031.

Who should Arsenal sign before the window closes? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Cristian Romero hasn't returned for pre-season training after the World Cup (Image: Richard Sellers/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images)

Roberto De Zerbi has spoken to Romero since he helped Argentina reach the World Cup final, but the Tottenham boss was coy when asked about the defender's future. "I texted with Cuti yesterday to make a plan for when he comes back to London," De Zerbi said earlier this week.

"(I do not know about) the transfer market. That's not my job. I know there are many solutions in the transfer market."

‌



Meanwhile, Inter sporting director Piero Ausilio recently declared his club's interest in signing the 28-year-old. "It's definitely a deal we are trying to sign with the player and the club," Ausilio revealed to Sky Italia. "These things take some time but there’s definitely interest. Let's see."

Tottenham's next pre-season friendly takes place on Saturday against Spanish side Getafe, although Romero won't be involved as he continues his break after the World Cup. The game will be played at Hotspur Way, Spurs' training ground.

Sports.title: Rodri's agent drops transfer bombshell as Man City star decides future
Sports.content:
Rodri's agent drops transfer bombshell as Man City star decides future

Real Madrid were long considered the favourites to sign Rodri before Barcelona entered the running, with the midfielder having entered the final 12 months of his contract at Manchester City

View 2 Images Rodri has decided his next club (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Rodri's agent has announced that the Manchester City star wants to join Barcelona over arch rivals Real Madrid. Rodri, 30, agreed personal terms with Barca on Thursday in a sudden and dramatic twist.

‌



The Spaniard had been in talks with Real for weeks after suggesting back in March that he was keen on a move to the Bernabeu. But Barcelona have hijacked the move after Rodri spoke to their manager, Hansi Flick, and sporting director Deco and was convinced to join the La Liga champions.

‌



Although City haven't given up hope of tying Rodri down to a new contract after he entered the final year of his current deal, Etihad chiefs are well aware of his desire to return to Spain. In a late-night interview with Cadena SER, Rodri's agent, Pablo Barquero, revealed all.

‌



"Out of respect for Madrid, as they have been class, Rodri informed them that his decision is to join Barca," Barquero told the Spanish radio station.

FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

Ex-Man City captain gives health update after being diagnosed with devastating rare condition READ MORE :

Barcelona are in the market for a midfielder after Frenkie de Jong was ruled out for several months. Rodri is seen as a plug and play option, having gotten over his injury troubles and helped Spain win the World Cup last month.

‌



The 30-year-old also picked up the Golden Ball at the tournament, playing an integral role for Luis de la Fuente's side. His departure from City would follow that of manager Pep Guardiola, defender John Stones and midfielder Bernardo Silva in a summer of change at the Etihad.

New boss Enzo Maresca remains desperate to keep him, though, and stated earlier this week: "It's very important (to have him). Any manager in the world wants Rodri because he's a top player; so it's important for me, the club and for everyone."

Should Manchester City sell Rodri? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Rodri was named Player of the Tournament at the World Cup (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

But Maresca's hopes could soon be dashed. Barcelona have room in their wage budget following the departure of Robert Lewandowski and appear to have enough funds to tempt City to the negotiating table, having bid around £100m for Atletico Madrid forward Julian Alvarez in June.

Rodri has spent seven years with City, winning four Premier League titles, one Champions League and two FA Cups. The former ex-Villarreal man received the Ballon d'Or in 2024, having won that year's European Championship with Spain.

Sports.title: Argentina at odds with England as statement released on FIFA president Gianni Infantino
Sports.content:
Argentina at odds with England as statement released on FIFA president Gianni Infantino

FIFA president Gianni Infantino has split world football this summer, with football associations sharing statements about his premiership, with Argentina and England again at odds

Gianni Infantino retains FIFA board’s support after crisis meeting

The Argentine Football Association have shared a statement in support of FIFA president Gianni Infantino's premiership over the last decade. That stance is at odds with the Football Association, who are withdrawing support for his re-election to a fourth term, much like the Football Association of Wales (FAW).

‌



The Football Associations of Finland, Serbia and Sweden have also done likewise ahead of the 77th FIFA Congress in mid-March. That is when the next presidential election will take place in Morocco.

‌



Denmark and Norway also oppose his re-election. Argentina, however, have now joined Egypt and several others in publicly supporting Infantino.

‌



View 2 Images Lionel Messi's Argentina have backed FIFA president Gianni Infantino (Image: Getty Images)

The AFA statement, translated into English from Spanish, reads: "Of our highest consideration, on behalf of the Argentine Football Association (AFA), and its Executive Committee, we address you, dear President, and through your worthy intermediary the FIFA board, to express our support for the management carried out during the last 10 years, which had as its main axes the development of football throughout the world and institutional solidity based on a clear governance model. stable and transparent.

"In this sense, in relation to the recent events that are public knowledge, we must recognise the decision of the Administration to withdraw a project that generated, within the football family and from its inception, many more uncertainties than certainties.

‌



"That is why it is worth highlighting the acceptance of the errors made in this process and the apology expressed in the heartfelt message displayed to the 211 member associations of FIFA. Prioritising governance standards is a fundamental pillar for strengthening good relations between FIFA, its member associations and the confederations.

View 2 Images The Confederation of African Football have backed Gianni Infantino, too (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

"In the same way, and as we have already expressed, you are leading a management that led to a profound transformation of FIFA, which opened the doors of the organisation to all member associations and confederations, so that with a frank and direct dialogue, we can, together, continue to promote football at all levels and disciplines.

‌



"From our point of view, this transformation was based on a model of transparent governance, respect for statutory structures and the monitoring of democratic procedures, essential principles for the football family to be united, firm and working to continue generating improvements in sports and institutions, which have an impact on a better quality of life for millions of human beings who practice our beloved sport.

"Accordingly, with the upcoming FIFA Congress approaching, the Association that I proudly preside over firmly believes and reaffirms that the way forward is to continue to work under your leadership, so that we can continue to develop better and even more inclusive football."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



The FA's last public statement was made last weekend regarding the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal being withdrawn by Infantino. They also acknowledged a statement from UEFA welcoming the move.

An FA spokesperson said: "We fully support UEFA's position. It is time for a full and robust review of FIFA's leadership and governance to ensure that the global game is run transparently, for the benefit of all 211 member nations and with the long-term stewardship of football at its heart."

Sports.title: Massey-Ellis retires from officiating to take up new role with FA
Sports.content:
Assistant referee Sian Massey-Ellis has retired from officiating and will take up a new role with the Football Association.

Massey-Ellis will become the FA's Senior Manager - Women Referees from September, where she will support and develop female officials across the country and help provide a pathway into the elite game.

The 40-year-old became only the second female assistant referee to officiate in the Premier League when she made her top-flight debut in 2010 and has since worked on more than 150 Premier League matches.

Her career also included five Women's FA Cup finals, while she became the first female assistant referee appointed to the Community Shield. In 2021, Massey-Ellis became the first woman involved in a men's FA Cup final when she served as an assistant VAR, before also working as an AVAR at the 2025 Carabao Cup final.

On the international stage, Massey-Ellis officiated at four Women's European Championships and two Women's World Cups, as well as the 2018 Women's Champions League final. In 2019, she became the first English woman to officiate a men's European fixture when she worked as an assistant referee in the Europa League.

To the young girl who simply loved refereeing, we did it. Thank you, football.

Massey-Ellis, who received an MBE for services to football, said: "Although I am stepping away from the touchline, I am not stepping away from football.

"If my journey has helped change perceptions, open doors or inspire even one young person to believe they belong in the game, then I will consider that one of my greatest achievements.

"As I prepare for one final walk onto the pitch, I leave with nothing but gratitude. It has been the greatest honour to serve the game I love and represent English officiating."

Chief Refereeing Officer Howard Webb described Massey-Ellis as a "powerhouse" whose impact on female officiating "will be felt for years to come".

"Sian has done us proud time and time again - domestically and on the international stage, breaking multiple barriers and setting the standard for those coming through in her footsteps," Webb added.

Gibbs' agents Athletes First announced the deal Thursday, hours after he took the field for the first time since the Lions' training camp started. His agents also noted the new contract includes $51.5m (£38.3m) guaranteed for the Pro Bowler.

Two days earlier, Atlanta briefly made Bijan Robinson the NFL's highest-paid running back in history.

Gibbs had been participating in meetings at camp, but Thursday was his first appearance on the field, an indication the Lions and his agents were close to a deal. Gibbs held his right arm high and gave a thumbs-up when asked if an agreement was close as he walked off the practice field.

Gibbs changed his jersey number from 26 to 0 ahead of the 2025 season and rushed for 1,223 yards and 13 touchdowns, and had 77 receptions for 616 yards and five scores.

Sports.title: England striker Toney charged with assault
Sports.content:
Ivan Toney, who represented England at this summer's World Cup has been charged with assault causing actual bodily harm following a nightclub incident in December 2025; he will appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Thursday September 24

England striker Ivan Toney has been charged with assault causing actual bodily harm, following a nightclub incident in December 2025.

Toney, who featured at the World Cup and plays his club football for Al Ahli in Saudi Arabia, will appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Thursday September 24.

England are due to play World Cup winners Spain two days later in a Nations League game at Wembley.

A spokesperson for Toney said: "Ivan acknowledges the charge and although he is naturally shocked, he looks forward to being given the opportunity to clear his name in court."

The charge relates to an assault which reportedly took place on Wardour Street in London.

Toney was a surprise selection in Thomas Tuchel's England squad this summer and went on to make appearances in the semi-final against Argentina as a late substitute and then started the third-place play-off win over France.

Toney, aged 30, joined Al Ahli in August 2024 from Brentford for a transfer fee of £40m. He scored 72 goals in 141 games for Brentford, including 36 in their three seasons in the Premier League.

Toney missed the first half of the 2023/24 season due to a gambling ban but went on to feature in England's run to the Euro 2024 final. The Saudi Pro League season begins on August 13.

Sports.title: Hearts humbled by Benfica as Hibs secure vital win; Motherwell held in Helsinki
Sports.content:
Hearts endured a predictably bruising evening in Lisbon as their hopes of progressing to the Europa League were all but ended by a 6-1 thrashing at the hands of Benfica.

After a largely demoralising summer, which began with being pipped to the William Hill Premiership title by Celtic in May, 1,300 embattled Jambos travelled to the Portuguese capital for one of the most formidable fixtures in the club's recent history, braced for a fourth consecutive defeat under new head coach Wouter Vrancken.

And that was exactly what transpired as Marco Silva's Benfica opened the scoring in the third minute, led by three at the break and then added another three in the second half to remove all sense of jeopardy from next Thursday's second leg at Tynecastle.

While the Portuguese giants are on course to face the losers of the Champions League tie between Aarhus and Sabah Baku in the Europa League play-off round, Hearts are staring at a likely Conference League play-off against Rapid Vienna, who lead Paide 4-1 after the first leg in Estonia.

Hibernian will take a valuable lead to North Macedonia for the second leg of their Conference League third qualifying round clash after overcoming Shkendija 2-1.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hibernian head coach David Gray says his side will get even better as they beat Shkendija in the first leg of their Conference League third-round qualifier.

Hibs had gone in front in the 73rd minute through Owen Elding, only for the visitors to level less than three minutes later courtesy of Marko Gjorgjievski.

However, Warren O'Hora notched a 90th-minute winner when he bundled in a Jordan Obita corner to leave Hibs in a good position to reach the competition's play-off round when they make the trip to Skopje for the second leg.

Image: Warren O'Hora (L) celebrates after scoring to make it 2-1 to Hibs at Easter Road

Motherwell's impressive start under Alfred Johansson continued as they secured a 1-1 draw away to HJK Helsinki in the first leg of their Conference League third qualifying round tie.

The Lanarkshire side's new Swedish boss briefly looked on course for his fourth consecutive victory at the helm after Tawanda Maswanhise's penalty gave the Steelmen the lead just after the hour mark.

Image: Tawanda Maswanhise put Motherwell ahead in Helsinki

However, 36-year-old former Celtic and Norwich City striker Teemu Pukki equalised for Finnish side HJK within seconds of coming off the bench.

Motherwell, who lost Alex Lowry and Regan Charles-Cook to injuries in the closing stages, will return home believing they have a good chance of setting up a glamour play-off showdown with Europa League runners-up Freiburg later this month.

Sports.content:
Super League: Harvey Barron scores treble as Hull FC end losing run with win over St Helens

Winger Harvey Barron scored a first senior hat-trick as Hull FC ended a seven-game losing run with a 32-18 comeback win at St Helens.

Barron's treble boosted the Black and Whites' hopes of avoiding the Super League wooden spoon while casting further doubt on Saints making the end of season play-offs.

Hull had not previously won at the BrewDog Stadium in 10 games and nine years and sat just two points off bottom club Huddersfield Giants.

However, in this battle of the interim coaches, Andy Last got the better of counterpart Eamon O'Carroll, who last weekend oversaw Saints' first defeat at York in more than 80 years.

Hull trailed 14-10 approaching half-time but Barron struck almost on the hooter and completed his career landmark hat-trick after 47 minutes before substitute Cade Cust crashed over three minutes later.

Those 16 points in 11 minutes stunned Saints, still reeling from last month's exit of Paul Rowley after less than a year as head coach.

Despite a first away victory on Saints' territory since August 2017, Hull stay 13th although they are now level on points with Bradford Bulls.

St Helens have never failed to reach the play-offs but they remain seventh with all teams above them to play in the coming days.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hull FC interim head coach Andy Last said it felt fantastic for his side to end their losing streak Hull FC interim head coach Andy Last said it felt fantastic for his side to end their losing streak

They led three times in the opening 40 minutes but conceded their advantage each time and were fortunate to be level at 14-14.

The game's first mistake after barely two minutes saw full-back Logan Moy's knock-on punished by winger Lewis Murphy, who finished in the corner.

FC were behind only five minutes as Zak Hardaker's pass sent in Barron for the first of his treble.

Hastings edged Saints in front again with an 18th-minute penalty for Tom Briscoe's high tackle.

Prop Herman Ese'ese had a second Hull try ruled out for a double movement while he and Barron were repelled in quick succession before the visitors' deservedly hit the front.

Stand-off Jake Arthur's double cut-out pass freed Lewis Martin to finish in the left corner to make it 10-8.

Barron was denied again by last-gasp cover tackling and it was against the run of play when Jack Welsby raced 30 metres to touch down.

With 37 seconds remaining Saints captain Hastings dropped out. Thirty four seconds later Barron seized on Aidan Sezer's angled kick to cross again, waiting anxiously before video referee Chris Kendall overturned Liam Rush's on-field decision of 'no try'.

Tries for Barron and Cust, both converted by Hardaker, virtually put the contest out of reach.

By the time Harry Robertson scored a consolation try, Hardaker's 70th-minute penalty sealed the deal for Hull FC, who finished off with a further try from ex-Saint James Bell.

Jenna Foubister of Wigan celebrates their victory over St Helens

In the Women's Super League, Wigan Warriors saw off rivals St Helens 44-6 in the first match of the new Super Four format.

The defending champions outclassed St Helens with Ellise Derbyshire and Eva Hunter scoring a brace with further scores from Anna Davies, Molly Jones, Remi Wilton, Jenna Foubister and Mary Coleman at the BrewDog Stadium.
