Sports.title: Norway’s Klaveness tells Fifa president Infantino to resign: ‘There is no trust now’
Sports.content:
The Norwegian FA will ask Gianni Infantino to resign with immediate effect after his doomed attempt to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors. Norway is the first federation to call directly for the Fifa president to step down after a series of controversies that came to a head with the current crisis surrounding his Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme.

The decision was made in a meeting of the Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) on Thursday night. Norway has consistently taken a lead in efforts to scrutinise Fifa’s governance and recent events have taken any faith in its leadership beyond the point of no return.

“We decided that there is no trust in Infantino now,” the NFF president, Lise Klaveness, told the Guardian. “We have been worried consistently and there has been one more step in worrying direction every year, every part of the year. The trust is now gone for us, there is no way back for Infantino.

“We’re left in a very polarised cooperation globally and, I would say, chaos. So we will ask him to resign immediately so that the global football community can look ahead and cooperate going into the future.”

The NFF is expected to formally write a letter requesting Infantino’s resignation in the coming week. Norway was among a handful of countries not to back his re-election as president next March, although several European federations have withdrawn their endorsement in the past week.

“We understand that we’re one country, but it’s our position,” Klaveness said. “It’s just one step further for us. We did not vote for him in 2023 but we hoped we would support him, he was elected and the reason why we were so clear in our statements was to really give the signal that we wanted him to implement the good reforms he was part of. But he didn’t, and now we will ask him to resign.”

Norway will also formalise a fresh complaint to Fifa’s ethics committee on three fronts, taking in the FFE scandal, the award of Fifa’s “peace prize” to Donald Trump and the Folarin Balogun affair of the recent World Cup. It will attempt to bring a number of major federations onboard for its submission.

Sports.title: England striker Ivan Toney charged with assault after Soho nightclub incident
Sports.content:
The England striker Ivan Toney has been charged with assault after an incident at a nightclub in Soho.

The Metropolitan police said Toney, 30, of Northampton, was charged on 31 July with assault causing actual bodily harm.

The force said the charge relates to an alleged assault that reportedly took place on 6 December last year at a nightclub on Wardour Street in central London.

Toney, a striker for Saudi Pro League club Al-Ahli, will appear at Westminster magistrates court on 24 September.

The Sun newspaper reported on 8 December that Toney had been arrested after an alleged head-butt.

A spokesperson for Toney said: “Ivan acknowledges the charge and although he is naturally shocked, he looks forward to being given the opportunity to clear his name in court.”

Sports.title: Mexico and Argentina line up behind Infantino to deepen football’s civil war
Sports.content:
The Mexican football federations have broken ranks with the rest of Concacaf by issuing their public backing for beleaguered Fifa president Gianni Infantino in a move that has deepened world football’s civil war.

Concacaf has called for a thorough review of Fifa’s governance in the light of the World Cup sell-off debacle, and is backing Uefa’s demands for meaningful change, although has yet to follow their European counterparts by threatening to boycott tournaments if they do not achieve their objectives.

A statement issued on Thursday night by the Mexico federation (FMF) went some way towards explaining Concacaf’s reticence, as their second biggest member after the United States was unequivocal in their support for Infantino.

In a Fifa statement released under Infantino’s name on Wednesday, the world governing body had called for its institutional practices to be respected, a coded way of condemning any leadership challenge before next March’s scheduled presidential election, which the FMF endorsed.

“The Mexican Football Federation is convinced that football is its fundamental value and that its best defence lies in institutional integrity and respect for the governance and processes that safeguard it,” the FMF said.

“Therefore, the FMF will not recognise or approve any process convened outside of this institutional framework, and it embraces the call issued by President Infantino on August 5, 2026, to collectively continue developing football for the benefit of its 211 member associations. The FMF supports President Infantino’s leadership in continuing to promote the development of football through institutional strengthening.”

The Argentina Football Association (AFA) followed Mexico’s lead by backing Infantino in a gushing tribute and expressing support for his leadership over the past decade.

Unlike Concacaf, South America’s Conmebol appears united behind Infantino, while in an intriguing subplot there is growing speculation that Mexico would like to switch confederations to join the latter.

“In relation to the recent events that are public knowledge, we must recognise the decision of the administration to withdraw a project that generated, within the football family and from its inception, many more uncertainties than certainties,” the AFA statement read.

“That is why it is worth highlighting the acceptance of the errors made in this process and the apology expressed in the heartfelt message displayed to the 211 member associations of Fifa. Prioritising governance standards is a fundamental pillar for strengthening good relations between Fifa, its member associations and the confederations.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“In the same way, and as we have already expressed, you are leading a management that led to a profound transformation of Fifa, which opened the doors of the organisation to all member associations and confederations, so that with a frank and direct dialogue, we can, together, continue to promote football at all levels and disciplines.

“From our point of view, this transformation was based on a model of transparent governance, respect for statutory structures and the monitoring of democratic procedures, essential principles for the football family to be united, firm and working to continue generating improvements in sports and institutions, which have an impact on a better quality of life for millions of human beings who practice our beloved sport.

“Accordingly, with the upcoming Fifa Congress approaching, the association that we proudly preside over firmly believes and reaffirms that the way forward is to continue to work under your leadership, so that we can continue to develop better and even more inclusive football.”

Earlier on Thursday the Confederation of African Football had reaffirmed its support for Infantino, providing him with further allies as he fights to extend his 10-year reign.

Sports.title: Afcon’s biennial switch cost African governing body deal worth more than $1bn
Sports.content:
A deal worth at least $1bn in secured income over eight years was abandoned by the Confederation of African Football (Caf) because the governing body decided to switch the Africa Cup of Nations from a biennial to a four-yearly event, the Guardian can reveal.

On 5 July 2025, the eve of the delayed Women’s Africa Cup of Nations in Morocco, the Caf president, Patrice Motsepe, told the Guardian in Rabat, after a prolonged discussion of the bidding process at an executive committee meeting, that a decision on a winning bid would be made “in due course”.

“We announced in Addis Ababa this $1bn partnership that we are looking at over the next eight years. There is a lot of good progress that has been made,” he said.

On 23 July, four days after the World Cup final in New York, Caf opened a fresh tender for the marketing and commercial rights of the 2028, 2032 and 2036 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) tournaments, with bidders given until 24 August to hand in their bid books.

The tender is in complete contrast to the 2025 bidding round, in which the entirety of Caf’s competition portfolio was bundled for sale.

Luxolo September, Caf’s head of communications, confirmed that the change in Afcon frequency is wholly responsible for the abandonment of the 2025 bidding round that was on the verge of completion.

“As foreshadowed by the president in his comments last year, following the receipt and evaluation of bids and presentations from the bidders, in the second half of 2025, Caf entered into detailed discussions with shortlisted bidders regarding the precise terms and conditions of their proposals.

“However, at its meeting on 20 December 2025, the Caf executive committee took a unanimous decision – in the interest of African football – to move the Afcon to a four-year cycle, bringing the competition into alignment with the international match calendar,” September said. “This was a significant decision for African football. That executive committee decision materially changed the scope of the commercial rights available for tender, with the result that the 2025 ITT (Invitation To Tender) process could no longer proceed in its existing form.”

View image in fullscreen Patrice Motsepe (left) said in 2025 that ‘good progress’ was being made over a $1bn deal for Caf. Photograph: Angela Weiss/AFP/Getty Images

It has been seven years since Caf has had a long-term deal to secure its financial future. The 2016-2028 billion-dollar “minimum guarantee” revenue contract that it signed with the French company Lagardère during the tenure of Issa Hayatou, the late Cameroonian president of Caf, was the first of its kind for the organisation.

“The Memorandum of Understanding with Lagardère was agreed by a team I led with Hicham [El Amrani, then Caf general secretary] in May 2015, in Zurich,” Suketu Patel, then chair of Caf’s finance committee, said in 2019.

“On that same day, we met with Infront. Their indicative offer on the table was a $450m minimum guarantee for eight years, as opposed to the $1bn, for 12 years, from Lagardère.

“If you look at our earlier contract of 2009, we had a minimum guarantee of $150m, but our income for the period was actually around $350m. We anticipated that the 12-year contract would have yielded about $1.3bn.

“I can tell you that whilst President Hayatou and I had differences on political matters, we never had one on the management of Caf finances. He did not interfere with the processes established for good governance.”

But that agreement was unilaterally terminated in December 2019 during the tenure of Ahmad Ahmad, Hayatou’s successor as Caf president.

A protracted legal dispute at the International Chamber of Commerce led to Caf, just over a year into the presidency of Motsepe, paying Lagardère a final settlement of $50m, as compensation for the breach of contract, just before the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.

“There is no way that any sponsor will be prepared to pay the same amount of money for a deal in which you would normally have four Afcons over an eight-year period, when you will now only have two. That is certainly a no-brainer,” said a former FA president with expertise in financial matters.

Sports.title: Football transfer rumours: Cristian Romero to leave Spurs for … Arsenal?
Sports.content:
Twenty-five years after Sol Campbell’s move from White Hart Lane to Highbury, are we finally getting a sequel? Cristian Romero, Tottenham’s captain, has piqued Arsenal’s interest, the Athletic reports, though they also reckon it’s pretty unlikely that Spurs will allow such drama. D’oh. It would bring some tantalising chaos to this transfer window, but Diego Simeone may well swoop him away to Atlético Madrid. Inter have their sights on him, too.

It could just be that a move for Rodri is what headlines the summer, the man who has completed football caught in a tug-of-war between Barcelona and Real Madrid. He’s said to have spoken to the Barça hierarchy as he looks to continue his shtick of winning everything in sight.

How about Djed Spence to Liverpool? There’s been some noise about a potential switcheroo with his new Spurs teammate Andy Robertson, but the Liverpool Echo says it’s not something the Reds have in mind. Forget the troubles at the back then: Andoni Iraola’s side continue to be linked with Paris Saint-Germain’s Ibrahim Mbaye as they look to strengthen out wide.

Joshua Zirkzee has been tagged with a move back to Serie A after two tough campaigns at Manchester United – maybe a loan deal at Juventus is the perfect tonic for the former Atalanta man. Could Arsenal’s Gabriel Jesus join him in Italy? Napoli – who enjoy taking in former Premier League marksmen – are said to be circling for the Brazilian. His teammate Ethan Nwaneri could be on for some minutes in the Bundesliga, with RB Leipzig apparently taking an interest in the 19-year-old forward.

A 22-year-old former Brighton man who now plays for Strasbourg, Julio Enciso must surely be on his way to Chelsea, right? No, it’s Ipswich who reportedly remain in the hunt to bring the Paraguayan back after his loan spell at the club last year, reuniting him with Gary O’Neil, his former manager in France. The Tractor Boys are also close to shoring up their midfield with Fulham’s Sasa Lukic, Sky Sports reckon.

A World Cup icon (in the eyes of the Mill) could be on his way to Glasgow. Egypt’s Haissem Hassan was electric against Argentina in their epic last-16 tussle last month, dancing down the wing to help set up the greatest goal that never was and very nearly delivering an all-timer of an upset. Celtic are in the market for the Real Oviedo winger.

Sports.title: Behind Milburn’s magic: Wor Jackie was a pit village hero and ‘everybody’s friend’ in Newcastle
Sports.content:
Of all the footballers who have worn the black and white, that possessive geordie pronoun “Wor” (our) was unique to Jackie Milburn; for he was a man of the people as much as he was a great sportsman. In that respect, his birthplace of Ashington in Northumberland only added to the mythology.

“The biggest pit village in the world,” as it was known, was the north-east in microcosm – a one-horse coal town where miles of identical terraced houses spread out from the pitheads and the menfolk were obsessed by whippets, leeks, association football and pints in the club. Nevertheless, he had a self-discipline that saw the pitfalls of alcohol: “Certainly it prevented my dad, Alec Milburn, from making the big time,” Jackie recalled. “He could have gone to Tottenham but preferred to stay home and drink his ale.”

At the St James’ Park homecoming following the 1951 FA Cup final, “Wor Jackie” (by which epithet his skipper Joe Harvey introduced him) was invited to address the throng. “At first I tried to ‘talk posh,” Jackie later recalled, “then there was a roar of laughter when a voice shouted, ‘Taak tiv us in your own language, Jackie!’” The dialect of Ashington is one of the most melodious varieties of the ‘pitmatic’ geordie of the coalfields, and still the butt of numerous jokes to this day (when an electrician asked a barmaid where the mains were, the answer came, “Tha just doon there, past the ladies.”)

View image in fullscreen A statue by Tom Maley of Jackie Milburn at Woodhorn Colliery Museum, near Ashington in Northumberland. Photograph: John Angerson/Alamy

Jackie’s lineage was important, for Ashington was an unusually fertile footballing hotbed. His great-grandfather, “Warhorse” Milburn, had kept goal for Northumberland in the 1880s, and young Jackie grew up reading about the Football League exploits of his four Milburn cousins who played professionally, while another cousin, Cissie Charlton, née Milburn, was later almost equally famous as the mother of World Cup winners Jack and Bobby.

Although the coalmines of Ashington demanded their human tribute, professional football was a feasible way out for many – and Milburn once counted 47 local boys he knew of who had played in the First Division. In his 1957 autobiography Golden Goals, he recalled waking early one Christmas morning to find a new pair of football boots at the end of the bed. He slipped them on straight away and headed out into the back lane at half past three in the morning only to find “most of my friends, wearing their new boots, playing football by torchlight in the middle of the street”.

View image in fullscreen Jackie Milburn’s second cousin Bobby Charlton thought that ‘his ball control at speed was as good as anyone I’ve seen’. Photograph: Colorsport/Shutterstock

The prevailing work ethic in pit villages throughout the coalfield helped to mould such formidable players. Miners were famed for their stamina, and with generations of pitmen in his family tree Milburn’s genetics shaped the way he played. In Ashington folklore it was told that Jackie kicked the same stone to school and back for three years, and his one-time teammate Len Shackleton was always impressed by his tenacity and “never-say-die spirit”. This was exemplified by tireless high pressing, and a trademark sliding tackle that hooked the ball from any defender unwise enough to prevaricate on the ball. In his early life he had made money as a sprinter, competing at Edinburgh in the famous Powderhall Handicap and running 100 yards in around 10 seconds.

With his pace, allied to phenomenal shooting power with either foot Milburn rightly takes his place in the Newcastle pantheon. His record of 200 goals in 401 appearances is second only to that of Alan Shearer.

Until 1948 Milburn combined football with work at local collieries, and as he didn’t then have a car, with almost too-perfect symbolism he would take the bus from Ashington into Newcastle with the same supporters who would pay to watch him. “The size of the crowd meant that it sometimes took us up to three-quarters of an hour to walk up the bank and round to the players’ entrance,” Milburn recalled. “But what could we do? Our supporters were a marvellous warm-hearted lot. They even flooded the club with clothing coupons to help kit out the side.” That cosy, close-knit and deeply sociable world of the postwar north-east suited Jackie down to the ground.

View image in fullscreen Newcastle United captain Joe Harvey (c) introduces Prime Minister Winston Churchill (l) to Jackie Milburn (r) before the 1952 FA Cup final. Photograph: PA Images/Alamy

“He was everybody’s friend!” wrote his famous second cousin Jack Charlton. “If you ever walked through Newcastle with him, you got stopped every two minutes; everybody said hello to him.”

Yet he never sought this fame, and it’s telling that whenever he went to the pictures in Ashington, he always waited until the lights were down before he entered the auditorium. Here was a modest and even shy man, who shared the small-c conservatism that characterised the otherwise Labour-voting north-east. He was thrilled to meet Winston Churchill at Wembley in 1952 – “the greatest hero of my life whose bust has occupied pride of place in our house since 1948” – as well as the ailing King George VI, whose courage he admired.

View image in fullscreen Newcastle centre forward Jackie Milburn with his wife Laura and daughters Linda (3) and Betty (2) in front of a picture on the wall of Milburn shaking hands with King George VI at the 1951 Cup Final, when his goal won the Cup for Newcastle. Photograph: Mirrorpix/Getty Images

In Golden Goals Milburn presents an image to the world of domestic bliss with his wife, Laura, admitting his aversion to gardening and patterned socks, and his enjoyment of watching TV, reading thrillers and going to the dog track most Wednesdays (greyhounds were always a miners’ passion).

Due to the dominance of a handful of dangerous, heavy industries it was a truism to say that communities across the north-east thrived on being in it together. This may have been one of the reasons why Jackie never quite made a consistent mark on the international stage, despite his 13 caps and 10 goals for England. In later life he confessed that many of his international teammates were too self-obsessed to play as a team and even suggested that “one or two of them were outright snobs”.

View image in fullscreen The Manchester City defenders can only stop and stare as Newcastle United’s Jackie Milburn (left) heads home to score his first-minute goal in the 1955 FA Cup final. Photograph: Popperfoto/Getty Images

Milburn became talismanic for Newcastle. When United’s new manager Dugald Livingstone took the probably rational decision to drop the ageing Milburn for the 1955 FA Cup final against Manchester City on form and fitness grounds, the wily former manager Stan Seymour – by then back upstairs in the boardroom – stepped in to overrule him. Milburn was duly reinstated and would score what was then the fastest Cup final goal – with a rare bullet header from a corner after only 45 seconds.

The people of the area saw in Jackie Milburn the image of their favourite son. He was modest, witty, warm and honest. He was effortlessly, unaffectedly dashing and handsome. He was hard when necessary, but always ready with a grin and a conciliatory word. He was a canny lad with a passion for his homeland.

He was never cautioned in his 14-year career, and the noted First Division whistler Arthur Ellis concluded that: “If there were 22 players on the field like Jackie you wouldn’t need a referee!” His teammate Joe Harvey noted that Jackie was “gentle and generous in victory, always first with the handshake in defeat”, and Milburn himself conceded that his innate courtesy, and tendency to play in colleagues when he had a chance to shoot himself, was a drawback. “I had a lack of devil.”

It’s amazing to think how much more lethal a ruthless Jackie Milburn would have been. But then he probably wouldn’t have been so endearing.

Sports.title: Arsenal hopes dashed after Vinícius Júnior extends Real Madrid contract to 2032
Sports.content:
Vinícius Júnior has ended summer speculation over his future by agreeing a new six-year contract with Real Madrid. Arsenal had been heavily linked with a move for the Brazil international, who had entered the final 12 months of his deal at the Bernabéu.

A tumultuous 2025-26 campaign in which Real failed to win a trophy and initial uncertainty after the arrival of José Mourinho in Madrid alerted the Premier League champions, but Vinícius has now committed his long-term future to the Spanish club.

“Real Madrid and Vinícius Júnior have agreed on the extension of our player’s contract, which links him to the club until 30 June 2032,” a club statement read.

“Vinícius Júnior joined Real Madrid in July 2018 at the age of 18. In his eight seasons wearing our jersey, he has played 375 matches, scored 128 goals, and won 14 titles: two Champions Leagues, three Club World Cups, two Uefa Super Cups, three La Liga titles, one Copa del Rey, and three Spanish Super Cups.

“His contribution to all these titles has been pivotal due to his gameplay, assists, and goals.”

Vinícius wrote on Instagram: “Eight years at the Bernabéu are too few … six more years, and for ever!”

The 26-year-old had hinted at extending his association with Real during an in-house interview on Tuesday where he spoke about Mourinho wanting him to be “happy” and “joyful” after a difficult spell.

A shock last-16 World Cup exit in America with Brazil also added to a frustrating 12-month period for Vinícius, but with his future settled the former Flamengo prospect will aim to help Real get back to competing for major honours again under Mourinho.

Tying down ‌Vinícius represents another significant ​step in an ​active summer for Real. The club have also strengthened their squad with the arrivals of winger Yan Diomande, midfielder Bernardo Silva, centre-back Ibrahima Konaté, left-back Marc Cucurella and wing-back Denzel Dumfries.

Sports.title: Kerolin failed to report for pre-season at Manchester City before Barcelona switch
Sports.content:
The Brazil forward Kerolin failed to report back for pre-season training at Manchester City in July before her transfer to Barcelona had been agreed.

Barcelona announced their signing of the 26-year-old on Tuesday but it was not until Thursday evening when Manchester City first made any reference to the transfer, eventually confirming they had received a WSL record fee for a sale more than 48 hours later.

Several staff and players at Manchester City were disappointed at what were perceived to be efforts by Kerolin to force a transfer to Barcelona and that her time at the club ended on a surprisingly sour note. She did not join pre-season with the Women’s Super League champions, which began in late July, despite previously having been felt to have been on good terms with the squad.

The deal, worth an initial €1.2m (£1m), represents the largest transfer fee received by a WSL club, and it could rise with add-ons to approximately £1.25m, although this has not been officially confirmed. It is one of the largest transfer fees in women’s football.

City said of Kerolin: “She grabbed 14 goals and six assists during that time, helping City to a WSL and FA Cup double in her solitary full season in England. And upon her transfer to Barça, City have received a WSL-club record transfer fee of €1.2m.

“Everyone at Manchester City would like to thank Kerolin for all her efforts at the club and wish her the very best in her future career.”

Kerolin was part of the City side that lifted their first WSL title in a decade last season and also helped them win the Women’s FA Cup. But within weeks of those celebrations many of her City colleagues have been stunned after she did not say goodbye in-person. Kerolin’s representatives have been contacted for a response.

High-profile examples of such transfer standoffs have been seen in men’s football, but incidents in the women’s game have been comparatively rare.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

City have no objections to the transfer in principle but sources have said the team were taken aback by the former North Carolina Courage star’s absence from pre-season fitness testing. For Kerolin, it is a dream move to the European champions, who beat OL Lyonnes in last season’s Women’s Champions League final.

City and Barcelona will meet in a friendly at the Joie Stadium on 15 August as the reigning champions of England and Spain step up their pre-season preparations.

Sports.title: Dele Alli can still make English football return as Championship transfer mooted
Sports.content:
Former Salford boss Karl Robinson believes Dele Alli is 'still a talent' but cannot afford to waste another opportunity.

Alli has not appeared in a competitive fixture since March last year, although that ended in despair.

3 Alli joined Como on a six-month deal with the option of an extra 12 months, but it didn't go to plan Credit: Getty

Making his comeback for Como after nearly 750 days in the cold, Alli came on in the 81st minute but was sent off less than 10 minutes later.

It proved to be his only appearance for Cesc Fabregas' side.

But Alli is now attempting to get his career back on track once again, with reports claiming he is training at Championship side West Ham United.

And Robinson, who bumped into Alli in Marbella whilst the latter was put through his paces during a pre-season camp, believes the 37-time England international still has plenty to give.

However, Robinson was quick to warn that given Alli's time away from football, he cannot be expected to return to the levels he's previously shown straight away.

The 'tell-tale sign' whether Alli is ready to return

"I had about an hour just chatting to him, just bumped into him really," Robinson told Alan Brazil and Ray Parlour on talkSPORT Breakfast.

"We spoke just about football in general, about how well he feels and how he wants to get himself back playing and how he seeks an opportunity.

"I think the problem you have in the modern world is social media governs an awful lot of our perception of them as a human being, first and foremost. We forget the fact he was and still is a talent.

"I think being away from football for so long, he was saying before about a pre-season, being away from a training ground for six weeks, it can be difficult to come back in and hit the ground running.

"Somebody who's not played competitive football for probably over 12 months, that's going to be the tell-tale sign. When he goes back over that white line with an actual match shirt, to see where he's actually at."

3 Robinson believes Alli can still succeed, but needs to have the right attitude Credit: Getty

Even though Alli may still have magic in his feet, Robinson acknowledged the attacking midfielder is very much in last chance saloon territory.

Robinson: It's all down to Alli now

He believes West Ham are fully aware of Alli's enduring talent and it is not too late for the ex-Tottenham man to revive his career in the Championship.

"Now, he's had multiple chances to get himself back playing, so you can't blame everybody else," Robinson continued.

"You've got to look at yourself, first and foremost.

"And at the end of the day, if he is given this opportunity and he goes in to West Ham and hits the ground running, they know they're going to have such a talented footballer. But that's down to him. It's not down to anybody else now.

"I think it's about him just putting his boots back on and doing something that he loves."

3 Alli made nearly 270 appearances for Spurs, scoring 67 goals Credit: AFP

Should Alli be offered a deal at West Ham, it would mark the first time he has appeared in the Championship following the Hammers' relegation from the top flight.

He began his career with MK Dons in League One before joining Tottenham in February 2015.

Alli spent six-and-a-half years in north London before he joined Everton.

But since he moved to the Toffees, Alli has played a total of 29 competitive fixtures in four-and-a-half years.

The Hammers begin their 2026/27 season on Saturday with a Carabao Cup first round fixture against Portsmouth, with talkSPORT providing live coverage from 1pm.

Sports.title: Ivan Toney left shocked as England striker charged with assault after incident at Soho nightclub
Sports.content:
Ivan Toney left shocked as England striker charged with assault after incident at Soho nightclub

England striker Ivan Toney has been charged with assault following an incident in London last December.

A statement from the Met Police read: "Ivan Toney, 30, of Northampton, was charged on Thursday, 31 July with assault causing actual bodily harm.

2 Toney will appear in court in September Credit: Getty

"He will appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Thursday, 24 September.

"The charge relates to an assault, which reportedly took place on 6 December 2025 at a nightclub on Wardour Street, W1."

Following the Met Police's statement, a spokesperson on behalf of Ivan Toney said: "Ivan acknowledges the charge and although he is naturally shocked, he looks forward to being given the opportunity to clear his name in court."

What is alleged to have happened at the Soho nightclub?

Toney is alleged to have headbutted a person at a venue in Soho.

According to reports, the incident was sparked by a fan who grabbed the England international for a photo, only to be pushed away.

After Toney repeatedly requested the man to get off of him, he allegedly dished out a headbutt.

Five officers were reportedly dispatched to the venue to deal with the situation.

The man who was headbutted by Toney got taken to a local hospital in an ambulance.

However, his injuries were not believed to be life-changing or life-threatening.

Toney was arrested at the scene on suspicion of two counts of assault and one count of affray.

2 The incident did not prevent Toney from playing games for club side Al-Ahli Credit: Getty

The 30-year-old was charged by police weeks after he participated in the World Cup for England.

Toney featured just twice for the Three Lions as they finished the tournament with a bronze medal.

He came off the bench in the dying stages of England's semi-final loss to Argentina as Thomas Tuchel's side desperately searched for a late equaliser.

Toney was then handed a starting berth for the third-place play-off against France, which ended in a 6-4 victory for the Three Lions.

The 30-year-old was drafted in to the England squad for the World Cup after he scored an impressive 42 goals in 49 games for Al-Ahli during the 2025/26 season.

Toney's eye-catching campaign at club level was bookended by Al-Ahli winning the AFC Champions League Elite for a second consecutive season.

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: Vinicius Junior signs new Real Madrid deal, Arsenal to announce Bruno Guimaraes, Spence latest
Sports.content:
'We will see'

Newcastle United new manager Matthias Jaissle has promised the Toon fans that new signings will be in place before the start of the season.

The German was officially confirmed as Eddie Howe's replacement yesterday.

And Jaissle's preparations for the upcoming Premier League campaign start with a tie against Valencia on Saturday.

Newcastle then start the season against Liverpool on Sunday, August 23.

And speaking to the media the first time, Jaissle discussed transfers.

He said: “Where can we finish this season after all the changes? That’s a tough question after one day of officially being the manager.

“We lost a couple of really important players, but I can see it as a positive challenge. We can search for excuses but that's not our idea.

“Give me a bit of time to get to know the players. I want to get to know them (players) first to see if they can show up. I want to give them a chance. We can wait.

“But we have the capacity do something in the market (sign players). Our sporting director is aware of that, so I'm sure when the season starts we will see some new faces."

Sports.title: ‘Shock horror’ – Argentina reveal stance on Gianni Infantino after World Cup controversy
Sports.content:
The Argentine Football Association (AFA) have pledged their support for besieged FIFA president Gianni Infantino.

Argentina have gone against the status quo amid increasing calls for Infantino to resign after his failed plans to launch the controversial FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE).

3 Infantino has support of the Argentine FA Credit: Getty

UEFA have reiterated their threat of boycotting the World Cup given that the 56-year-old acknowledged the mistakes with FFE, but is still in post.

They have 'lost confidence' in his presidency, whilst the Jordanian FA president Prince Ali bin Al Hussein made an accusation of 'blackmail' over endorsement of his re-election.

However, Infantino has received backing from the AFA, who released a statement to explain that he should continue as president.

"With our highest regards, On behalf of the Argentine Football Association (AFA), and its Executive Committee, we address you, dear President, and through you to the FIFA board, to express our support for the management carried out during the last 10 years, which had as its main axes the development of football throughout the world and the institutional solidity based on a clear, stable and transparent governance model.

"In this regard, with respect to the recent events that are public knowledge, we must acknowledge the Administration's decision to withdraw a project that, within the football family and from its inception, generated far more uncertainties than certainties.

"Therefore, it is worth highlighting the acknowledgment of the errors made in that process and the apology expressed in the heartfelt message sent to FIFA's 211 member associations. Prioritising governance standards is a fundamental pillar for strengthening good relations between FIFA, its member associations, and the confederations.

"Similarly, and as we have already stated, you are leading a management that has brought about a profound transformation of FIFA; that has opened the doors of the organisation to all member associations and confederations, so that through frank and direct dialogue, we can all continue to promote football at all levels and disciplines.

"From our perspective, this transformation was based on a transparent governance model, respect for statutory structures, and adherence to democratic procedures—essential principles for the football family to be united, strong, and working to continue generating improvements in both sporting and institutional aspects, which translate into a better quality of life for millions of people who practice our beloved sport.

"Therefore, given the proximity of the next FIFA Congress, the Association that I proudly preside over firmly believes and reaffirms that the way forward is to continue working under its leadership, in order to continue developing a better and even more inclusive football."

The Mexican Football Federation (FMF) also support Infantino, who they say is 'continuing to drive the development of football through institutional strengthening'.

3 Infantino has chosen not to resign despite depleting confidence in his presidency Credit: Getty

Little to no surprise

Now that Argentina have pledged support for Infantino, fans took to social media to reveal their lack of astonishment with the stance.

"Imagine my shock finding out Argentina support Infantino," one sarcastically commented.

A second added: "Shock horror Argentina back Infantino."

"Are we even surprised?" a third simply added.

World Cup questions

Argentina had a World Cup campaign that was filled with controversy this summer as fans threw unfounded accusations of bias at FIFA for supposedly supporting Lionel Messi's route to the final.

They entered as reigning champions and were bidding to become the first nation to win back-to-back titles since Brazil in 1962.

3 Argentina were at the centre of controversy during the World Cup Credit: Getty

However, their progression to the final was overshadowed by alleged racist abuse of internet star IShowSpeed from fans during their last 32 win over Cape Verde.

In their comeback win over Egypt in the last 16, Argentina were saved by VAR when Mostafa Ziko's first goal was ruled out for a seemingly soft foul on Lisandro Martinez moments before.

Mohamed Salah was also denied a penalty before Enzo Fernandez's winner, and Egypt boss Hossam Hassan claimed that FIFA wanted Lionel Messi to stay in the tournament.

Argentina then displayed a banner that read 'Las Malvinas son Argentinas', which means 'The Falkland Islands are Argentine' after they beat England in the semi-finals.

FIFA rules state that 'Equipment must not have any political, religious or personal slogans, statements or images', and later opened disciplinary proceedings against them.

The 2022 champions then disgraced themselves at full-time in their final defeat to Spain when their players attacked the opposition.

Leandro Paredes and Nahuel Molina were spotted lashing out, and are now facing assault charges.

Sports.title: Every Championship club ranked as final 2026/27 table predicted with potential record points total
Sports.content:
Every Championship club ranked as final 2026/27 table predicted with potential record points total

The new Championship campaign is almost upon us as another season of ups and downs awaits.

Following Coventry City, Ipswich Town and Hull City's promotion last term, who will reach the Premier League this time around?



6 Who will follow in Coventry's footsteps in the Championship this season? Credit: Getty

The season begins on Friday, August 14 as Wolves host Blackburn Rovers at Molineux, live on talkSPORT.

Wolves are one of three relegated sides returning to England's second-tier alongside Burnley and title favourites West Ham United, who are already using the transfer window to ensure their return.

Meanwhile, Lincoln City, Cardiff City and Bolton Wanders join the division following promotion from League One earlier this year.



This season will also see the play-offs expanded to eight teams, with more than half the division harbouring realistic promotion hopes.

The fallout from Southampton's Spygate scandal also continues to loom as the Saints begin the campaign with a four-point deduction.



Ahead of the season's kick-off, here is where all 24 clubs stack up in talkSPORT's predicted Championship standings.

Birmingham

Chris Davies' side achieved a respectable 10th place finish on their Championship return last season.



The Birmingham boss has once again been backed in the transfer market with more than £10million spent already.

However, it is the free transfer arrival of former Middlesbrough captain Dael Fry which could prove the most impressive.

A serious play-off push may be required to maintain the support of fans for Davies after periods of discontent last term, though.

talkSPORT Prediction: 6th

Championship on talkSPORT talkSPORT will bring you unmatched live and exclusive coverage of the Championship's opening weekend. Just look at what we've got in store! FRIDAY 14th AUGUST Wolves v Blackburn - 8pm (talkSPORT) SATURDAY 15th AUGUST Bolton v Preston - 12.30pm (talkSPORT)

Around the Grounds with Adrian Durham - 2.30pm (talkSPORT)

Middlesbrough v Lincoln - 3pm (talkSPORT 2)

Sheffield United v Birmingham - 5.30pm (talkSPORT 2) SUNDAY 16th AUGUST Watford v Southampton - 1.30pm (talkSPORT 2)

Burnley v West Ham - 4pm (talkSPORT 2) MONDAY 17th AUGUST Cardiff v Wrexham - 8pm (talkSPORT 2)

Blackburn

A change in the dugout for Blackburn this summer has done little to lift the spirits amongst supporters at Ewood Park.



Tony Mowbray is now in his second spell in charge, replacing Michael O'Neill, who steered Rovers to safety at the end of last term.

Their 20th place finish represented the second time in three seasons that the club had ended the campaign in the bottom six.

With just two new additions to the squad, a difficult season awaits for Rovers' long-suffering supporters.

talkSPORT Prediction: 23rd

Bolton

Bolton return to the Championship after a seven-year absence following their League One play-off triumph in May.



The Trotters are managed by former Stoke and Plymouth boss Steven Schumacher.

However, his squad remains limited on Championship experience despite the arrival of six new faces this summer.

Former loanees Mason Burstow and Amario Cozier-Duberry scored a combined 20 league goals last term and without them Bolton could be staring at an immediate return to the third-tier.

talkSPORT Prediction: 22nd

Bristol City

An exciting summer off the pitch has caused renewed optimism amongst the fanbase at Ashton Gate.



The Robins saw their play-off hopes fade last term before Gerhard Struber was sacked, with Michael Skubala now in place as his successor.

He has since brought in strikers Lorent Tolaj and Dom Ballard to bolster his attack, with the former scoring in an impressive friendly win over Newcastle United.

Repeating their sixth place finish from two seasons ago may prove a step too far, though, but another play-off push looks on the cards.

talkSPORT Prediction: 10th

Burnley

Burnley have clinched an instant return to the Premier League in each of their last two seasons at this level.



However, their is a feeling of the unknown around Turf Moor this summer under new boss Nicky Hayen.

6 Burnley suffered relegation for the third time in five seasons last term Credit: Getty

A title winner in Belgium, Hayen will be getting his first taste of English football this season.

The departures of several key players, including Maxime Esteve, Jaidon Anthony and Axel Tuanzebe, could prove to keep the Clarets out of the top two.



talkSPORT Prediction: 4th

Cardiff

Another of the newly-promoted sides, Cardiff finished second in League One last season under Brian Barry-Murphy.

As a result, they returned to the Championship at the first time of asking having finished bottom in 2024/25.

Just one top half finish in their last four seasons at this level suggests it could be another relegation battle for the Bluebirds this time around.

Barry-Murphy has put together a young side with plenty of exciting homegrown talent, though, which should have enough to survive.



talkSPORT Prediction: 20th

Charlton

Charlton avoided relegation on their return to the Championship last season.

Despite winning just one of their final nine matches, Nathan Jones' side ended the campaign six points above the drop zone.

The Addicks have since added Championship experience to their squad in the form of Karlan Grant and Danny McNamara.

Another strong start to the campaign may be crucial to build a gap between themselves and the wrong end of the table.



talkSPORT Prediction: 21st

Notable 2026/27 Championship fixtures Blackburn vs Burnley November 22 - Turf Moor

February 6 - Ewood Park Cardiff vs Swansea November 29 - Swansea.com Stadium

March 13 - Cardiff City Stadium Millwall vs West Ham September 19 - The Den

February 21 - London Stadium Portsmouth vs Southampton October 11 - St. Mary's Stadium

February 28 - Fratton Park Southampton vs Middlesbrough November 27 - St. Mary's Stadium

March 13 - Riverside Stadium West Brom vs Wolves September 20 - Molineux

February 20 - The Hawthorns

Derby

The Rams only missed out on a place in the play-offs on the final day of the season in May.

Their eighth place finish marked their highest for seven years as John Eustace's side came agonisingly close to extending their campaign.

With the new format expanding the play-offs to eight teams, Derby would have qualified if they had been introduced a year earlier.

The permanent signing of former loanee Bobby Clark, Sammie Szmodics' return and the promising arrival of Filip Bilbija could see another tilt for the top eight on the cards this term.



talkSPORT Prediction: 11th

Lincoln

Few outside of Lincoln would have predicted the Imps would win the League One title last season.

However, the club's first season in the second-tier for 66 years is already threatening to turn sour.

Promotion-winning manager Skubala has departed, with head coaches Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw replacing him in a dual-role.

Meanwhile, heavy pre-season defeats to lower league opposition is also a cause for concern.



Underdog status did not hinder Lincoln's promotion bid last season, but they may need a miracle to extend their Championship stay.

talkSPORT Prediction: 24th

6 Lincoln could be set for a difficult campaign after their promotion last season Credit: Getty

Middlesbrough

For much of last season, Middlesbrough looked destined to join Coventry in winning automatic promotion to the Premier League.

Boro ended 35 out of 46 matchdays inside the top two but ultimately faltered at the tail end of the campaign to finish fifth.



Kim Hellberg's side were subsequently beaten in the play-off final by Hull after being reinstated following Southampton's disqualification.

A busy summer in the transfer window has included the additions of Will Lankshear and World Cup star Sebastian Berhalter as promotion buzz once again sweeps Teesside.

The imminent arrival of goalkeeper Radek Vitek from Manchester United will see Boro's spending spree reach close to £40million.

talkSPORT Prediction: 3rd

Millwall

Millwall came agonisingly close to sealing promotion last term as they missed out to Ipswich on the final day.



The Lions went on to lose to Hull in the play-off semi-finals to consign them to a 10th consecutive season in the Championship.

Alex Neil has once again blended youth and experience with his signings this summer.

However, last seasons' club record points tally for this level will be difficult to repeat for the London club.

talkSPORT Prediction: 9th

Norwich

Philippe Clement's arrival in November triggered a stunning turnaround for Norwich in the 2025/26 campaign.



Having been 23rd when he was appointed, the Canaries went on to finish ninth under the Belgian.

The £8million signing of Andre Brooks from Sheffield United is one of four new additions to his side already this summer.

Having seen their late season surge come up short last term, Norwich could be one of the clubs to benefit from the expanded format.

talkSPORT Prediction: 8th

6 Millwall were flying but fell short despite their own record points total Credit: Getty



Portsmouth

John Mousinho remains in charge at Fratton Park despite interest from Bristol City at the start of the summer.

The Pompey boss once again avoided relegation last season despite countless injuries and one of the Championship's smallest budgets.

He has seen his transfer kitty increase this term with the reported £3million spent on striker Marko Milovanovic the club's biggest outlay on a single player since 2009.

Despite six new signings, keeping hold of Mousinho will likely prove Portsmouth's best business of the summer.



Whilst it may be too soon to dream of the play-offs, a more comfortable campaign can certainly be expected for fans.

talkSPORT Prediction: 17th

Preston

Paul Heckingbottom's side found themselves as close to the bottom three as the top six last season as they ended the campaign in 14th.

A run of one win in 13 between January and March proved to be the undoing for any faint promotion hopes.

Preston have since broken their transfer record to bring former loanee Alfie Devine back to the club from Tottenham Hotspur.



However, the expected departure of captain Ben Whiteman to Wrexham represents a blow on the eve of the new campaign.

talkSPORT Prediction: 18th

QPR

QPR spent time in both the relegation zone and the play-offs during a topsy-turvy first season in charge for Julien Stephan.

Their 15th place finish was enough to earn their French coach a new contract this summer, though.

An impressive transfer window has followed on paper for the Hoops, with former Premier League star Tariq Lamptey amongst the new arrivals.



Glen Kamara and highly-rated goalkeeper Pierce Charles have also joined on loan, leading fans to believe their 11-year stay in the Championship could come to an end.

talkSPORT Prediction: 13th

Sheffield United

A woeful start under Ruben Selles put an almost immediate end to any promotion hopes for the Blades last term.

Although legendary manager Chris Wilder steadied the ship on his return, he could only achieve a 13th place finish.

It marked a stark contrast to finishing third and suffering play-off final heartbreak the previous season.



A quiet window in terms of incomings along with the departure of Brooks to Norwich could see promotion once again out of the question for the Blades this time around.

talkSPORT Prediction: 14th

Southampton

Tonda Eckert's side embarked on a 19-match unbeaten run to end last season as they ultimately finished fourth in the table.

However, controversy soon followed as the club were disqualified from the play-offs for spying on Oxford United, Ipswich and Middlesbrough ahead of matches.

FA charges are now looming above Eckert's head with the outcome yet to be announced.



In terms of transfers, impressive loan signings Daniel Peretz and Cyle Larin have returned to St. Mary's, whilst Lewis Dobbin has been signed from Aston Villa.

A four-point deduction for their Spygate antics could prove costly for the Saints in the promotion race, though.

talkSPORT Prediction: 7th

6 Saints boss Eckert is awaiting to discover the outcome of his FA charges Credit: Getty

Stoke

The Potters have not finished higher than 14th since their relegation from the Premier League in 2018.



Mark Robins' side ended last season in 17th as fans were subjected to another mediocre campaign.

Hopes of a surge up the table are bubbling away, though, with over £20million spent already this summer.

Amongst their new arrivals, the signing of Ethan Galbraith from Swansea City has been tipped as a potential 'signing of the summer'.

If further interest inn Harry Clarke and George Hirst comes to fruition, a top half finish might not be out of the question.



talkSPORT Prediction: 16th

Swansea

Swansea were another club to benefit considerably from a managerial change last season.

Vitor Matos guided the club to an 11th place finish after taking over in November.

The goals of Championship top scorer Zan Vipotnik were largely to thank and the Slovenia striker has so far remained at the club.

Despite Galbraith's exit to Stoke, the Swans will hope to avoid being drawn into a relegation battle this season.



talkSPORT Prediction: 12th

Watford

Watford head into the new season fresh from appointing their 24th permanent manager in the last 14 years.

Alessio Dionisi is the new man in charge after Ed Still was sacked at the end of the previous campaign.

The Italian will be managing overseas for the first time in his career, with all six of his new signings to date arriving from Serie A.

Of those, five have been from Udinese, who like Watford are also owned by the Pozzo Family.



Since relegation from the top-flight in 2022, the Hornets have not finished higher than 11th and another bottom half finish appears likely this term.

talkSPORT Prediction: 19th

West Brom

Baggies fans will be desperate to put last season behind them as quickly as possible.

The club's 21st place finish represented their worst league campaign for 26 years following a two-point deduction in April for breaching PSR rules.

Former interim boss James Morrison has been rewarded for securing survival by being placed in permanent charge.



Whilst he has added to the squad, his side still appear to be lacking options on both wings.

A better season than last is almost certain, but play-off ambitions may have to be put on hold for another year.

talkSPORT Prediction: 15th

West Ham

The Hammers are set to play outside the Premier League for only the second time since 2005 this season.

Meanwhile, their last campaign at this level saw the club secure an immediate top-flight return via the play-offs 12 years ago.



Fans will expect nothing less than promotion again this term, with captain Jarrod Bowen remaining at the club.

Manager Nuno Espirito Santo and cult hero Tomas Soucek have also stayed put for the Championship.

Despite selling Mateus Fernandes to Tottenham and Crysencio Summerville to Saudi club Al Hilal, West Ham are more likely to set a points record than be subjected to a second season at this level come May.

Certainly the odds are pointing to a resounding title win.

talkSPORT Prediction: 1st

6 Keeping hold of Bowen has set the Hammers up for a Championship title tilt Credit: Getty



Wolves

Wolves have followed their disastrous Premier League campaign with an almost equally turbulent summer off the pitch.

Rob Edwards was sacked in June despite playing a key role in the signings of Kieran Trippier and Raul Jimenez.

His replacement Cesar Peixoto has now been charged with clinching an immediate top-flight return after their eight-year stay ended last term.

Wolves finished the campaign bottom of the table with just three league wins to their name.



With Joao Gomes their only notable departure and midfielder Andre signing a new deal, their squad appears too strong on paper for the majority of the division.

talkSPORT Prediction: 2nd

Wrexham

Phil Parkinson's side only missed out on the play-offs on the final day of the season last time out.

The Red Dragons ended the campaign two points adrift of the top six in seventh on their return to the second-tier after 44 years away.

Wrexham's Hollywood owners Rob McElhenney and Ryan Reynolds have taken a more reserved approach in the transfer market so far this summer.



Danny Imray is so far their only new addition, with the right-back arriving from Crystal Palace.

However, a deal for Fiorentina centre-back Matias Moreno is also thought to be close to completion.

Building on an impressive first season in the Championship, the Welcome to Wrexham cameras could be capturing promotion celebrations in nine months' time.

talkSPORT Prediction: 5th

Sports.title: Rodri’s decision made public in Barcelona vs Real Madrid transfer race
Sports.content:
Rodri has told Barcelona he wants to join them this summer, his agent has revealed.

Real Madrid recently opened talks with City over a move for the World Cup winning Spain captain.

2 Fresh from winning the World Cup, Rodri finds himself at the centre of a high-profile transfer battle Credit: Getty

However, their famous arch rivals have swooped in to hijack the deal.

talkSPORT reported on Thursday that Barca had moved ahead of Madrid in the race to sign Rodri.

Now, the 30-year-old's agent Pablo Barquero has told Spanish TV that his client is prioritising a move to the Nou Camp.

“Out of respect for Madrid, as they have been class, Rodri informed them that his decision is to join Barca," Barquero said.

Rodri is out of contract at the Etihad next summer, but City are still thought to be demanding a significant transfer fee, more than the £42million being reported.

City are not yet resigned to losing Rodri this summer and could elect to keep the four-time Premier League winner - even if he refuses to sign a new deal.

The midfielder, who won the Ballon d'Or in 2024 and the Golden Ball at the 2026 World Cup, is thought to prefer a move to Spain due to family reasons.

Rodri is expected to be sidelined for the beginning of the season, wherever that may be, after recently undergoing back surgery.

Keep at all costs?

City recently signed Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for £116m and are expected to land superstar Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi.

However, talkSPORT host Adam Catterall recently argued that losing Rodri could cost City their shot at regaining the Premier League title.

2 Anderson is City's latest big-money signing Credit: Isaac Parkin / Manchester City FC

"There's a lot of chat about Rodri, at the moment, off the back of his fantastic World Cup (with Spain)," he said.

"I know that off the back of his injury last year, he wasn't at his scintillating best, but the World Cup kind of pointed in the direction that the Ballon d'Or winner is back to his very, very best.

"I genuinely believe that if he does go to Real Madrid in this window, that will scupper any chances that Manchester City have of winning the Premier League.

"I think he's that influential. He has to be at City, if City are going to make a Premier League challenge this year."

Ex-Premier League defender Ashley Williams added: "My concern is that they've brought in Elliot Anderson and think, 'We can probably live without Rodri', but they can't, I think they need both of them.

"I love Elliot Anderson, I think he's brilliant, he'll be the future.

"But wouldn't it be great for him to have all that he's got already and learn off Rodri with the way he plays? And have both of them at least overlapping for a couple of seasons.

"At no point would you ever, ever get rid of Rodri, for no amount of money. They could offer me whatever and I wouldn't sell Rodri."

Sports.title: Inside Leeds' blueprint to get into Europe: Daniel Farke's brutal pre-season regime borrowed from Jurgen Klopp, how they beat Champions League clubs to sign Harry Wilson and the two new faces they want now
Sports.content:
Inside Leeds' blueprint to get into Europe: Daniel Farke's brutal pre-season regime borrowed from Jurgen Klopp, how they beat Champions League clubs to sign Harry Wilson and the two new faces they want now

Unlock more from inside the Leeds camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

Leeds United are making a splash this summer – and not just because players had the pleasure of rubbing shoulders with Michael Phelps in the United States last week.

The minority investor was there to watch his team play Liverpool off the park in the second half of a 4-2 friendly win in Chicago, with two training-ground throw-in routines that would not have looked out of place in the NFL matches Soldier Field usually hosts.

Phelps, the greatest Olympian of all time with 23 gold medals, has brought his kids up as Leeds fans and he will be hoping Daniel Farke’s team are ready to progress after a season battling to stay afloat upon their return to the Premier League.

Leeds have had an encouraging summer window so far that saw them win races to sign Harry Wilson on a free transfer and England goalkeeper James Trafford in a club-record £45million deal from Manchester City.

New £34million Bosnia defender Tarik Muharemovic, fresh from having his ankle trodden on by Folarin Balogun at the World Cup, looks a solid buy from Sassuolo to replace Pascal Struijk. And, with a couple more signings – a left back and another attacker are on the list – Leeds could have a squad ready to challenge the top half of the Premier League after finishing 14th last time out.

Some are even mentioning the dreaded ‘E’ word and want to take inspiration from Sunderland and Nottingham Forest, two clubs who managed to get into Europe within three years of promotion back to the top flight, as well as Brighton and Bournemouth.

Leeds turned on the style in Chicago last week against Liverpool, coming from 2-0 down to win 4-2

Daniel Farke put the squad through a gruelling pre-season. Many days saw two training sessions, with double workouts to condition the body for an arduous campaign ahead

Minority investor Michael Phelps was there to watch his team play Liverpool off the park in Chicago

Farke put the squad through a gruelling pre-season. Many days saw two training sessions, with double workouts to condition the body for an arduous campaign ahead. In the morning, they would be football-focused and, in the afternoon, sessions would be strength-based.

There were two days of fitness tests to start pre-season and the footballs have been out every day but one, with players feeling a difference on the pitch after Farke’s physically demanding routines.

Farke, who asks players to call him ‘boss’ and dislikes the moniker ‘gaffer’, took inspiration from Jurgen Klopp for his workouts that involve a 1km running drill known as the lactate test, which measures how long it takes for lactic acid to build quicker than the body can clear it. The longer, the better – and it exposed who was keeping fit and who had slacked over summer.

When Leeds were promoted 12 months ago, the recruitment team were ahead of the curve in noticing a trend in the Premier League. They knew the game was switching to a more direct style and many of their transfer targets were, for want of a more diplomatic phrase, big brutes. Anton Stach is 6ft 4in, Jaka Bijol and Sebastiaan Bornauw 6ft 3in, Lukas Nmecha and Sean Longstaff 6ft 1in.

This year, they will stick by that policy and 6ft 4in Muharemovic fits into it – but Leeds are keen for a bit of flair, too. Germany winger Julian Brandt was targeted but ended up going to Ajax. Former Fulham man Wilson, then, is the star attraction.

Several clubs, including Champions League-bound Aston Villa, had made a pitch to sign Wilson when it became clear he would follow manager Marco Silva out of the door at Craven Cottage. But he chose Leeds for a number of reasons.

One was the fact Leeds made a push to sign him 12 months earlier, which proved to Wilson that they did not simply want him because he was available for nothing. With the possibility of qualifying for the World Cup with Wales, Wilson did not want the turbulence of moving at that time.

Chairman Paraag Marathe has recently stepped aside from his position at the San Francisco 49ers to focus on his football ventures, including Rangers. He sold the winger a dream on the second of many calls between player and club. Marathe made Wilson feel wanted.

New 6ft 4in, £34m signing Tarik Muharemovic (right) adds to Leeds' land of the giants

Several clubs, including Champions League-bound Aston Villa, had made a pitch to sign Harry Wilson, but he chose Leeds

Chairman Paraag Marathe has recently stepped aside from his position at the San Francisco 49ers to focus on his football ventures, and played a key role in convincing Wilson to join Leeds

He talked about the loud, proud and loyal fanbase and discussed how Leeds were in the process of redeveloping Elland Road to increase its capacity.

‘After the first call I had with Leeds, with the chairman about the direction of the club, they were my number one choice,’ Wilson told us this week. ‘I spoke to a couple of other teams and nothing changed my mind.

‘The ownership group, the plans they have for the club. They know the size of the club with the fanbase and the history and the work they're doing to the stadium already to increase the capacity, the investment they're putting into the squad. It's all just going in one direction and that's what I want to be a part of.’

Marathe and a phone call from Farke, who tried to sign Wilson at his former club Norwich City, went a long way – but nothing sweetened the deal more than the persistence of club captain Ethan Ampadu, a Wales team-mate.

‘I almost had to block Ethan!’ laughed Wilson. ‘He played a big role. I'm really close with all the Welsh boys here. DJ (Dan James), I've played with since we were 14. Joe (Rodon), similar.

Asked about his ambitions, Wilson – who had the best season of his career last term, with ten league goals and seven assists – added: ‘Clubs have shown in recent years that the first season back in the Premier League, it's all about making sure you stay up. But in the end, Leeds stayed up really comfortably last season.

‘When you look at the likes of Sunderland and Forest, who've come up in recent years and have got into Europe, that's definitely an aim that we can have.

'But I think that second season syndrome has been the case with a few teams. So this season let's try and build on what the club created last year, that strong base, making sure our home form is good, which is massive and let's see where that takes us.’

Harry Wilson (left) adds to the Welsh contingent in Leeds' squad, including Daniel James (second left), Ethan Ampadu (right) and Joe Rodon (not pictured)

Wilson believes Leeds can take inspiration from the likes of Sunderland and Nottingham Forest in qualifying for Europe soon after promotion to the Premier League

Farke is set to stick by the back-five formation that turned his fortunes around last term. The boss had been sleepwalking towards the sack as Christmas approached, with Leeds in the relegation zone with a run of six defeats in the seven games leading up to December.

But after the switch, Leeds lost only five of 25 matches and reached an FA Cup semi-final.

Farke was criticised for his negative tactics at Wembley and knows he must build on solid defensive foundations with more exciting football this time around.

Trafford is a marquee signing. Some City observers believe he should have been given the No 1 jersey ahead of Gianluigi Donnarumma and many in the England set-up expect him to be the long-term successor to Jordan Pickford.

Comfortable in possession and a strong shot-stopper, it is an excellent addition, beating Newcastle United to the punch. Business is not done yet and a versatile attacker is top of the list. Dominic Calvert-Lewin had a fine season, scoring 15 times in all competitions, but needs help in sharing the goals around, with none of his team-mates managing more than eight.

Farke believes US international Brenden Aaronson is vastly underrated but another creative outlet would be welcomed with open arms, especially after Jack Harrison departed for MLS side New England Revolution. A deputy for injured left back Gabriel Gudmundsson is also wanted.

The boss has three more friendlies to fine-tune his squad: RB Leipzig and Augsburg at home on back-to-back Saturdays, and a clash with rivals Manchester United in Dublin at Croke Park on Wednesday.

Farke fell into coaching by accident having graduated in economics and originally wanted to be a sporting director.

This is his third crack at the Premier League after two relegations with Norwich, but sources insist he is growing every week and he believes that relationships have a greater impact than tactics.

Farke believes US international Brenden Aaronson is vastly underrated but another creative outlet would be welcomed with open arms

Sources insist Farke is growing every week and he believes that relationships have a greater impact than tactics

A literature nut whose favourite author is Gabriel Garcia Marquez, he also likes 19th-century poet Walt Whitman. The American’s best-known line ‘I contain multitudes' speaks to how leaders must contradict themselves to find answers.

Farke and the hierarchy will be mulling those over in the coming weeks: how to maintain Leeds’ solid base but still take attacking strides? How to keep his trademark calm demeanour while demanding more? How to be more ambitious in the transfer market without it coming back to bite financially?

If they can get the answers right, they can be successful this season. Just maybe not quite as successful as Mr Phelps.

Atletico Madrid remain in talks with Tottenham over Cristian Romero but are yet to table a formal offer
