Sports.title: Roy Keane and Micah Richards dress up as traditional Victorian gentlemen, perform pigskin keepy-uppies and enjoy a day out at the terraces as they turn back the clock for Sky Bet's new 'Game's Back' advert
Sports.content:
Roy Keane and Micah Richards have embraced football's roots by dressing as Victorian gentlemen for Sky Bet's latest 'Game's Back' campaign.

Revisiting football's earliest days ahead of the new Premier League season, the popular Sky Sports punditry duo donned period costumes as they took in the action from the terraces and showed off their keepy-uppy skills with a traditional pigskin ball.

Sky Bet's new advert, which officially launched on August 7, plays on the familiar 'game's gone' phrase often used by supporters looking back nostalgically at how the sport has changed over the years, from players refusing to celebrate against former clubs to the introduction of VAR.

The advert begins with Keane and Richard sitting on the sofa watching modern-day football, before the Manchester United legend complains that the 'game's gone' over a five-minute VAR decision.

The punditry duo then take a trip through different eras of football to discover that supporters were always questioning how the game was evolving.

Transported first to 1965, the pair complained about the introduction of the substitutions law before heading further back in time to 1891 to learn how fans moaned when nets were first attached to goalposts.

Popular punditry duo Roy Keane and Micah Richards have embraced football's roots by dressing as Victorian gentlemen for Sky Bet's latest 'Game's Back' campaign

Richards and Keane also showed off their keepy-uppy skills with a traditional pigskin ball

In one light-hearted moment, Richards shushes his famously fiery punditry partner while the pair watch on from the stands, poking fun at Keane's well-known habit of questioning changes in the modern game.

Sky Bet also shared behind-the-scenes footage of Keane and Richards shooting the advert, which showed off the duo's chemistry.

Keane said: 'One thing about football history is that people have always questioned changes to the game, but it's funny looking back at some of the things we'd never want to lose now.

'We had good fun bringing those moments to life.'

Richards added: 'Football fans love a debate and that's never going to change'.

'Game's Gone is a phrase that has engrained itself in football culture and beyond,' said Harry Phillips, Sky Bet Marketing Director.

'Yet even though we all love to moan about the game, it's never been more universally popular and when push comes to shove, it's the incredible moments of football culture, both on and off the pitch that keeps us coming back.

Sky Bet's new campaign plays on the familiar 'the game's gone' phrase often used by supporters looking back nostalgically at how the sport has changed over the years

'We believe football always has and always will create moments no fan can resist. And at Sky Bet, we champion those iconic moments of football and fandom by giving our customers more ways to get in on the action.'

The new Premier League season kicks off with champions Arsenal hosting newly-promoted Coventry City on Friday, August 21.

Sports.title: Powerlifting racism row: Spotter declares 'I am racist' after sabotaging star's record attempt - admitting in astonishing social media post: 'I did it intentionally'
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

A powerlifting assistant is under police investigation in Lithuania after claiming he deliberately sabotaged a Black athlete's squat attempt because he is 'racist'.

Belgian athlete Sonita Muluh's attempt to squat 334.5kg at the World Classic Open Powerlifting Championships in Lithuania in June was disqualified after spotting assistant Ernestas Kusinas placed his knee under the barbell during the lift.

After the event, Kusinas sparked outrage by claiming in an Instagram post that he had deliberately sabotaged Muluh's lift because he is 'racist', a remark he later insisted was intended to mock those accusing him of racism.

The Lithuanian Powerlifting Federation referred the case to police, who have launched an investigation into both the Instagram post and the events at the championships, a spokesperson told Reuters.

The Instagram remark read: 'Sorry for you morons, I'm racist and I did it on purpose because I hate you pieces of s***'.

If found guilty, Kusinas could face a maximum sentence of two years in prison.

Powerlifting assistant Ernestas Kusinas (above) is under police investigation in Lithuania after claiming he deliberately sabotaged a Black athlete's squat attempt because he is 'racist'

The spotter placed his knee on the barbell during Sonita Muluh's attempt to squat 334.5kg

Kusinas later told Reuters the Instagram post was written in anger and was intended to mock social media users who had accused him of racism, rather than reflect his true views.

The spotter claimed he had unintentionally interfered with Muluh's attempt as a result of being tired from his duties at the event.

Kusinas, who has since been banned for life from all powerlifting events by the Lithuanian federation and switched his social media accounts to private, claimed he had 'thrown him the bone he wanted' in response to an unidentified Instagram user who had accused him of racism.

Muluh, 29, became world champion in 2024 and has won medals at multiple Powerlifting Championships throughout her impressive career.

The Cameroon-born powerlifter's partner Kristof De ​Coninck urged that she could have won the event in Lithuania without Kusinas' interference, insisting poor assistance risked 'very serious injuries'.

'Initially, we thought it was a mistake,' De Coninck said.

'But then, it became clear (because of the social media comment) that the person had done it ⁠deliberately, motivated ​by racial bias.'

Speaking to BBC Sport about the controversy, Muluh said: 'It's shocking to wake up five weeks later and it's all over the internet that he did it on purpose because of the colour of my skin.

'I feel unsafe and uneasy that this person is standing beside me with massive weight, with what can go wrong, with the amount of weight on your back.

'I was lucky when I realised [it hit his knee] and I could stabilise it. Not everyone could. It was the heaviest ever squat for a female.

'(Kusinas) did not reach out afterwards to apologise, but he is not obliged to. I thought it was a human mistake, that cost me a lot on the day.

In an Instagram post after the event, he claimed he did it intentionally because he is 'racist'

Muluh, pictured in 2025, admitted she feels 'unsafe and uneasy' after his Instagram comment

'But there was no hatred [from me]. I didn't lash out; didn't curse at him. There was a video of it posted afterwards and I said: "I hope he does not get hate." I believed it was an honest mistake.

'And then I find out five weeks later that he said this.'

Meanwhile, the Lithuanian Powerlifting Federation has said in a statement: 'We would like to address the situation that unfolded on social media.

'We reviewed available information relating to Ernestas Kusinas and were deeply shocked by the views and activities addressed publicly which contradict the principles we stand for.

'The federation takes full responsibility for addressing this matter.'

Sports.title: Former Man United striker and Uruguay legend appointed as national team head coach after Marcelo Bielsa exit
Sports.content:
Diego Forlan has been appointed as head coach of Uruguay's national team and their Under-20s side.

Forlan succeeds Marcelo Bielsa, who stepped down as Uruguay boss after their failure to progress from the group stage at the World Cup.

Uruguay drew with Saudi Arabia and Cape Verde in their opening two matches, before defeat to Spain confirmed the two-time champions' exit from the competition.

The Uruguayan Football Association stated that Forlan will take up his dual role as part of a project to strengthen the pathway from the Under-20 side into the senior national team.

Former Man United and Atletico Madrid striker Forlan will take charge of the national team for the first time in their upcoming friendlies in September and October.

'One of the most important figures in the history of La Celeste begins a new chapter: he will be the head coach of both the Under-20 and Senior National Teams,' a Uruguayan Football Association statement read.

Diego Forlan has been announced as head coach of Uruguay's national and Under-20 teams

Forlan succeeds Marcelo Bielsa, who oversaw their disastrous World Cup campaign

'Forlan returns to where he left an indelible mark. A role model, icon, and emblem of an unforgettable generation, the best player of the 2010 South Africa World Cup returns now to contribute his experience, leadership, and profound knowledge of international football from a technical position.

'The new coach will begin working immediately with the under-20 team. There, he will lead a project aimed at developing young talent, supporting their growth, and strengthening their path to the senior national team.

'He will work with Santiago Espasandín and Diego Perez as assistant coaches, Marco Mansulino as physical trainer, Ignacio Bordad as goalkeeping coach, and Gabriel Skrilec as video analyst.

'His first challenge at the helm of the senior national team will come during the September-October international window, when Uruguay plays its FIFA friendly matches.

'It will mark the beginning of a new era, with one of its greatest idols once again at the helm.'

Reports have claimed that Forlan's appointment as national team coach is initially on an interim basis, with a review expected to take place in March next year.

During his playing career, Forlan scored 36 goals in 112 appearances for Uruguay and represented the national team at three World Cups and Copa Americas.

Forlan captained and starred for Uruguay on their run to the World Cup semi-finals in 2010

Forlan starred at the 2010 World Cup in South Africa, where he scored five goals and was named player of the tournament as Uruguay reached the semi-finals for the first time since 1970.

The forward was part of Uruguay's Copa America winning side the following year.

Forlan has limited managerial experience having coached his former club Penarol for 11 matches before being sacked in 2020, before a brief 12-match spell in charge of Atenas.

The 47-year-old also made his professional tennis debut back in 2024.

Sports.title: FREDDIE BURNS interview: I beat the All Blacks on my England debut - then woke up at the training ground in a pile of my own sick
Sports.content:
FREDDIE BURNS interview: I beat the All Blacks on my England debut - then woke up at the training ground in a pile of my own sick

Unlock more of the best of our rugby coverage with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

Freddie Burns is laughing down the phone from Romania.

‘It was typical of me to miss out the slide on my Instagram post that actually said I was retiring,’ chuckles the former Bath, Gloucester, Leicester and England No 10.

‘I had to post it again separately just to make sure people were clear!’

In an 18-year professional rugby career, Burns, now 36, has always been an entertaining character. So, it was fitting he continued that trend when announcing it was coming to an end on social media this week.

In an era where most modern players trot out anodyne press conference quotes and seem reticent to show their true selves, Burns has always been an outlier.

‘I’ve had some good moments and some f****** low ones,’ says Burns, who will play one more season with Dinamo Bucharest before calling it quits.

Freddie Burns has announced he will retire from rugby later this year. 'I've had good moments and some f****** low ones,' he tells Daily Mail Sport

Burns kicked two penalties against the All Blacks on debut in 2012 as England stunned the world champions with a 38-21 hammering

He also became a Leicester cult hero, after kicking the drop-goal that sealed the Premiership title for the Tigers in 2012

He will depart as one of English club rugby’s cult heroes. A more-than-talented fly-half, whose last-gasp drop-goal sealed Leicester the PREM Rugby title in 2022, Burns won five England caps. His Test debut was one to remember. He kicked two penalties as a replacement in a famous 2012 victory over New Zealand. Not a bad way to start.

‘All I remember from that night was being hammered when I went up to collect my England cap at the post-match function at Twickenham,’ recalls Burns.

‘I was bumping into all these legends, guys like Richie McCaw and Dan Carter. I was s*** faced. It was just after the 2011 World Cup and all the shenanigans that had gone on there. Stuart Lancaster was the coach and the RFU were still trying to save some face. So, we drank hard at Twickenham, then got the bus back to Pennyhill Park instead of going out.

‘I woke up on the floor of the bathroom in my room at Pennyhill. It had a heated floor and there was a lovely little pile of sick cooking next to me. I was still wearing my suit.

‘I was quite glad we didn’t go out that night as there would probably have been a good chance I’d have ended up in the Thames!’

Burns adds: ‘As a boy, I lived down the road from where Bath trained. When I watched them, I remember thinking playing just a minute of PREM Rugby would have been enough for me. My career went miles beyond what I expected.

‘I could have played more for England. But I want to be grateful for the five caps I got, not the ones I didn’t. It was five more than most people get. I want to avoid being bitter about things that didn’t happen because I’ve had so many good ones that did. I want to be thankful for that.’

Burns played hard and celebrated harder. But his outgoing character – sadly all too rare in the game these days – shouldn’t distract from his on-field ability.

Three of Burns' five Tests came against New Zealand, scoring 20 points in two matches on England's 2014 tour

‘I could have played more for England. But I want to be grateful for the five caps I got, not the ones I didn’t'

Burns started at Gloucester, had two stints at Leicester, and also represented his home city of Bath. Rugby also gave him the chance to travel the world. He made trips to Japan and New Zealand with Shokki Shuttles and the Highlanders respectively and will end his playing days in one of the game’s more unusual outposts in Romania.

‘In rugby, there are a lot of very, very tough days with a few brilliant ones sprinkled in,' Burns says, 'One thing I’d say to young players now is make sure you enjoy your wins.

'That doesn’t mean you have to have 20 beers. Now, players focus on having their protein shake and a good sleep. When you have a good win, sit in the changing room with your mates you’ve gone to battle with. Enjoy having a drink or two. Share time with the opposition. It all goes by so quick.

'I definitely made the most of my career in terms of celebrating! But even now, I still wish I’d enjoyed certain moments more.

'One of my frustrations with rugby is that there are so many brilliant personalities in the game, but some lads don’t want to express themselves or say their opinion. The Six Nations Netflix documentary was so f****** boring. It didn’t show the personalities of the players. You’re starting to see that more now with guys like Henry Pollock. Hopefully it continues.’

If downing the All Blacks and slotting a PREM-winning drop-goal were Burns’ highs, one of the lows came in 2018. In action for Bath against Toulouse, he celebrated what should have been a try too early and Frenchman Maxime Medard knocked the ball from his grasp.

Burns broke through as a 19-year-old, having joined Gloucester from Bath's academy and going on to spend six seasons at Kingsholm

Burns celebrates too early while playing for Bath against Toulouse in a Champions Cup match and has the ball knocked out of his hand by Maxime Medard

‘The thing I’m most proud of in my career is my resilience,’ Burns says. ‘That’s what that incident taught me.

'The biggest frustration with that game is if I’d scored and we’d won, I reckon I’d have been man of the match! I had a brilliant game at full-back. I scored one and kicked a couple of long-range penalties. Yes, I s*** the bed at the end but on the whole, I was all right! I’m glad it happened because of the way my career panned out after that.

‘I went to Wasps the weekend after and I kicked well in a draw. I got off the bus there and immediately, there was a camera in my face. I knew it was what all the pundits were talking about. The keyboard warriors were after me.’

Burns celebrated winning the PREM in 2022 by doing the post-match press conference in his pants, before a big night out, a mammoth McDonald’s order and heading to bed with the trophy.

‘We partied hard. It was just a big feeling of relief,’ he says. ‘Before I’d come back to Leicester, I’d had to deal with the blow to the ego of going to Japan. It was one of the best things that happened to me, but at the time going to the Japanese second division at 30 was tough.

‘I was thinking, “F****** hell, is this where my career has gone?”.

‘The funniest stories have come from the hard times. When Aaron Mauger was coach at Leicester, he came in one day and put a Tigers shirt in the bottom of an empty bucket.

‘He gave each player an empty pint glass and said: “Go and fill your glass up with how much you’ve given to the shirt and what you’re willing to do for this club.”

‘Most guys filled their glasses two thirds or so full. One of the academy lads who hadn’t really played much walked up to the bucket so slowly because his cup was so full. We absolutely f****** hammered him for that!

'I don't really care what people thought of me as a player,' reflects Burns. 'But I'd always like to think they'd say I was a good bloke'

'I tried to never lose the love of the game. Sometimes I was s*** and sometimes I was OK, but I’d like to think the fans always saw I tried.

'I don’t really care what people thought of me as a player. People will think I’m good, bad and indifferent. But I’d always like to think that when my name comes out of someone’s mouth, they’d say I was a good bloke.

'If that’s all I’m remembered for, then I’ll be happy.’

Sports.title: How Enzo Maresca and Hugo Viana created the new Man City with two-year post-Guardiola plan - the four 'cornerstone' players set to fill leadership void and who's coming and going in midfield overhaul
Sports.content:
There has been an obvious drive over the summer to futureproof the Manchester City squad, with Jeremy Doku becoming the latest star to commit to a new five-year contract.

Doku joins Josko Gvardiol, Phil Foden and Abdukodir Khusanov in agreeing fresh terms over the past fortnight, the quartet seen as integral to the new era of City. A City without Pep Guardiola and a City without so many of the stalwarts synonymous with rampant success.

Gvardiol and Doku, two of last season’s standout performers, are still only 24 (Foden is 26, Khusanov 22) and the hope is that the pair are the sort of figures who will provide a cornerstone to an evolving team and club.

Clearly, director of football Hugo Viana and new boss Enzo Maresca have identified the men they believe can step into the shoes of Bernardo Silva, Kevin De Bruyne, Riyad Mahrez and more than a few others in exacting standards and taking on the responsibility of delivering consistent trophies.

It is difficult to think of too many harder jobs in elite football than that right now, especially if Rodri secures a move back to Spain, with Barcelona now rivalling Real Madrid for his signature.

A departure of a midfielder crowned the best player at the World Cup would leave City’s four-man leadership group cut in half in recent months and points to the lack of real experience – something Maresca addressed earlier in the stifling week in Seoul.

Jeremy Doku (left) has become the latest Manchester City star to commit to a new five-year contract

Defender Josko Gvardiol has also agreed fresh terms, and is a key part of the City rebuild under Enzo Maresca

Rodri will leave very large boots to fill should he leave for Barcelona or Real Madrid

Gvardiol and Foden have both publicly raised their hands to take roles in the captaincy team and there is jostling behind the scenes between players who want to make their mark under a fresh regime – one that ought to offer some of them renewed energy.

Nico Gonzalez, who failed to start a single league game between January and May, insisted that he is one of them.

‘I’m happy here,’ said Gonzalez, who joined for £50million 18 months ago. ‘I don’t want to leave and I think the club wants me to stay. If we win, I’m happy. My dream is to win trophies.

'If I don’t play any matches and we win the Champions League next year, I will be so happy. The final of the FA Cup I was not picked but we won so it was an amazing day for me. To be honest, last season I couldn’t have expected to have played almost 30 matches in the starting XI. I played really good. I’ve had many opportunities.’

Gonzalez – who didn’t even make the bench for that FA Cup final he referenced – does have his price but it has become clearer in recent days that Tijjani Reijnders is more likely to exit the building before the window closes. Nottingham Forest and Newcastle United are monitoring the Dutchman, valued at £55million.

Be it Rodri or Reijnders or both, City sources have indicated that they are ready to replace any potential outgoings. The pursuit of Ayyoub Bouaddi, a breakout talent at the World Cup with Morocco, is a separate entity and they are pressing ahead with negotiations with Lille regardless of movements in the other direction.

They had accelerated the rebuild in January, spending £85million on Antoine Semenyo and Marc Guehi, with the two signings from Bournemouth and Crystal Palace embedded into the squad then rather than now – which ought to represent something of an advantage moving forward.

Semenyo contributed to two trophy wins – scoring the FA Cup-winning goal over Chelsea – while Guehi was ineligible to feature in the Carabao Cup final, a decision that riled Guardiola.

Nico Gonzalez insists he is happy at City despite failing to start a league game between January and May

City are pressing ahead with negotiations with Lille for Moroccan midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi (right)

But Tijjani Reijnders could be on the way out amid interest from Nottingham Forest and Newcastle

City believe the strategy of doing those deals six months early, and supplementing it by breaking their transfer record with £116million Elliot Anderson once Maresca assumed the post, will reap its rewards.

‘I don’t think any player has the position guaranteed for all the matches,’ Gonzalez added. ‘We are one of the best teams in the world and obviously there is competition in every position. That is what makes us be in the position that we are, winning so many Premier Leagues and competing for everything.’

Gonzalez is talking about a different squad though. He’s never won a title. Only five of this group were around for the Treble, revealing quite how much rebuilding has gone on in the three seasons since.

City have spent much of the last two years planning for this moment, for life after Guardiola, and now the time has come to determine how meticulous that has been.

Sports.title: Man City target new goalkeeper after James Trafford sale, Bruno Guimaraes nears £75m Arsenal move and Man United confirm signing of star, 18: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Arsenal interested in Spurs captain

Arsenal admire Cristian Romero - but a sale to the Gunners would not be contemplated by Tottenham.

The Spurs captain remains the subject of strong interest from Atletico Madrid and Inter who had a £34.2m fee in place.

Spurs meanwhile are preparing a new long-term contract for defender Micky van de Ven.

The Netherlands centre-back has a deal until 2029.

Spurs defender Ashley Phillips is joining Middlesbrough for £7m and the deal could rise to £20m with bonuses. Spurs have also negotiated a 20 per cent sell-on clause and matching rights into the transfer agreement.

Real get their Diomande

Real Madrid have reached an agreement with RB Leipzig to sign one-time Liverpool target Yan Diomande on a seven-year contract.

Real are paying a guaranteed fee of £107million for the 19-year-old, with the total deal worth up to £120m.

Yan Diomande - who was a target for Liverpool earlier this summer - has joined Real Madrid

Liverpool had an offer worth £85m rejected earlier in the window while PSG also tried to sign the Ivory Coast international. Diomande scored 13 goals and provided 10 assists in 36 appearances last season.

Liverpool are currently working to add PSG pair Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye.

Nestory time at Sporting

Sporting Lisbon have agreed a deal worth around £17m for Watford forward Nestory Irankunda.

Bayern Munich have a 40 per cent sell-on clause for the Australia international and will be due around £7m.

Diomande in doubt

Ousmane Diomande's move to Nottingham Forest has hit a major snag with the deal now far from certain.

Forest had been close to agreeing a fee of about £35m with Sporting Lisbon for the centre-back but Daily Mail Sport understands talks have hit the buffers.

Oliver Glasner had made the centre-back his top target - as he did at Crystal Palace last summer, which also proved unsuccessful.

Ousmane Diomande's move to Nottingham Forest is understood to have hit a snag

It now remains to be seen if the transfer can be revived in the remaining days of the window.

TOM COLLOMOSSE

Trafford completes Leeds switch

James Trafford has completed a move from Manchester City to Leeds in a deal that could reach £45m.

Trafford becomes the most expensive English goalkeeper of all time after the clubs struck an agreement on £40m plus £5m in add-ons.

Man City are closing on agreement with Marseille for goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli.

The 34-year-old will cost around £2.9million and will replace Trafford.

The deal will allow Lucas Perri to move from Leeds to Torino. The Italians are waiting for Perri to recover from a small injury which kept him out of Leeds' last two pre-season games before finalising the move.

Leeds have a list of around five goalkeepers as they plot their search for Trafford's deputy.

They have Alex Cairns but want another to cover Perri's departure too.

San Lorenzo's Paraguay international Orlando Gill is one but they are yet to make an offer.

Dykes snubs Charlton for Millwall

Scotland striker Lyndon Dykes has agreed a one-year deal with Millwall.

The 30-year-old has completed a medical and is finalising his move.

Dykes rejected a longer term offer from Charlton Athletic, where he spent the second half of last season, as he looks to help Millwall earn promotion.

Scotland forward Lyndon Dykes is set to join Millwall

Villa and Toon keep tabs on defender

Racing Santander defender Jorge Salinas is attracting attention from Aston Villa and Newcastle United.

The 19-year-old can play left back and centre back and has also been watched by Barcelona and Manchester United scouts.

Some of the clubs view him as a player for the future while others are considering a bid this month.

Bruno heads to the capital

Bruno Guimaraes is understood to be in London to finalise his £75million move to Arsenal.

The 28-year-old left Newcastle's pre-season camp on Wednesday after a fee of £75m was agreed with Arsenal. Newcastle are continuing to work on a replacement.

Napoli have enquired about striker Gabriel Jesus at Arsenal.

Bruno Guimaraes is in London to complete his move from Newcastle to Arsenal

Gunners keep tabs on the next Kvaratskhelia

Arsenal scouts were at Larne's Europa League qualifier against Iberia 1999 on Tuesday.

They were understood to be running the rule over the Georgian side's attacking midfielder Andria Bartishvili.

The exciting 17-year-old has been on Arsenal's radar for a number of months and has been compared in style to compatriot Khvicha Kvaratskhelia at Paris St Germain.

Indeed, the French side are also understood to be among his admirers as well as clubs in Italy.

Bartishvili is on loan at Iberia from Kolkheti 1913, however, he is expected to be sold in the coming days as interest intensifies.

Hammers confirm Veltman

West Ham have confirmed the signing of former Brighton defender Joel Veltman.

The Dutch defender has signed a one-year contract with an option for a second year.

'I'm delighted to have signed, and I can't wait to get started,' said Veltman. 'The project here really excites me.'

'I spoke to Nuno [Espírito Santo], as well as my family and my agent, and everything added up. We know that West Ham need to be in the Premier League, and for sure that is our goal for the season.

'I think I bring my experience, my winning mentality and togetherness. I bring leadership - I've been the captain at Ajax, and I enjoy talking to my teammates and using my experience to help the squad.

'I'm just so excited to give everything, to meet my new teammates and to see all the supporters too.'

West Ham are also prepared to break the Championship transfer record of £17.5m to sign Troy Parrott from AZ Alkmaar. Talks have opened between the clubs.

Talks for Spurs winger Manor Solomon are currently off over bonus payments.

West Ham have announced the signing of Brighton defender Joel Veltman

JOEL VELTMAN STATS Played 24 Premier League matches in 25-26, but only started nine and played 1050 minutes Scored once last season - against West Ham (2-2 draw at London Stadium to salvage a point for Brighton) Across the Premier League season, Veltman made a total of 99 defensive contributions Won 75 duels (67% success rate) Won 20 aerial duels (62.5% success rate) 31 tackles 18 interceptions Six shots blocked 10 fouls committed 40 recoveries 44 clearances Five yellow cards Started all four cup matches he played in (two in Carabao Cup, two in FA Cup) *By Isabelle Martin

Barca rival Real Madrid's interest in Rodri

Barcelona have finally made their interest in Manchester City midfielder Rodri official to rival Real Madrid for his signature.

Rodri wants to return to Spain but Manchester City have been waiting for other clubs to declare their interest to get the optimum price for the 30-year-old.

Barcelona have finally expressed their interest in Manchester City and Spain midfielder Rodri

They have made a new contract offer to the Spain captain who has one year left but are aware of his desire to explore a move back.

Rodri was keen on a move to Madrid but equally is understood to be open to joining Barca's project where eight of the national team are in the current squad.

Sanchez joins Cherries

Bournemouth have announced the signing of right-back Juanlu Sanchez, 22, from Sevilla in a deal worth £11.2m.

Man United's newest signing

Man United have signed 18-year-old midfielder Cristian Orozco from Colombian side Fortaleza CEIF for their U21s.

Boro agree deal for Phillips

Tottenham and Middlesbrough have agreed a £7million deal plus add ons for centre back Ashley Phillips.

The 21-year-old's former club Blackburn are due a sell on percentage.

A central defender became Boro's priority after Dael Fry's decision to leave for Birmingham at the end of his contract.

Munoz reports for duty

Spain winger Victor Munoz reported to Liverpool training for the first time yesterday following his £34.5million move from Osasuna.

Munoz moved to Los Rojillos last summer from Real Madrid, for whom he made four appearances after graduating from their youth set-up having previously been with the academy of his hometown club, Barcelona.

Munoz was the first new addition after the arrival of head coach Andoni Iraola.

Victor Munoz with agents Juanma Lopez and Andy Bara from Niagara Sports

And Chambers could head to Championship

Liverpool left-back Luke Chambers is attracting interest from QPR, Blackburn Rovers and others.

The 22-year-old has impressed during Liverpool's pre-season and has drawn several enquiries including another from a European club and one more Championship side.

The former England U20 international has previously been on loan at Kilmarnock, Wigan Athletic and Charlton Athletic.

Saints teen heads to Italy

Southampton winger Jay Robinson arrived in Milan's Linate airport at 9pm last night ahead of sealing his loan move to newly-promoted Serie A side Monza.

The 19-year-old, who made his Premier League debut in 2025, made 23 appearances in the Championship last season but his campaign was hindered by a quad injury.

The teenager, who has also represented England at every age group from U16s up to the U19s, is hoping to gain regular game time in Italy's top flight.

Southampton winger Jay Robinson is set to seal a loan move to Serie A club Monza

Celtic have made a £6m bid for Real Oviedo’s Egyptian winger Haissem Hassan. The fee could rise to £9m if all bonuses are achieved.

Ipswich Town are in advanced talks with Fulham over the signing of midfielder Sasa Lukic. The 29-year-old could have a medical today at Ipswich where Miami Heat basketball star Udonis Haslem has announced he is a minority owner.

Fulham have failed with a bid for Rennes centre-back Abdelhamid Ait Boudlal.

Ipswich remain in talks with Strasbourg over the signing of Julio Enciso.

Leicester have signed Ipswich winger Wes Burns. The 31-year-old has joined on a three-year deal. Leicester are also in talks for forward Admir Bristric from Olimpija Ljubljana.

Sports.title: Troy Williamson reveals secret weapon for Callum Simpson rematch
Sports.content:
Troy Williamson reveals secret weapon for Callum Simpson rematch

Williamson dropped his rival four times last December before stopping him to become British, Commonwealth and European super-middleweight champion

View 2 Images Callum Simpson is knocked out by Troy Williamson

‌



Troy Williamson is confident he can KO Callum Simpson for a second and final time - thanks to his new herbal super power.

‌



Williamson dropped his rival four times last December before stopping him to become British, Commonwealth and European super-middleweight champion. Williamson saw no need for a second fight but Simpson activated his rematch clause and the pair will cross paths again in Leeds on Saturday night.

‌



And the Darlington man believes his new Tongkat Ali supplement - derived from an Asian plant - has given him added knockout strength. "It's just not just my power; my drive, my focus, my energy have all improved," the ten percent athlete said. "But most importantly my strength has increased. The Tongkat Ali is the best supplement on the market. Obviously as a professional athlete, everything needs to be tested. But everything I take from Ten Percent Club is Informed-Sport tested, which is a bonus."

Anthony Joshua sets out demands to move Tyson Fury fight to New York READ MORE :

Williamson admits he was surprised when Simpson demanded a rematch - but is relishing the chance to repeat his last performance. "I was surprised they asked for a rematch," he added. "But Callum's a fighter at the end of the day. His ego was damaged and he'll obviously want to try and get that revenge. I can see why he wants to fight again, but really, his team, his coach, his manager, even his promoter, should have told him it's time to move on.

Article continues below

"They've made a bad decision activating the rematch because when I knock him out again, he's got going to be coming off two back-to-back knockout losses and that's going to be hard to come back from. I want to put it all to bed, put everything behind me and move on towards bigger and better things."

Troy Williamson was speaking on behalf of Ten Percent Club, one of the leading supplementation brands in professional sports. Ten Percent Club work with several professional footballers and athletes, including the likes of Eddie Hearn and Matchroom Boxing. Several other footballers have endorsed the products, including Sam Johnstone, Matty Cash, Beth Mead and Maya Le Tissier . For more information, visit: https://www.tenpercentclub.net/

Sports.title: Michael Carrick's telling response after being told to sell eight players by Man Utd hero
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick's telling response after being told to sell eight players by Man Utd hero

Manchester United boss Michael Carrick has not yet followed transfer instructions previously laid out by Paul Scholes

View 4 Images Manchester United boss Michael Carrick was told by a former team-mate to sell some players (Image: Getty)

Michael Carrick has not sanctioned any major sales so far this summer at Manchester United. This is despite United hero Paul Scholes recommending eight stars be sold.

‌



Carrick is currently taking charge of his first pre-season and there are just a few weeks until the Premier League returns. With only three first-team signings made so far in Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Karl Darlow, more additions are expected.

‌



However, there has yet to be a major exit from the club, aside from Casemiro's departure. In April, Scholes was asked for a series of United stars who were surplus to requirements and of the eight players he listed, only one appears set to leave as things stand.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

7 Man Utd players face uncertain futures as part of huge summer overhaul of squad READ MORE :

Jadon Sancho's Man Utd decline and manager trend leaves unwanted star in awkward spot READ MORE :

Joshua Zirkzee was among the players that Scholes believed should be sold and the former Bologna forward is edging closer to a return to Italy. La Gazzetta dello Sport claims that Zirkzee is willing to join Juventus, who are pursuing a loan arrangement with an option to buy.

View 4 Images Zirkzee could be on the move soon (Image: Getty)

‌



Scholes and Carrick spent seven seasons together in United's midfield during their playing days. However, whilst the pundit's suggestion to move on Zirkzee may materialise, the other seven stars Scholes mentioned could all remain part of United's squad next term, with Carrick's response clear.

The 51-year-old stressed the importance of United revamping their defence. Speaking on The Good, The Bad and The Football podcast, Scholes said of Leny Yoro: "I think he's struggled, me. I think there's something in there, I think he needs a bit of time, but if you had to make a choice now, I'd probably sell him."

He also argued that the shift away from ex-boss Ruben Amorim's three-at-the-back system would have implications for Noussair Mazraoui. Mazraoui has been linked with a departure this summer, though he remains part of Carrick's side. Highly-rated defender Yoro has also expressed a desire to make his mark at United next season.

‌



View 4 Images Yoro was a surprise inclusion (Image: Getty)

Every subscription now comes with 135 channels alongside free subscriptions to HBO Max, Netflix, Disney+, discovery+ and Hayu.

Turning to midfield, Scholes felt Manuel Ugarte would depart and the Uruguayan was linked with a move before picking up an injury at the World Cup. Mason Mount also featured on Scholes' eight-man list, though the England international has caught the eye during pre-season.

‌



Additionally, Scholes felt the moment had arrived to say goodbye to Harry Maguire, who continues to have a key role at United. He said: "I'm thinking about a Manchester United team you want to win the league and the Champions League and that's where United should be aiming. I'm not sure you'd do that with Maguire."

Elsewhere, United have held an interest in Newcastle United full-back Lewis Hall in the transfer window. Focusing on the left-back position, Scholes previously urged the club to offload long-serving Luke Shaw due to doubts about his reliability, despite him having featured in every Premier League fixture last season. He was equally prepared to let Patrick Dorgu leave.

View 4 Images Mount, Shaw and Maguire were three of the players that Scholes named (Image: Getty)

Article continues below

Scholes said on Dorgu: "They brought him in as a wing-back and he's not really played much there. I'd probably sell. I'm not sure what position he is. Again, if you keep him then he's just a squad player."

Overall, of the eight players Scholes recommended be sold, only Zirkzee appears set for an imminent exit. There has been little speculation regarding the remaining seven of Yoro, Mazraoui, Shaw, Dorgu, Mount, Ugarte and Maguire.

Sports.title: Arsenal's 10 highest Premier League sales – and why it speaks volumes for Andrea Berta
Sports.content:
Arsenal's 10 highest Premier League sales – and why it speaks volumes for Andrea Berta

Arsenal sporting director Andrea Berta has plenty on his plate as the Premier League champions bid to kick on this summer

View 4 Images Andrea Berta has a lot on his plate as Arsenal's sporting director (Image: Getty)

Arsenal's sporting director Andrea Berta has overseen some important signings since joining the club, with more expected to follow. But sales have been a challenge for the Gunners, with the problem persisting long before the Italian took up the role.

‌



The north London side's record sale still sits at just £35million. To put that into context, only three of the other 19 Premier League sides - Sunderland, Hull and Coventry - have lower records. Arsenal simply aren't selling well.

‌



A total of three sales this summer have raised less than £40m combined, with Karl Hein, Jakub Kiwior and Leandro Trossard completing permanent exits. Arsenal have already paid in the region of £34m for both Piero Hincapie and Christos Tzolis, whilst the anticipated move for Bruno Guimaraes will see them more than double their outlay.

‌



When it comes to record sales, it's telling that the top four spots are occupied by transfers from the Arsene Wenger era, and the club simply aren't keeping up with the big-money exits that clubs like Chelsea and Manchester City sanction. Here are their 10 most lucrative offloadings, in reverse order, per Transfermarkt figures.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Two Champions League rule changes announced by UEFA ahead of new season READ MORE :

Ex-Arsenal star makes winning return to English football with League Two club READ MORE :

10. Joe Willock (£25.2m)

Willock's move to Newcastle was a case of striking whilst the iron was hot. The midfielder scored eight goals during a loan spell at St James' Park, driving up his value and convincing Arsenal to cash in.

‌



The England Under-21 international hasn't yet matched that goal tally across more than 100 games as a permanent Newcastle player, though his role became far less attacking under Eddie Howe. He was used sparingly last term, struggling to displace Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali.

9. Eddie Nketiah (£25.4m)

Another recent sale, Nketiah demonstrated Premier League pedigree in an Arsenal shirt when he scored a hat-trick against Sheffield United in 2023. Months later, Crystal Palace took the plunge with a big-money bid and the striker - battling with the likes of Kai Havertz and Gabriel Jesus for opportunities - decided to try his luck elsewhere.

View 4 Images Nketiah is about to embark on his third season at Crystal Palace (Image: Getty)

‌



Get Arsenal's new 2026/27 home kit This article contains affiliate links, we will receive a commission on any sales we generate from it. Learn more £85 Fanatics Buy Now on Fanatics Product Description Arsenal have launched their new home kit for the 2026/27 season, said to incorporate classic Arsenal design features that tie into the club's heritage.

The Eagles could end up paying even more for the England international if conditions for add-ons are met. However, his second season at Selhurst Park was cut short by injury and he will hope for a fresh start under new boss Pierre Sage.

8. Folarin Balogun (£25.7m)

Balogun, like Nketiah, moved in search of more regular first-team football. Again, Arsenal got good money for a fringe player when he followed up a 21-goal Ligue 1 season at Reims with a move to their rivals Monaco.

‌



The United States international top-scored for his club last term and thrived for his country at the World Cup. There's no guarantee he would have developed at the same speed in North London, though.

7. Alex Iwobi (£26m)

Academy graduate Iwobi grew into his role at Arsenal, scoring in the 2019 Europa League final defeat to Chelsea and playing 100 league games for the Gunners. But the arrival of Nicolas Pepe meant he was considered disposable.

Marco Silva signed the Nigerian international for Everton but was gone within months in a tough first season. Things have gone better for Iwobi after a reunion with Silva at Fulham, where he has thrived in a deeper midfield role than the one he occupied at his boyhood club.

‌



6. Robin van Persie (£26.3m)

View 4 Images Van Persie's United move was one of 2012's most talked-about transfers (Image: Getty)

The £26m paid by Manchester United for Van Persie in 2012 was worth a great deal more then than now. Still, it's telling that a deal from more than a decade ago is one of the top 10 on this list. And it's not the only one.

The Dutch striker's move was hugely dramatic at the time, with plenty of fans turning on a former favourite. United will have considered the move a success after his goals brought an immediate league title but the following two years were less fruitful for player and club and he left for Fenerbahce in 2015.

‌



5. Emile Smith Rowe (£27.2m)

Academy graduate Smith Rowe made a fast start as a teenager but found himself overtaken in the pecking order during Mikel Arteta's tenure. He left for Fulham in 2024, with Mikel Merino brought in by Arteta just weeks later.

The three-cap England international has remained a solid presence in Fulham's midfield, featuring in 71 of 76 available league matches. However, he has not looked close to a Three Lions recall, nearly four years on from his most recent cap.

‌



4. Cesc Fabregas (£29.1m)

Your eyes don't deceive you. That's a 2011 sale in the top five - by way of comparison, Chelsea have sold 20 players for more money since then, give or take the margin of error for conversions between Euros and Pounds.

It was one of two big-money moves for Fabregas in his career, with the Spaniard also joining Chelsea in 2014 for a similar amount to the Barcelona deal after Arsenal opted against bringing him back. He won two Premier League titles with the Blues and has now made an impressive start to his managerial career with Como.

3. Alexis Sanchez (£29.1m)

You might not even want to count this one, given the fact that it came as part of an effective swap deal. We're leaving it in just to emphasise the task facing Berta as he looks to succeed where his predecessors struggled.

‌



Sanchez moved to United in 2018, with Henrikh Mkhitaryan joining Arsenal from the Red Devils. The Londoners came out of the deal a little better but neither club had huge success from the arrangement.

2. Nicolas Anelka (£30m)

Those tricky conversion fees mean reports vary for how much Anelka went for in Pounds. Even so, it says a lot that a sale from 1999 features on this list.

View 4 Images Anelka joined Real Madrid more than a quarter of a century ago (Image: Getty)

‌



Anelka was an example of Arsenal turning a huge profit on a player they signed for less than £1m from Paris Saint-Germain. He would go on to make more than 500 career league appearances across several countries and also played for France at the World Cup and European Championships.

1. Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain (£35m)

Arsenal's record sale remains the £35m they received when Oxlade-Chamberlain joined Liverpool in 2017. The England international became a Premier League and Champions League winner during his time at Anfield but was plagued by injury.

Despite spending six years as a Liverpool player, he made just 103 league appearances. He left for Besiktas on a free transfer in 2023 and is now at Celtic.

Sports.title: Liverpool were linked with World Cup winner and £53m star for ages but never signed them
Sports.content:
Liverpool were linked with World Cup winner and £53m star for ages but never signed them

Transfer sagas spanning years is a situation Liverpool know a thing or two about

View 5 Images Nabil Fekir's failed move to Liverpool was shrouded in controversy (Image: NurPhoto/PA Images)

Few things ignite the football world quite like a transfer saga, and Liverpool have certainly starred in their fair share over the years. There's been plenty of wins in the market for the Reds, such as their past acquisitions of Mohamed Salah and Sadio Mane, or besting Bayern Munich to the signing of Florian Wirtz last summer.

‌



High-stakes moves trigger an intense mix of fan hype and deadline-day anxiety, but the tension usually dissolves the second a player hits the pitch in red. Every so often, however, years of following a particular target and intense negotiations end in heartbreak.

‌



From controversial collapses of deals to players simply opting for another club, Mirror Football takes a look at five targets Liverpool failed to drag across the finish line - and why the deals fell apart.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Nabil Fekir

Arguably the most infamous collapsed transfer in recent Liverpool history, the breakdown of Nabil Fekir's switch to Anfield in 2018 sparked accusations of dishonesty and family drama. The Frenchman had undergone a medical ahead of his £53million transfer from Lyon and agreed personal terms before the Reds pulled out of the deal.

Liverpool weigh up hijacking £60m Arsenal transfer to appease desperate Andoni Iraola READ MORE :

Man Utd forced to fork out millions as Marcus Rashford benefits from contract loophole READ MORE :

The attacking midfielder had even posed for promotional photographs with the club, who insisted their decision to abandon the deal was down to a knee cartilage issue. Fekir dismissed the Reds' explanation as a lie and rejected claims from his then-agent, Jean-Pierre Bernes, who suggested that the Frenchman's brother-in-law tried to secure a cut from the transfer.

‌



"Lots of lies were told, and they affected me," Fekir told L'Equipe in 2019. "Especially those told about my family. It hurt them and me. Especially when you know that what's being told is false.

"What was said is not the truth. My knee is good - I had a quick medical check at Clairefontaine [the headquarters of France's national team] - my knee wasn't even mentioned. If my knee had been in such a bad state, would [then-Lyon chairman Jean-Michel Aulas] have made [a sufficient offer to keep the player]?"

Gareth Barry

View 5 Images Gareth Barry was wanted twice by Rafael Benitez (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

‌



Countdown to Kickoff: The Ultimate 26/27 Sky Sports Bundle This article contains affiliate links, we will receive a commission on any sales we generate from it. Learn more £44 Sky Get the deal here Product Description Sky's Ultimate TV and Sky Sports bundle includes at least 215 live Premier League clashes across the 2026/27 season with more than 1,400 live games across the EFL and beyond, plus F1, golf and darts. Every subscription now comes with 135 channels alongside free subscriptions to HBO Max, Netflix, Disney+, discovery+ and Hayu.

Liverpool's pursuit of Gareth Barry began in the summer of 2008. A vital component of Aston Villa's midfield engine room, Rafael Benitez had identified the Englishman as the ideal replacement for Xabi Alonso, who had endured an injury-disrupted campaign throughout 2007/08.

Yet the Reds fell short of Villa's £18m valuation for their skipper, forcing Barry to remain at the Midlands club. Liverpool returned to the negotiating table twelve months on, with their persistent interest in the midfielder ultimately prompting Alonso to seal a switch to Real Madrid.

‌



It proved a double setback for Benitez as Barry chose Manchester City over Anfield. Reflecting on his decision to snub Liverpool, Barry told Birmingham Live's Claret and Blue podcast: "Something appealed to me more about Man City than Liverpool at the time. Liverpool had won the Champions League not so long ago and Man City hadn't won a trophy for many years, but I went with that route."

Arda Turan

View 5 Images Arda Turan was linked to the Reds during his time at Galatasaray and Atletico Madrid (Image: Jean Catuffe/Getty Images)

Arda Turan was repeatedly linked with a switch to Liverpool over a six-year period between 2009 and 2015. The speculation started during his stint at Galatasaray, but it was Atletico Madrid who secured his services in 2011.

‌



His impressive four-year spell in the Spanish capital, which featured their La Liga triumph in 2014, didn't halt talk of his possible arrival on Merseyside, according to AS. It was claimed the Turkish star grew up watching Liverpool and his father supported the club.

Despite his family's reported affection for the Reds, Turan never turned out for the club and instead moved to Barcelona in 2015, before hanging up his boots in 2022 with Galatasaray.

Simao Sabrosa

We're turning back the clock with Simao Sabrosa. A prominent figure in Portuguese football during the 2000s, the former forward came within touching distance of joining the Reds in the summer of 2005 before Benfica pulled out of the arrangement.

‌



A reported £10m deal had been struck between the two clubs, with Simao even leaving Portugal's training camp to undergo a medical. The 46-year-old opened up about the collapsed transfer in 2022, when speaking to Liverpoolfc.com.

He recounted: "At that time I'm in the national team, three or four days until the end [of the window]. I received a call at like five o'clock in the morning, 'You need to come, we go to Liverpool.'

View 5 Images Simao Sabrosa was inches away from becoming a Liverpool player (Image: AFP/Getty Images)

‌



"I go to [Luiz Felipe] Scolari and the director of the national team to give me permission to go out. When I go to the office of my agent, in that moment the president of Benfica called and said, 'We don't have a deal, you don't have permission to fly, so you need to stay.'

"It's strange because I thought it was done. But when the president went home, he called again and said, 'It's impossible to fly to Liverpool and get a new contract with Liverpool, so you need to stay. Because if you sign for Liverpool, Benfica fans will be angry [with me].' At that time I said, 'OK, I stay.'

"The office of my agent is near the airport and the agent gave me some impression, 'Let's go to the airport. When we arrive in Liverpool, maybe the president says yes.' I said, 'No, it's impossible to take the plane and fly to Liverpool.'

‌



"I was representing the national team and if I take this decision, I have a lot of problems with the national team, my club, so I decided to stay." His switch to Atletico Madrid in 2007 did little to silence ongoing speculation of a transfer to Anfield, but nothing advanced as close as it had a year prior.

Julian Draxler

The former Germany international is another footballer familiar to Liverpool supporters. The 32-year-old, who presently features for Qatari outfit Al-Ahli, emerged into the spotlight with boyhood side Schalke in 2011, which is when his enduring connections to Liverpool commenced.

Former Reds manager Brendan Rodgers reportedly made a personal trip to the Veltins-Arena to run the rule over Draxler during a Champions League clash against Basel. However, a deal never came to fruition as the attacking midfielder ultimately joined fellow Bundesliga outfit Wolfsburg in 2015.

‌



View 5 Images Julian Draxler opted to join Paris Saint-Germain (Image: Getty Images)

A switch to Paris Saint-Germain followed two years on, though not before Liverpool had once again registered their interest in the 2014 World Cup winner, this time under Jurgen Klopp. The German tactician was eager to bring compatriot Draxler to Merseyside, but the player chose a move to the French capital instead.

He has since admitted to pondering what might have unfolded had he chosen to test himself in the Premier League. "When I was still very young at Schalke and extended my contract, I could have gone to Arsenal," he told BILD, as quoted by Sport Witness.

Article continues below

"Honestly, I'd be interested to see what would have become of me if I had learned from Arsene Wenger so early. I've also wondered what would have happened if I hadn't gone from Wolfsburg to Paris, but to Jurgen Klopp at Liverpool. I had that opportunity, too. Nevertheless, I'm happy. I'm at peace with my decisions."

Sports.title: Man Utd dream attack as Marcus Rashford exits plus free agent striker and World Cup star join
Sports.content:
Man Utd dream attack as Marcus Rashford exits plus free agent striker and World Cup star join

Manchester United continue their hard work in the summer transfer window with more players on the way

View 4 Images Marcus Rashford's Manchester United future is still up in the air (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Manchester United could offload Marcus Rashford's hefty wages and a struggling striker to make way for more new signings to arrive at Old Trafford. The Red Devils are continuing their activity in the summer transfer window with Michael Carrick building a squad capable of competing across various competitions.

‌



United have spent £83m so far this summer, and have seen some huge salaries drop off the wage bill. Jadon Sancho departed the club as a free agent and Casemiro headed for Inter Miami, both of which freed up some room in the budget.

‌



A £35m move for Youri Tielemans has been completed, with the former Aston Villa midfielder signing a five-year deal at Old Trafford. Andrey Santos also joined from Chelsea for an initial £48m, plus £2m in add-ons to beef up the middle of the park.

‌



Karl Darlow, Kit Margetson and Tynan Thompson have also arrived. However, Carrick will still be eager for more players through the door. Some stars will have to depart to accommodate this, with Rashford's future one of a number up for discussion.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Man Utd closing in on transfer deal after Michael Carrick dropped hint READ MORE :

Joshua Zirkzee is also being linked with a switch to Juventus, though only on a temporary basis. Reinforcements will be required for Carrick to have enough squad depth to compete both at home and in Europe.

Here, Mirror Football has looked at what a dream United attacking lineup could look like this season.

Free agent striker

United signed Zirkzee for £36.5m in 2024 but he has slipped down the pecking order at Old Trafford. The Dutchman has made a few appearances under Carrick but watched on as Benjamin Sesko leapfrogged him to spearhead the attack last season.

‌



Italian newspaper Corriere dello Sport reports that Juventus are closing in on a loan deal for Zirkzee, with boss Luciano Spalletti 'saying yes' to the move. It looks increasingly likely that the former Bologna man will depart this summer, one way or another.

United will likely need reinforcements if that is to happen, although Carrick may not want to disrupt the progress of Sesjo, who impressed towards the back end of last term. This is where the free agency market could prove invaluable. Dusan Vlahovic is one among several forwards who have been linked to Old Trafford – and he could represent the perfect signing for nothing at all.

View 4 Images Dusan Vlahovic represents a cheap but effective option (Image: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images)

‌



The 26-year-old left Juve following the expiry of his deal this summer, having netted 68 goals in 168 outings. He has amassed 140 club goals throughout his career.

Vlahovic boasts a considerable European pedigree but could provide adequate cover for Sesko, who has impressed under Carrick's guidance. Securing a free agent would demonstrate the manager's faith in the Slovenian forward while allowing him to develop through competition with the Serbia international.

Vlahovic would additionally offer greater flexibility in attack, enabling Carrick to rest Sesko and maintain squad fitness throughout a demanding campaign.

‌

Rashford decision

Rashford's situation at United continues to hang in the balance. At present, the academy product is set to rejoin pre-season preparations with the club following the collapse of a Barcelona switch.

He remains heavily linked with a move away from the club, including in recent days to Fenerbahce. Earlier in the window, however, it was thought that Rashford wouldn't be keen on a move to Turkey, which could put the skids on any potential move before it has even gotten going. Tottenham have also registered their interest, and with several weeks remaining before the transfer window shuts, whether Rashford's future lies at Old Trafford or beyond remains very much unresolved.

‌



View 4 Images Iliman Ndiaye's experience would be greatly welcomed at Old Trafford (Image: Vince Mignott/MB Media/Getty Images)

Should he depart permanently, Iliman Ndiaye could prove an ideal replacement, bringing with him solid Premier League pedigree. The 26-year-old has racked up 20 goal contributions across 70 appearances for Everton and is strongly linked with a move to United.

It is understood that the Toffees will hold out for around £70m for the left-winger, who is also attracting attention from Saudi Pro League outfit Al-Hilal.

‌



United's dream attack

View 4 Images United's attacking is shaping up quite nicely (Image: Paul ELLIS / AFP via Getty Images)

With Benjamin Sesko currently leading the line, Vlahovic could be the ideal option for United to call upon when needed. With two top-quality strikers at their disposal, focus would then shift to the wide positions.

Amad and Bryan Mbeumo have the right flank well covered, with the latter likely to get the nod to start. Ndiaye would fit seamlessly on the left, and there is always the option to utilise Patrick Dorgu in a more advanced role after impressing last season.

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Bradley Barcola price tag slashed as star 'says yes' to PSG transfer
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Bradley Barcola price tag slashed as star 'says yes' to PSG transfer

The Reds have been quoted a new price tag for Bradley Barcola as the club's transfer activity heats up

View 3 Images Bradley Barcola is significantly valued by PSG (Image: Rob Newell - CameraSport, CameraSport via Getty Images)

Liverpool will be eager to ramp up their transfer business as the new Premier League season edges closer. The Reds will face Monaco in a friendly at Anfield this weekend, having recently completed a pre-season tour of the USA.

‌



The Anfield outfit finally welcomed new signing Victor Munoz to the club this week, after he signed from Osasuna earlier in the summer. The Spanish winger and French centre-back Jeremy Jacquet are the only new faces at the Reds so far this pre-season, with Liverpool in need of more reinforcements.

‌



Much has been made of the club's chase of Paris Saint-Germain winger Bradley Barcola, with the European champions said to be demanding a huge fee from the Reds. Today's news sees PSG's latest stance on Barcola's price tag emerge, while a World Cup star reportedly agrees to a move to Paris.

‌



PSG set Bradley Barcola terms

PSG are reportedly insisting on raking in a staggering £128million for Barcola this summer, according to L'Equipe. The substantial price tag is believed to be the reason a transfer to Liverpool has failed to materialise so far, but it is less than the initial £145m that the French side were originally quoted as wanting for the player.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Jamie Carragher criticises Mohamed Salah's Turkey move after Liverpool exit READ MORE :

Liverpool exploring Ibrahim Mbaye transfer as PSG star's stance on move emerges READ MORE :

It's believed that the Reds would prefer to pay around £103m for the winger with Barcola said to be open to the move. The BBC say Liverpool are preparing to change their stance and up their offer to get the deal over the line, while L'Equipe says that, while the two clubs are "very far apart", the transfer is expected to be sealed before the window closes.

‌



The fee for Barcola has some concerned. Ex-Anfield star Michael Owen believes the Reds will have to be realistic when it comes to shelling out such cash for the French winger.

View 3 Images Liverpool's interest in Bradley Barcola remains strong (Image: Getty Images)

Owen told the ECHO, via Casino.org: "Barcola, he's obviously the big name on everybody's lips. It sounds like he might be available. It sounds like he's going to be expensive, though - but they're going to have to make some form of statement signing, of course. You know, it used to be Salah, and [Sadio] Mane and [Luis] Diaz.

"Obviously [Barcola has] played at the highest level, but, yeah, at some point you've got to say no, haven't you? If it gets to £145m, wow, that's eye-watering."

Ferran Torres 'says yes' to transfer

Barcelona star Ferran Torres has reportedly agreed to join PSG this summer in a move that could grease the wheels for Barcola to join Liverpool. The Spanish World Cup winner is said to be mulling over his future while on holiday after his exploits at the tournament this summer.

‌



That decision has been made according to Spanish outlet Sport, with Torres giving the green light to PSG boss Luis Enrique for a switch. The forward has made no secret of his openness to leaving Barca in recent interviews.

"In the world of football, you never know," Torres said when questioned about a possible departure from the Catalan giants this summer.

View 3 Images Ferran Torres netted the winner in the World Cup final (Image: FRANCK FIFE / AFP via Getty Images)

‌



In July, Sport reported that Enrique himself intervened to bring the former Manchester City star to Paris. Barcelona have stated they would sell for a generous offer but are happy to keep the forward this summer.

PSG are now set to make an offer for Torres' transfer, with the desire to finalise a move before the Spanish international's return next week following the World Cup. The capture of Torres would represent another building block as PSG look to restructure their attack this summer.

Monaco winger Maghnes Akliouche is reportedly close to joining while they are also working on a deal to sign Mika Godts, the Belgian forward from Ajax. If those deals go through, it could potentially lay the groundwork for Barcola to depart for the Reds and put to bed the long-running transfer saga.

Sports.title: Man Utd news: Marcus Rashford clause emerges as Barcelona transfer swoop causes issues
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Marcus Rashford clause emerges as Barcelona transfer swoop causes issues

There's still plenty of business to be done in the transfer window at Manchester United with further high-profile arrivals and exits on the cards

View 3 Images Michael Carrick is on his first pre-season tour as Manchester United boss (Image: Getty)

Manchester United have been reasonably busy in the transfer market - but there could still be plenty more to come before the deadline. With Michael Carrick preparing for his first full season in charge, his side remain active on several high-profile fronts.

‌



Their midfield has already been strengthened by the arrivals of Andrey Santos from Chelsea in a £50million deal and Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa for £35m. Even so, United are still believed to be in the market for at least one more man in the centre of the park.

‌



Attention will also soon turn to trimming the squad. Most notably, there's the question of what to do with Marcus Rashford, who is currently in limbo after being denied a move to Barcelona.

‌



With less than a month remaining before the transfer window closes and negotiations gathering pace across Europe, Mirror Football takes a look at the latest Manchester United transfer headlines.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Marcus Rashford primed for Ruben Amorim reunion after Man Utd transfer twist READ MORE :

Man Utd overhaul accelerates with another transfer agreed after booking medical READ MORE :

Rashford contract clause emerges

United's efforts to move Rashford on this summer have been handed an added sense of urgency after details of a lucrative clause in his contract came to light. The 28-year-old currently earns an estimated £300,000 a week at Old Trafford, but that figure is now set to rise after United secured a return to the Champions League.

‌



View 3 Images Rashford is set for a seven-figure bonus on top of his hefty United wages if he stays put (Image: Getty)

Before Sir Jim Ratcliffe overhauled the club's wage structure, United players were entitled to an automatic 25 per cent pay rise if the club qualified for Europe's premier competition. That bonus scheme was scrapped in 2024, but existing contracts signed beforehand - including those of Rashford and Mason Mount - still contain the clause.

With Rashford already earning roughly £16m a year, his salary is expected to increase by around £4m following United's Champions League qualification. It only strengthens the club's desire to find a buyer before the transfer window closes.

‌



For much of the summer, a permanent move to Barcelona appeared the most likely outcome after his loan spell in Catalonia. However, the Spanish champions' £70m signing of Anthony Gordon looks to have ended that possibility. With just over three weeks remaining in the window, both player and club are running out of time to resolve his future.

Barcelona swoop causes problem for Man Utd

Barcelona's surprise move for Manchester City midfielder Rodri could have a significant knock-on effect on United's transfer plans. Real Madrid had appeared to be leading the race for the Spain captain, whose contract at the Etihad Stadium has less than a year left. Jose Mourinho's side were reportedly willing to pay upwards of £60m for the 30-year-old and City are open to cashing in.

View 3 Images Rodri is being chased by Spain's two biggest clubs (Image: Getty)

Article continues below

For United, a move to the Bernabeu would be the ideal outcome. Rodri's arrival could pave the way for Aurelien Tchouameni to leave, since the club would need to free up space in midfield and raise funds to keep their finances in check. The France international remains high on United's wishlist.

But convincing Real Madrid to part with him looks highly is they lose out on a midfielder of Rodri's calibre. Barcelona's interest has now complicated the equation. Should the Catalan giants win the race for Rodri, Real Madrid would have little reason to entertain offers for Tchouameni - dealing a major blow to United's hopes of pulling off a late midfield coup.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Vinicius Jr agreement, Ezri Konsa twist, new Declan Rice issue
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Vinicius Jr agreement, Ezri Konsa twist, new Declan Rice issue

Arsenal are continuing their hard work in the summer transfer window after missing out on numerous targets

View 4 Images Vinicius Junior has made his decision (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

Arsenal are shifting their focus to other transfer targets as Real Madrid close in on a new deal for Vinicius Jr. Mikel Arteta was keen to bring the Brazilian winger to the Emirates Stadium but it is increasingly likely that he will remain in Spain.

‌



The Gunners are close to completing a transfer of their own with a £75million bid accepted for Newcastle's Bruno Guimaraes. The midfielder has reportedly completed his medical and will sign a four-year deal in north London.

‌



Christos Tzolis, Illan Meslier and Piero Hincapie have already joined Arsenal for a combined £68.5m. Riccardo Calafiori has insisted his team must continue to add high-quality stars to their ranks as he targets more silverware.

‌



Mikel Arteta gives blunt response to Bruno Guimaraes question after Newcastle transfer agreed READ MORE :

The defender told Sky Sports: "Of course we are on that level now, we are on top. We want to win the league again and we want to be even better than last season, if we can, so we need those kind of players, I think."

Here, Mirror Football has the latest coming out of the red side of north London.

‌



Vinicius Jr agreement

View 4 Images Vini Jr is looking increasingly likely to remain in Spain (Image: Antonio Villalba/Real Madrid via Getty Images)

Reports claim that Real are close to agreeing an extension for Vini Jr, putting any plans of Arteta securing the winger to bed. Fabrizio Romano states that the verbal agreement is nearly finalised, with the 26-year-old giving "the green light" to move forward with a new long-term deal.

Real manager Jose Mourinho has reportedly pushed for Vini to stay, stating that he was ready to welcome the winger back into the fold. Speaking ahead of the Brazilian's return to pre-season training, Mourinho said: "I’m concerned about not having everyone, and I would like to have three weeks of work with the others. It’s not possible.

‌



"On Monday, Vini Jr, Brahim, and Bernardo will arrive. Little by little, until the boys who played in the World Cup semifinals and final arrive, with the final being only Cucurella."

Ezri Konsa twist

View 4 Images Ezri Konsa has a few Premier League sides to choose from (Image: Neville Williams/Aston Villa FC via Getty Images)

Liverpool are threatening to rival Arsenal for Aston Villa's Ezri Konsa thanks to their major defensive crisis. Joe Gomez was injured during pre-season with Jeremy Jacquet yet to feature and Virgil van Dijk still on a break after the World Cup.

‌



The Gunners registered an interest in Konsa following William Saliba's back injury at the World Cup, but Villa's £60m price tag is thought to be above what they are willing to pay. The 28-year-old is a Premier League veteran and with two years left on his deal, he could be a great addition to either Liverpool or Arsenal.

Discussing the Reds' depth issues in defence, Andoni Iraola said: "With the centre-back, with the right-back situation, in terms of defensive depth, we are, I think, very thin right now so I think it's a solution that we are trying to find, yes."

‌



Declan Rice issue

View 4 Images Bruno Guimaraes and Declan Rice both operate in the same area (Image: David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Guimaraes' imminent arrival at Arsenal could spell trouble for Declan Rice. The England international could be forced into an unnatural position in the squad.

Rice has been Arsenal's ever-reliable No. 8, making 158 appearances as the club's main playmaker. However, Guimaraes also operates in the creative slot and could shift the 27-year-old to a deeper No. 6 area.

‌



While this may create an issue for the duo, Jay Bothroyd believes they are "up there" with the best midfield pairing in the Premier League.

He said: "I do believe with Rice and Guimaraes, of all of those [Rodri and Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez and Moises Caicedo, Matheus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali], I would probably say, as athletes as well as football players, they would be the best partnership in terms of fitness, physicality, both boxes.

"I think tactically, Rodri and Elliot Anderson might be better, but I think definitely for the way Arsenal play, I wouldn't swap that pairing for any of the others."
