World.title: ‘It’s a thankless job’ — Madugu responds to Super Falcons criticism
World.content:
Super Falcons head coach Justin Madugu has acknowledged that criticism is an unavoidable part of his job, insisting he will continue to focus on improving the team rather than allowing outside noise to affect his decisions.

Madugu spoke after Nigeria’s emphatic victory, reflecting on the expectations surrounding the Super Falcons and the intense scrutiny he and his players have faced throughout the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations.

The coach admitted that he cannot prevent criticism, stressing that football supporters, journalists and other observers are entitled to their opinions and interpretations of the team’s performances.

“I cannot stop criticisms. I cannot, like I keep saying, it’s the nature of the job, you cannot please everybody,” Madugu told reporters in Morocco.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“And like I say, everybody looks at the game from a different perspective and they have their own interpretations. So even when people criticize, I will not blame them for it, they are entitled to their opinion.”

Rather than dismissing criticism outright, Madugu said coaches should be willing to examine negative feedback and identify anything useful that could help the team improve.

“I cannot begin to fire people because we are criticizing. And sometimes even from the negative criticisms, you look at what people are saying. What can you take out of it? If there are positive things that you feel, you can also look at,” he added.

“We’re all human beings, even we as coaches make mistakes. So when you make mistakes and then you realize that, no, I didn’t do this thing well, the onus is on you to own up and then try to get it better the next time.”

Madugu also described coaching as a “thankless job”, pointing out that even players who are left out of the starting XI can be unhappy with his decisions.

“It’s a thankless job. You cannot please everybody, even your players. Anybody that does not play is not happy that I am not playing,” he said.

The Super Falcons coach noted that the scrutiny comes from all directions, with employers, friends, the media and supporters all watching the team’s performances.

“You know, your employers are also there watching. My friends, the press, are also watching. The fans are also watching,” Madugu said.

“So, I mean, it’s something that we must learn to live with as coaches because that’s the nature of the job. And just take the positives out of it, be focused, and then try to do the best that you can.”

Madugu further rejected the idea that he or his coaching staff would deliberately make decisions that could jeopardise the team’s success, insisting that everyone involved benefits when the Super Falcons win.

“We are the principal beneficiaries when a team wins. So why would you jeopardize your joy that you have done well, and you see something that is wrong, and then you want to go ahead to do the wrong things that you know will make you unhappy, that will make everybody unhappy,” he said.

“There’s no reason why anybody would be thinking in that manner. But nobody will look at it from that perspective and they feel, no, no.

READ ALSO: Jessica Oji wins historic World U20 Shot Put gold for Nigeria

“They want to read different meanings into anything you do. Each time you go out for a match, you want to win, and you want to make sure that you present your best.”

The coach also urged supporters to show patience with players, noting that even those in good form can have an off day.

“Even players can have bad days, you see a player doing well, you have the hope that, yes, this person will do well. But when she gets onto the field of play, something else happens, and you cannot crucify the player just because maybe she didn’t do well in one game and the rest of it,” Madugu explained.

“You have to find out what went wrong and then try to find a solution to it. But we’ll continue to do our best. We’ll continue to do our best and make the team better.”

World.title: CAF Champions League: Rangers, Rivers Utd learn opponents
World.content:
CAF Champions League trophy

By Enitan Abdultawab

Rangers International and Rivers United have been drawn against their opponents for the first qualifying round of the 2026/27 CAF Champions League.

Rangers will face AS Sobemap of Benin Republic, while Rivers United have been drawn against Ivorian side San Pedro.

Rangers, who won the Nigeria Premier Football League title last season, will host AS Sobemap in the first leg at the Remo Stars Stadium in Ikenne before travelling for the return fixture.

AS Sobemap are making their continental debut after winning their first-ever league title in Benin Republic last season.

Should Rangers progress, they will face the winner between ASN Nigelec of Niger Republic and Algerian giants MC Alger in the second qualifying round, with a place in the group stage at stake.

Rivers United, meanwhile, will begin their campaign away from home against San Pedro before hosting the Ivorian side in the return leg.

San Pedro secured their first league title in Ivory Coast last season and will be hoping to carry that form into their continental campaign.

If Rivers United advance, they will meet either Uganda’s Vipers or FC Nouadhibou of Mauritania in the next qualifying round for a place in the group stage.

The first-leg fixtures are scheduled for September 4 to 6, while the return legs will take place from September 11 to 13.

Meanwhile, Nigeria will also have two representatives in the CAF Confederation Cup.

Shooting Stars have been drawn against Tunisian club CS Sfaxien, while President Federation Cup winners El-Kanemi Warriors will face Guinea-Bissau’s União Desportiva Internacional de Bissau (UDIB).

Nigeria has not had multiple clubs feature in the CAF Champions League and Confederation Cup in the same season since the 2019/20 campaign, when Enyimba and Rangers represented the country.

The four Nigerian clubs will now begin preparations for their respective continental campaigns, with the first qualifying ties scheduled for September.

World.title: Teen kills grandparents, six others in Thailand school shooting
World.content:
A teenage student in Thailand killed his grandparents before opening fire at a secondary school near Bangkok on Friday, leaving at least eight people dead, including three teachers and three students, police have said.

According to the national police, the teenager first shot his grandparents using his grandfather’s handgun before heading to Debsirin Nonthaburi School in Nonthaburi province, where he carried out the attack.

The suspect, who was a student of the school, was also reported dead after the incident. Local media reports gave conflicting accounts of whether he was killed by police or died by suicide.

Dozens of police officers and emergency responders were deployed to the school as parents rushed to pick up their children, while distressed students and staff consoled one another outside the premises.

A student, Pawarisa Maylissa, said she feared for her life during the attack, adding that she heard several gunshots from what appeared to be a floor above her classroom.

“I was afraid that I would die, and I was scared that I wouldn’t be able to pursue my dreams,” she said.

Deputy Interior Minister Polapee Suwunchwee said 15 students sustained injuries while trying to escape the scene, though they were not hit by gunfire.

Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul described the incident as a tragedy that should never have happened.

“It’s such a terrible incident. It should never have happened. How could this happen in our country?” he told reporters at Bangkok’s Government House.

Images released by local media showed the suspect wearing a purple school uniform and carrying a black cross-body bag, with bullet casings seen scattered on the ground.

Mental health workers were also deployed to the school to provide support for affected students, families and staff.

The attack has renewed concerns over gun violence in Thailand, a country with one of the highest rates of civilian gun ownership in Southeast Asia. Estimates suggest there are about 10 million firearms in circulation in the country.

Previous efforts to tighten gun control measures have failed to prevent repeated shootings.

In February, police arrested a teenager who allegedly used a police officer’s gun to kill a school principal and injure two students in southern Thailand.

In one of the country’s deadliest mass killings, an ex-police officer armed with a gun and knife attacked a nursery in northern Thailand in 2022, killing 24 children and 12 adults.

World.title: Uzodimma to Davido: I’m not an Osun voter
World.content:
Governor Hope Uzodimma

OWERRI – Imo State Governor, Senator Hope Uzodimma, has clarified that he is not a voter in Osun State and has no direct role in determining the outcome of the state’s governorship election.

Uzodimma made the clarification while distancing himself from a statement attributed to Ambrose Nwogwugwu, who described as “emotional blackmail” an appeal by music star David Adeleke, popularly known as Davido, urging the governor to use his influence to promote peace during the election.

Davido, who is a nephew of Osun State Governor and candidate of the Accord Party in the August 15, 2026 governorship election, Ademola Adeleke, had appealed to Uzodimma as the Chairman of the Progressive Governors Forum (PGF) and Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Osun State Governorship Campaign Council.

In a statement issued by his Chief Press Secretary and Special Adviser on Media, Oguwike Nwachuku, Uzodimma said he neither authorised Nwogwugwu nor anyone else to respond to Davido’s comments.

The governor described Davido as “his son” and said the musician’s presence in Osun during the election was because of his commitment to the APC and not because he was an eligible voter in the state.

“Davido remains my son. His coming to Osun for the exercise is solely because he is a committed member of the All Progressives Congress (APC), and not one of the voters in the state’s governorship election on Saturday next week or at any other time,” Uzodimma said.

He maintained that the APC had always supported peaceful, credible, free and fair elections, adding that the party would continue to seek the support of Osun voters for its candidate, Asiwaju Munirudeen Bola Oyebamiji.

Uzodimma said supporting a political candidate during an election was part of democratic practice and not an indication that party leaders or campaign officials were voters in the areas where elections were being conducted.

“It is not new in a democracy in general, and in Nigeria in particular, for party leaders and members to join their candidates and seek support for them during elections, not as electorate from the same area who are expected to cast their ballot,” he said.

The governor assured Davido of his continued respect for him and the people of Osun State, stressing that his role in the election was to support the APC candidate and promote a peaceful electoral process.

He urged Davido, Osun residents and the general public to disregard Nwogwugwu’s comments, describing them as personal opinions that did not represent his views or those of the APC campaign council.

Uzodimma said the clarification became necessary to prevent the misinterpretation of the remarks attributed to Nwogwugwu.

World.title: Norwegian football federation calls for Infantino to resign
World.content:
Infantino

The Norwegian Football Federation (NFF), among the fiercest critics of FIFA president Gianni Infantino for several years, will call for his resignation, its head Lise Klaveness said on Friday.

“He does not have the institutional trust required to lead FIFA in a stable manner in the current climate. There is no turning back for Gianni Infantino,” Klaveness told reporters.

“We are going to ask the FIFA president to resign now,” she said, a day after a meeting of the Norwegian federation’s governing bodies, which among other things examined the fate of the much-criticised FIFA chief.

He is standing for re-election for a fourth and final term next March.

President of FIFA since 2016 and currently the only declared candidate, Infantino must secure a majority of the 211 votes from the organisation’s members in order to be re-elected.

Candidates must declare by November 18.

The Italian-Swiss lawyer has come under enormous pressure since the failure of his plan — which was revealed last week — to open FIFA competitions, including the jewel in the crown the World Cup, to private investors.

AFP

World.title: 3 fire fighters injured in Abuja tanker explosion -FCT fire service
World.content:
Firefighters avert tanker explosion in Ondo

The FCT Fire Service says three of it firefighters sustained varying degrees of injuries in the Thursday night fire incident at the AYM Shafa filling station, Abuja.

The service Public Relations Officer (PRO), Ibrahim Muhammad, confirmed the development to the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) Abuja on Friday.

Mohammad said that the filling station located at Area 3 Garki, was engulfed with fire after a fuel tanker filled with petrol earlier exploded.

According to him, the service got information about the incident at about 9; 44p.m., and immediately mobilised personnel and appliances to the scene.

“Owing to the magnitude of the incident, other fire service authorities also joined the emergency response, resulting in a coordinated inter-agency firefighting operation.

“In the course of controlling and putting the fire off, three of our fire fighters were grossly injured, with one currently receiving intensive medical care at the Trauma Centre of National Hospital, Abuja.

“Medical specialists are making effort to ensure his recovery, while the other two were rushed to Alliance hospital, Area 11, Garki, Abuja and are receiving medical treatment.”

He added that the cause of the fire remained under investigation.

“Members of the public are advised to refrain from speculation and await the outcome of the official investigation,” he said.

He also said that the service appreciated the cooperation of sister emergency agencies, security personnel and members of the public who assisted in ensuring a coordinated emergency response.

He further said that the FCT fire service commended the dedication, professionalism and bravery displayed by all responding fire fighters and emergency personnel.

According to him, their prompt intervention prevented what could have resulted in an even greater disaster.

Muhammad however said that preliminary assessment revealed that the fire affected the filling station premises and adjoining structures.

“One fuel tanker loaded with approximately 45,000 litres of petroleum product was engulfed by the fire.

“Preliminary damage assessment reveals that 13 fuel dispensing pumps were within the affected facility.

“Three fuel dispensers were directly affected by the fire, while two civilian vehicles were completely burnt.

“Parts of the Federal Revenue Service (FRS) office and sections of Ahmad Plaza, a two-storey commercial building beside the station were affected by the incident,” the PRO said.

He urged operators of fuel stations, commercial facilities and members of the public to strictly comply with fire safety regulations.

Muhammad said it was imperative to ensure regular maintenance of fire protection systems and report any fire emergency immediately through the appropriate emergency channels 020-9290-6118.

He quoted the Director of the FCT fire service, Adebayo Zacchaeus, as expressing concern for the injured fire fighters and calling on members of the public to keep them in their prayers as they continue receiving treatments.

Zacchaeus said that the service remained steadfast in its commitment to protecting lives and property through prompt emergency response, public education and the enforcement of fire safety standards.

NAN reports that the emergency operation was personally supervised by the Federal Fire Service Controller General, Olumode Samuel, FCT Fire Service Director, alongside other tactical and rescue operators.

World.title: Rudeboy breaks silence after Mr P’s fresh claims about Lola, late mother
World.content:
Rudeboy

By Enitan Abdultawab

Singer Paul Okoye, popularly known as Rudeboy, has reacted to fresh allegations by his twin brother, Peter Okoye, popularly known as Mr P, concerning their late mother and Peter’s wife, Lola.

Mr P made several claims in the latest episode of his video series documenting the long-running dispute within the Okoye family.

In the eighth episode released on Thursday, he alleged that his late mother, Josephine Okoye, and other family members confronted him and Lola over their relationship shortly after the birth of their son.

According to him, a family meeting was held at his residence in Omole, Lagos, with their mother, brothers Jude, Rudeboy and Tony, as well as pastors in attendance.

Mr P alleged that neither he nor Lola was properly welcomed during the meeting.

“Everybody was seated. I went to call Lola. When she entered the room, nobody stood up or said, ‘Lola, sit down.’ Nobody even bothered to welcome her properly. Lola and I just sat on the floor,” he recounted.

Mr P further claimed that their mother told Lola that the family had decided she should end her relationship with him.

He also alleged that Jude made a derogatory comment about his infant son during the confrontation, which he said left Lola in tears.

“Lola started crying. The pastors tried to calm her. They pushed Lola out of the house,” he alleged.

Mr P further claimed that Jude and Rudeboy had opposed Lola’s pregnancy and that an anonymous email questioning the paternity of his unborn child was circulated within the family.

He, however, said their mother later acknowledged that the child was his biological son and asked his brothers to apologise to him, but that the apology never happened before her death.

Mr P also rejected claims that Lola had a poor relationship with his late mother, saying his wife supported her during her illness.

“When my mom was sick… Lola stayed with her in the hospital till midnight and took the pastors back home every day for over two months,” he said.

Rudeboy, however, has now responded to the claims in a brief social media post.

“Unfortunately, you’re not here to defend yourself. Continue resting, Mum,” he wrote.

Although Rudeboy did not directly address the specific allegations made by his brother, his statement was widely seen as a defence of their late mother.

The latest development adds another layer to the long-running dispute between the former P-Square members, which has involved disagreements over family relationships, music royalties, business management and the collapse of their reunion.

Mr P has made several allegations against Jude and other members of the family in his ongoing series, which Jude has denied and maintained that some of the issues are already before the courts.

Rudeboy, meanwhile, has largely avoided engaging in the public back-and-forth, with his management indicating that the singer remains focused on his music career.

World.title: Oro-Obolo State move: Ibibio group decries attacks on Ekid Peoples Union President
World.content:
…Backs Udonsak; Clears air on new state agitation

By Soni Daniel

The umbrella union for the Ibibio-speaking people of Akwa Ibom State, Akwa Esop Imaisong Ibibio, has criticized the attacks unleashed by their Oron-speaking people on the leader of the Ekid People’s Union, Dr. Samuel Udonsak, for exposing the antics being deployed by the Oron people to secure the creation of Oro-Obolo State out of Akwa Ibom State.

The Ekid Peoples Union President, Dr. Samuel Udonsak, had used the inauguration of the 12th International President and Executive Council of Mboho Mkparawa Ibibio International in Uyo on Friday, July 24, 2026 to expose the steps being taken by their Oro neighbours to undermine the Ibibio in their bid to secure Oro-Obolo State.

Angered by the exposure by Udonsak, Oro Union slammed the Ekid Peoples Union leader for his speech and made other remarks, which have not gone down well with the Ibibio leadership.

Dr. Samuel Udonsak, who was invited, in his capacity as the Leader of Ekid People’s Union, did say, as part of his remarks to the gathering, that contrary to their renewed claims, Oro Nation is not a littoral community, as it does not have any direct border whatsoever, wheresoever, with the Atlantic shoreline.

Among other things, Udonsak insisted that no official map in history, or any judgement/pronouncement of court in any of the various historical decided cases on the matter, has ever shown Oro Nation as a littoral region.

Udonsak also argued that the resurgence of the Oro-Obolo consciousness and its quest for (Obolo) State creation is a game plan by the Oro ethnic group to tactfully annex parts of Southern Ibibio ancestral lands into Oro Nation so as to gain access, and make inroads to the seashore in aboriginal Ibibio territory.

In response to the attack, the umbrella Ibibion union, Akwa Esop Imaisong Ibibio threw its weight behind Dr. Udonsak, arguing that what he said is nothing but the truth, which is backed by facts and figures dating many decades.

The Ibibio group stated: “Akwa Esop Imaisong Ibibio knows that the core essence of the scheme is for Oro Nation to gain land contiguity to the Obolos in Eastern Obolo LGA for the purpose of the creation of their proposed OroObolo State on parts of Ibibio soil and land.

As a conscious Ibibio leader and patriotic Akwa Ibom son, the Ekid People’s Union President further made the cogent point at the auspicious gathering, that if the Ibibio, the majority ethnic group, keep quiet and allow Oro Nation, to pull through its scheme and game plan of disconnecting the Ibibio from the Atlantic coastline, and making the coastline part and parcel of the proposed Oro-Obolo State, the economy of the rest of Akwa Ibom State and its people (the Ibibio and the Annang) will consequently be totally strangulated and emasculated with the cut-off of the State from the Atlantic Ocean and the Gulf of Guinea.

“This is the absolutely patriotic point Dr Udonsak vehemently made, not just for the Ibibio, but for the rest of Akwa Ibom people,” the Ibibio union said in a statement jointly signed by Obong P.J Okon, the Ntisong Akwa Esop Imaisong Ibibio and Obong Tony Okpon, the Secretary General of Akwa Esop Imaisong Ibibio.

“Akwa Esop Imaisong Ibibio recognizes and respects the rights of all Oro people (currently living in Oron, Okobo, Urue Offong/Oruko, Udung Uko and Mbo LGAs), Obolo people (currently living in Eastern Obolo LGA) and Ibeno people (currently living in Ibeno LGA) of Akwa Ibom State, to seek a geographical entity (State) of their own.

“Akwa Esop Imaisong Ibibio and all Ibibio people at large, however, firmly hold the position that “no village, no section, no part, no inch of any of the Ibibio LGAs in Akwa Ibom State shall be made part of the proposed Oro-Obolo State, or any other State”.

“Clearly, the President of Ekid People’s Union, Dr Samuel Udonsak, was therefore, only re-echoing and re-sounding the non-negotiable position of Akwa Esop Imaisong Ibibio and the generality of Ibibio people, at home and in the diaspora, on the matter.

“Accordingly, Akwa Esop Imaisong Ibibio does not only align with, but wholly owns up the message eloquently delivered by Dr Udonsak to the Mboho Mkparawa Ibibio International convergence on July 24, 2026 for the inauguration of the 12th International President and Executive Council of the Organization.

“The personal attacks of Oro Union, their sons and daughters on Dr. Samuel Udonsak are therefore, totally unwarranted, and Akwa Esop Imaisong Ibibio warns that the attacks should stop forthwith! There are copious historical and legal facts and evidence which confirm and affirm the full Ibibio aboriginal ownership of the ancestral lands in Esit Eket, Eket, Onna, Ikot Abasi and Mkpat Enin LGAs – that directly bound the Atlantic Ocean at various points, and which have been the core targets of agitators for the creation of a new state in the region, by way of annexure of parts thereof into the proposed Oro-Obolo State.

“Oro is NOT littoral and can never be allowed to selfishly claim such, not only wrongly and brazenly, but to the objectionable, extortionist detriment of the IBIBIO NOW AND FOR ALL TIME, EVER! NEVER! Oro can continue to benefit like any other community from the commonwealth of Akwa Ibom State in peace.

“As the majority ethnic group in the State, the Ibibio have been more than fair to all others and hopes to remain so, but being taken for granted must stop now, forthwith! Contrary to their consistent and persistent claims, Oro Nation has not been marginalized in the public affairs of the State,” the statement said.

World.title: Abeokuta North enacts anti-open grazing law, commissions projects
World.content:
By Innocent Anaba

The Chairman of Abeokuta North Local Government Area, Ogun State, Mr. Olanrewaju Oyegbola-Sodipo, has commissioned a number of development projects across the council and signed into law a bye-law banning open grazing as part of efforts to deepen grassroots development and strengthen governance.



The projects, spread across the council’s 16 wards and four major communities, include interventions in education, healthcare, rural electrification, potable water supply, sanitation, road infrastructure and public facilities.



Speaking during the commissioning, the Ogun State Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, Ganiyu Hamzat, commended the council chairman for what he described as a robust grassroots development drive.



Hamzat said the investments in schools, water infrastructure, sanitation facilities and council assets reflected responsive governance and aligned with the developmental agenda of the Ogun State government under Governor Dapo Abiodun.



In a related development, the council has enacted the Abeokuta North Local Government Bye-Law on Livestock Grazing and Herders Registration, which prohibits open grazing, makes the registration of herders and livestock owners compulsory and provides a regulatory framework for livestock management within the local government.



To facilitate implementation of the law, the council organised a stakeholders’ sensitisation programme involving traditional rulers, community leaders, security agencies, farmers, herders, market associations, transport unions, youth groups and other stakeholders.



The forum, according to the council, was aimed at educating participants on the provisions of the new legislation and creating awareness on regulations against indiscriminate waste disposal, encroachment on government property and illegal occupation of public land.



Speaking on the initiatives, Oyegbola-Sodipo said sustainable development extends beyond the execution of physical projects.



He said: “Development is not measured solely by the number of projects we execute. It is equally reflected in the institutions we build, the laws we enact, and the level of public understanding and ownership we create.



“Our approach has always been to carry our people along because lasting development can only be achieved through partnership between government and the people.”



The chairman explained that the livestock regulation was designed to promote peaceful coexistence between farmers and herders, enhance public safety, protect agricultural investments and preserve the environment.



He added that sustained consultation and civic engagement remained critical to the successful implementation of government policies.



Oyegbola-Sodipo also reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to policies that encourage investment, improve public health, safeguard public assets, promote environmental sustainability and guarantee a secure environment for residents and businesses.



He expressed appreciation to President Bola Tinubu for efforts aimed at strengthening governance and security across the country, and commended Governor Dapo Abiodun for supporting grassroots development and creating an enabling environment for local governments in Ogun State.



According to the chairman, his administration has since assuming office focused on infrastructure renewal, healthcare, education, youth empowerment, environmental management, institutional reforms and community security as key pillars of its development agenda.

World.title: Kebbi Governor Meets Security Chiefs To Review State Security Architecture
World.content:
Onuminya Innocent

Kebbi State Governor, Dr. Nasir Idris, has convened another emergency security meeting as part of renewed efforts to contain emerging security challenges in some parts of the state.

The meeting, held in Birnin Kebbi, brought together heads of security agencies and key government officials to review the current security situation and strengthen the state’s security architecture.

Briefing journalists after the closed-door session, the Commissioner for Home Affairs and Internal Security, Hon. Haliru Wasagu, said the engagement was necessitated by the need to protect lives and property across the state.

According to Wasagu, deliberations focused on assessing existing strategies, identifying gaps, and fine-tuning operational responses to ensure a more coordinated approach to emerging threats.

He stated that Governor Idris directed security agencies to intensify patrols, surveillance, and intelligence gathering in flashpoints identified during the review.

The Commissioner stressed that the governor remains unwavering in his commitment to safeguarding residents and creating an enabling environment for economic activities to thrive.

“Our Governor is fully committed to flushing out criminal elements and dismantling their hideouts. Anyone found engaging in criminal activities will face the full weight of the law,” Wasagu quoted the governor as saying.

He added that the administration has continued to invest in logistics, mobility, and welfare for security personnel to enhance their effectiveness on the ground.

Wasagu also appealed to residents to cooperate with security agencies by providing timely and credible information that could aid in the identification, apprehension, and prosecution of criminal elements.

He emphasized that public vigilance and collaboration with security operatives remain critical to winning the fight against crime and maintaining peace in communities.

The Commissioner further commended the dedication, professionalism, and sacrifices of security agencies for their sustained efforts in ensuring peace, stability, and public safety across Kebbi State.

World.title: Alleged Off-budget Expenditure: Lawmakers Demand Emergency Reconvening of N’Assembly
World.content:
•Seek independent forensic audit of all reported off-budget expenditure

•Frown on under-implementation of the 2024, 2025, 2026 Appropriation Acts

•Lament constitutional controversy surrounding the State Police Alteration Bill

Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja

A group of bi-partisan lawmakers in the House of Representatives under the aegis of Save Nigeria Group has called upon the President of the Senate, Godswill Akpabio, and the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Hon. Tajudeen Abbas, to reconvene both Chambers immediately for an emergency session.

The emergency session, the lawmakers said, must address the issue of under-implementation of the 2024, 2025 and 2026 Appropriation Acts; the constitutional controversy surrounding the State Police Constitutional Alteration Bill; and allegations of off-budget expenditure.

Other issues they want the parliament to address as a matter of urgency included: non-release of capital funds to security agencies; the deteriorating security situation; and measures required to restore public confidence in the rule of law and democratic governance.

The concerned lawmakers stated this in a statement issued Friday and jointly signed by Hon. Awaji-Inombek Abiante (NDC, Rivers); Hon. Abubakar Kusada, (APC, Katsina) and Hon. Mansur Jega (ADC, Kebbi) on behalf of the group.

The lawmakers clarified that they are neither an opposition platform nor an instrument of any political interest, rather they are legislators increasingly alarmed by the direction of Nigeria’s democracy and the growing tendency of public institutions to subordinate the Constitution.

The lawmakers lamented that Nigeria’s democracy is nosediving, adding that silence in the face of repeated constitutional violations and institutional failures could no longer be justified.

They pointed out that the country is confronting an alarming disregard for the rule of law, chronic budget under-implementation, allegations of off-budget expenditure, worsening economic hardship and an unacceptable security situation.

The concerned lawmakers emphasised that democracy cannot survive where constitutional procedures are treated as inconveniences and legal safeguards are replaced by political improvisation.

They expressed concern over the emerging pattern in which constitutionally prescribed procedures are treated as optional.

The lawmakers recalled that during the approval of the declaration of a state of emergency in Rivers State in March 2025, the National Assembly relied on voice votes despite the requirement under section 305(6) of the Constitution that the proclamation must be supported by a two-thirds majority of all members of each Chamber.

They said more recently, serious constitutional and procedural questions arose from the purported passage of the Executive State Police Constitutional Alteration Bill by the House of Representatives on 23 July 2026.

The lawmakers stated: “The Speaker announced that 311 members had voted in support of the Bill, thereby exceeding the constitutional threshold of 240 affirmative votes.

“However, some of us were physically present throughout the proceedings and can state categorically that at no time that day were as many as 240 members in the Chamber, particularly when the Bill was considered.

“The figure announced by the Speaker could only have been reached by including votes transmitted through WhatsApp by members who were absent from the Chamber at the material time.”

The lawmakers stressed that Section 9(2) of the Constitution requires the affirmative votes of not less than two-thirds of all members of each Chamber before the Constitution can be altered.

According to them, The mere announcement of figures by the Speaker cannot substitute for strict constitutional compliance.

They added: “The Constitution cannot be altered by presumption, improvisation or undisclosed voting arrangements.

“Democracy is endangered when a state of emergency can be approved through an unverifiable voice vote and the Constitution can purportedly be altered through WhatsApp messages.

“State Police may be desirable, but a desirable reform must still be established through a lawful process.”

The lawmakers further lamented that throughout the 2024, 2025 and 2026 fiscal cycles, Nigeria has experienced repeated budget extensions, rollovers and severe delays in capital implementation.

They said in 2025, the federal government indicated that only approximately 30 per cent of the 2025 capital budget would be funded, while about 70 per cent would be carried forward into 2026.

The lawmakers pointed out that it is no longer an occasional administrative delay, but a recurring breakdown of fiscal governance.

They further recalled that Senate Chief Whip, Mohammed Monguno, publicly described the failure to implement an Appropriation Act as a breach of the law capable of amounting to an “impeachable offence.”

They noted: “We agree with Senator Monguno that the deliberate or persistent refusal to implement duly enacted Appropriation Acts raises grave constitutional questions.

“Repeated rollovers weaken parliamentary oversight, confuse fiscal accountability and make it almost impossible for Nigerians to determine which projects belong to which financial year.”

To this end, the concerned lawmakers therefore demanded comprehensive budget implementation reports for the 2024, 2025 and 2026 fiscal years; full disclosure of capital releases made to every ministry, department and agency.

They further demanded reconciliation of revenues collected against expenditure authorised by the National Assembly; an explanation for the failure to release duly appropriated capital funds; and a joint parliamentary investigation into chronic budget under-implementation.

They also called for appropriate constitutional action where deliberate or unjustifiable non implementation is established.

The lawmakers said that the Appropriation Act is law, and the federal government cannot choose which laws to obey.

While decrying reports of unrecorded public expenditure, the lawmakers maintained that allegations of misappropriation must be established through competent investigation and due process.

Nevertheless, they were of the opinion that available reports provide sufficient grounds for immediate legislative scrutiny and forensic auditing.

The lawmakers also recalled that in July 2026, the International Monetary Fund reportedly stated that public expenditure equivalent to approximately two per cent of Nigeria’s Gross Domestic Product had not been recorded in recent official budgets, an amount estimated at approximately ₦8.83 trillion.

The lawmakers emphasised that the reported unrecorded expenditure was said to have contributed to a discrepancy between Nigeria’s declared fiscal deficit and its actual financing requirements.

This matter, they insisted, cannot be dismissed through public relations or general denials by the Federal Ministry of Finance.

They noted: “Public funds cannot lawfully be spent outside duly enacted Appropriation Acts, concealed under opaque accounting classifications or omitted from fiscal information presented to the National Assembly and the Nigerian people.

“This administration cannot demand sacrifice from Nigerians while public expenditure remains opaque. Every naira spent by the Government belongs to the Nigerian people.

“Those entrusted with public funds must account for how the money was appropriated, released, expended and utilised.

“Budgetary opacity is not merely an accounting problem. It is a threat to constitutional government, public trust and Nigeria’s economic survival. We call for an independent forensic audit of all reported off-budget expenditure.”

On security, the lawmakers said while the protection of lives and property is the primary responsibility of government, Nigerians continue to be killed, kidnapped and displaced by terrorists, bandits, criminal gangs and other violent groups.

The lawmakers expressed worry by Monguno’s further disclosure that some security agencies had received no capital releases despite the worsening security situation.

They said reports indicated that approximately ₦20.27 billion, representing nearly the entire budgetary provision for the Presidential Air Fleet, was released, while only a small fraction of the Nigerian Army’s allocation for security equipment was made available during the period under review.

“The question is not whether the Presidential Air Fleet should be maintained. The question is why the comfort and mobility of public officials should receive more predictable funding than the equipment, logistics, operational vehicles, aircraft maintenance and protective resources required by personnel confronting terrorists and bandits,” they posited.

Against this background, the lawmakers called for the immediate release of duly appropriated capital funds to the Armed Forces, the Nigeria Police Force, intelligence institutions and other security agencies.

The lawmakers commended the Catholic Bishops’ Conference of Nigeria for speaking candidly about insecurity, economic hardship, democratic decline and concerns about emerging one-party dominance.

They added that the Bishops have demonstrated that patriotism sometimes requires telling those in authority uncomfortable truths.

They also commended the Supreme Council for Shari’ah in Nigeria for urging caution, wider consultation and national consensus before the establishment of State Police.

The lawmakers noted that Nigeria’s present circumstances do not permit the legislature to remain away from plenary while urgent constitutional, fiscal, economic and security questions remain unresolved.

They stated: “We call upon the President of the Senate and the Speaker of the House of Representatives to reconvene both Chambers immediately for an emergency session.

“The session must address: chronic under-implementation of the 2024, 2025 and 2026 budgets; the constitutional controversy surrounding the State Police Constitutional Alteration Bill; allegations of off-budget expenditure; non-release of capital funds to security agencies; the deteriorating security situation; and measures required to restore public confidence in the rule of law and democratic governance.”

They said the National Assembly is not merely an institution for passing Executive Bills and approving requests from the Presidency, but an independent arm of government constitutionally empowered to represent the people, defend the Constitution, appropriate public funds, conduct oversight and hold the Executive accountable.

The lawmakers stated categorically that while they are not opposed to State Police, economic reform or necessary public expenditure, they are however opposed to unconstitutional procedures, legislative shortcuts, unimplemented budgets, opaque expenditure and the continuing failure to protect the Nigerian people.

World.title: Women Lead Campaign Against Open Defecation in Abuja
World.content:
Michael Olugbode in Abuja

Women leaders from 16 communities in Kundu Ward of Kwali Area Council, Federal Capital Territory (FCT), have launched a community-driven campaign aimed at ending open defecation and improving hygiene practices across the ward.

The initiative, being implemented by the Resource Conservation and Development Initiative International (RCDI), seeks to harness the influence of women at the grassroots level to promote sanitation awareness, encourage toilet use and strengthen healthy behavioural practices within households and communities.

The intervention is being carried out under RCDI’s ThriveFlow programme on women’s health, dignity and community resilience, with support from ActionAid Nigeria through the Renewed Women’s Voice and Leadership–Nigeria Project funded by Global Affairs Canada. The programme is being implemented in partnership with the FCT Rural Water Supply and Sanitation Agency (RUWASSA).

Speaking during the training of women sanitation champions in Kwali, RCDI Programme Officer, Mary-Jane Adaku Ukaegbu, said the project was designed to place women at the forefront of efforts to achieve Open Defecation Free (ODF) status in Kundu Ward.

She said women play critical roles in household hygiene, childcare, water management and community mobilisation, making them effective advocates for behavioural change and improved sanitation practices.

According to Ukaegbu, 80 women drawn from the 16 participating communities will be trained and deployed to conduct house-to-house sensitisation campaigns, educate families on proper sanitation and monitor progress toward ODF attainment.

She explained that the women would serve as sanitation champions, encouraging residents to consistently use toilets, wash their hands at critical times, maintain clean surroundings and eliminate open defecation.

The programme also incorporates menstrual hygiene education and support for women and adolescent girls. As part of the intervention, reusable sanitary pad kits will be distributed to selected beneficiaries to improve menstrual hygiene management and promote dignity among women and girls.

The WASH Coordinator of Kwali Area Council, Mrs. Aminat Dada, commended RCDI, ActionAid Nigeria and FCT RUWASSA for supporting efforts to improve sanitation standards in the area council.

She noted that Kwali Area Council had continued to implement sensitisation programmes to encourage toilet construction and usage, adding that the women-led intervention would complement existing government efforts and accelerate progress towards ODF status.

Dada described the initiative as timely and urged traditional rulers, community leaders and residents to support the women champions in their mobilisation activities to ensure lasting behavioural change.

One of the participants, Mrs. Ruth Abu, Women Leader of Sadaba Community, said the training had equipped participants with practical knowledge on hygiene, environmental sanitation and disease prevention.

She pledged to take the lessons learnt back to her community and mobilise households to adopt healthier sanitation practices.

Stakeholders expressed confidence that the women-led approach would strengthen community ownership of sanitation programmes, improve public health outcomes and contribute significantly to the attainment of Open Defecation Free status across Kundu Ward and neighbouring communities.

World.title: Afikuyomi Commends Tinubu’s Directive on Osun Accounts
World.content:
Sunday Ehigiator

Legal practitioner and Principal Partner at Liberty Semper Fidelis LP, Mr. Tokunbo Afikuyomi, has commended President Bola Tinubu’s directive to the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) to return to court and seek the discharge of the order freezing the accounts of the Osun State Government, describing it as a demonstration of commitment to electoral fairness and constitutional governance.

In a statement issued yesterday, Afikuyomi said the president’s intervention came at a time when public confidence in the neutrality of state institutions was under scrutiny, noting that the decision underscored the need for elections to be not only free and fair but also perceived as such by Nigerians.

He argued that by directing the EFCC to approach the court instead of pursuing any extra-judicial solution, the president had respected the constitutional process governing judicial orders.

According to him, while the president’s objective of protecting the credibility of the forthcoming Osun State governorship election deserves commendation, it must be pursued within the framework of the constitution.

According to him, “The directive issued today (yesterday) by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu instructing the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) to return to court and seek the discharge of the order freezing the accounts of the Osun State Government deserves commendation.”

He added that the EFCC remains a statutory body whose investigative and prosecutorial powers are exercised under the law, while the freezing order was issued by a court of competent jurisdiction and could only be reviewed, varied or discharged through due judicial process.

“The law equally provides the mechanism for such an order to be reviewed, varied or discharged upon a proper application. By directing the Commission to return to court rather than seek any extra-judicial resolution, the President has ensured that the matter remains where the Constitution requires it to be resolved: before the judiciary,” he stated.

Afikuyomi further stressed that Nigeria’s constitutional order is anchored on the separation of powers and the independence of institutions, noting that these principles are strengthened when each arm of government performs its constitutional responsibilities without encroaching on the authority of another.

He urged that the president’s concern for safeguarding the integrity of the Osun State governorship election should continue to be reflected in respect for the operational independence of investigative agencies and the constitutional authority of the courts.

The lawyer also called on all institutions expected to play roles in the conduct of the election to emulate the president’s stance.

He listed the Nigeria Police Force, the Armed Forces, the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), election observers, National Youth Service Corps members serving as ad hoc electoral officials, transport and logistics providers, universities whose academics may serve as returning officers, political parties, candidates, the media and the judiciary as stakeholders that should be guided by the commitment to electoral integrity.

According to him, the president’s intervention aligns with the democratic credentials that have characterised much of his public life, and serves as a reminder that protecting the integrity of elections is a collective constitutional responsibility.

Afikuyomi concluded by stressing that elections in Nigeria must always reflect the freely expressed will of the people, insisting that every public institution, political actor and citizen has a duty to uphold democracy and the rule of law.

“Our elections must reflect the freely expressed will of the Nigerian people. Free and fair elections are not negotiable. Every public institution, politician, and citizen bears a duty to protect that principle. History will ultimately judge not merely the outcome of elections but whether those entrusted with public authority discharged their responsibilities with fidelity to democracy and the rule of law,” he said.

World.title: Preserve PDP Unity, Saraki Urges Leaders, Stakeholders
World.content:
Hammed Shittu in Ilorin

Former Senate President, Dr. Abubakar Bukola Saraki, has urged Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) leaders and supporters to preserve the unity that has continued to strengthen the PDP across Kwara State, stressing that the party’s leadership is working seriously to ensure the electoral victory of the party in the state in the 2027 general election.

Saraki made the submissions in Ilorin Thursday during a meeting held with PDP leaders and stakeholders from Kwara North l and Kwara South senatorial districts of the state.

The meeting was attended by the PDP governorship candidate, Mr. Suleiman Bolakale Kawu; his running mate, Rev. C.O.S. Fawenu; the party’s National Assembly candidates from the two senatorial districts; members of the State Working Committee; party elders and other key stakeholders.

According to a statement signed by the Press Officer on Local Matters to the former Senate President, Abdulganiyu Abdulqadir, Saraki told the PDP leaders that all PDP candidates had been successfully uploaded to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) portal, fulfilling the assurance he had earlier given party members.

“As I assured our members earlier, all our candidates have now been successfully uploaded to the INEC portal. This marks another important step in our preparations for the 2027 elections,” he said.

He commended party members for their patience, confidence and steadfastness throughout the nomination process, describing the successful upload of candidates as another milestone in the party’s preparations for the polls.

Saraki also applauded the growing wave of defections into the PDP across Kwara North and Kwara South, saying the increasing support for the party reflects the people’s desire for purposeful leadership and good governance.

“What gives me even greater confidence is what is happening across both senatorial districts, where people are joining the PDP in droves because they see our great party as the only credible alternative for good governance,” he stated.

The former Senate President urged party leaders and supporters to preserve the unity that has continued to strengthen the PDP across the state, stressing that the party’s greatest asset remains its discipline and ability to work together.

“As our numbers grow, so does our responsibility to remain one family. I appeal to our leaders and supporters to accommodate one another and place the collective interest of the party above personal ambition.

“Our unity and discipline remain our greatest strengths,” Saraki said.

Reaffirming his commitment to the party’s success, Saraki pledged to continue providing every necessary support to the PDP and its candidates ahead of the 2027 elections.

“For my part, I will continue to give our party and our candidates all the support they require. With unity, commitment and hard work, victory is within our reach,” he added.

The stakeholders, in separate remarks, reaffirmed their confidence in Saraki’s leadership and pledged to intensify grassroots mobilization across Kwara North and Kwara South, expressing optimism that the PDP is well positioned to reclaim power in the state in 2027.

World.title: EnergyNet Honours NIWIMNRO for Driving Women’s Inclusion in Nigeria’s Mining Sector
World.content:
Folalumi Alaran in Abuja

The Nigerian Indigenous Women in Mining and Natural Resources Organisation (NIWIMNRO) has received an EnergyNet Leadership Award in recognition of its efforts in advancing women’s participation and leadership in Nigeria’s mining and natural resources sector.

The award, presented at the organisation’s Abuja office on Thursday, acknowledged NIWIMNRO’s contributions to promoting gender inclusion through advocacy, capacity building, policy engagement and community development initiatives aimed at empowering women across the extractive value chain.

Receiving the award, the Executive Director of NIWIMNRO, Felicia Dairo, described the recognition as a validation of the organisation’s sustained commitment to breaking barriers for women in a sector traditionally dominated by men.

She said the honour extends beyond the organisation itself to celebrate the resilience and achievements of women who continue to make significant contributions to the growth of Nigeria’s mining industry.

“This recognition is not just about our organisation; it is about the women who continue to break barriers in a sector that has traditionally been dominated by men. It is a celebration of their resilience, determination and contributions to the growth of the mining industry,” she said.

Dairo noted that NIWIMNRO was established to address gender disparities within the extractive sector and has since championed initiatives that improve women’s access to opportunities, strengthen their capacity and promote gender-responsive mining governance.

She disclosed that over the past year, the organisation had trained more than 200 women artisanal miners across six states on technical mining skills, occupational safety and business development to improve their productivity and economic prospects.

According to her, NIWIMNRO has also provided medical support and distributed personal protective equipment (PPE) to women miners to address health and safety concerns prevalent in mining communities.

Beyond capacity development, she said the organisation had installed two solar-powered boreholes in underserved mining communities across two states to improve access to clean water, with plans underway to construct two additional boreholes.

Speaking at the presentation, Editorial and Content Manager of EnergyNet, Charlotte Lamb, commended NIWIMNRO for equipping women miners with knowledge on their rights, workplace safety and financial management.

She also praised the organisation for supporting women to form cooperatives capable of securing mining licences and participating in formal commercial activities within the industry.

Lamb further highlighted NIWIMNRO’s efforts to establish aggregation hubs for strategic minerals, including lithium, gold and tin, to improve mineral grading and strengthen integration into the formal mining value chain.

Dairo said the recognition reinforces the importance of sustained investment in women-led initiatives to unlock the full potential of Africa’s natural resources.

According to her, empowering women in the mining sector would not only strengthen communities but also build a more resilient and sustainable extractive industry.

She expressed appreciation to EnergyNet for recognising the organisation’s vision and reaffirmed NIWIMNRO’s commitment to expanding opportunities for women artisanal miners, supporting mining communities and advocating policies that promote equity, safety and sustainable development across Nigeria’s mining sector.

World.title: As Leadership Crisis Rocks Ondo Assembly…
World.content:
Fidelis David reports that a deepening crisis in the Ondo State House of Assembly has exposed cracks within the state’s political establishment, with far-reaching implications for governance, legislative independence and the ruling All Progressives Congress as the 2027 elections draw closer.

For a state that only recently celebrated a relatively peaceful governorship election, Ondo has suddenly found itself confronting a different political battle, one being fought not on campaign grounds but within the hallowed chambers of the State House of Assembly.

What began last week as allegations surrounding the handling of an alleged N44 million released by the Ondo State Oil Producing Areas Development Commission (OSOPADEC) has snowballed into perhaps the gravest leadership crisis to confront the 10th Assembly since its inauguration.

At the centre of the storm is the Speaker of the House, Hon Olamide Oladiji, who has come under intense scrutiny over allegations of financial impropriety, lack of transparency and poor leadership. More specifically, some lawmakers accused him of failing to carry members along in the disbursement of the funds, a development that has fuelled growing discontent within the legislature.

The crisis, according to sources within the Assembly, is not limited to the office of the Speaker. It is also believed to have implications for the Deputy Speaker, Hon Ololade Gbegudu, while the Clerk of the House, Benjamin Jaiyeola, may equally be affected through a possible redeployment as part of efforts to restore stability.

One of the sources claimed that the Speaker had contemplated resigning last Monday ahead of a possible discussion of the matter during Tuesday’s plenary but was prevailed upon to shelve the decision.

“The Speaker contemplated resigning but did not go ahead with it. The issue is connected to an alleged N44 million involving funds released by OSOPADEC to the Assembly. The money was meant for the entire House, but there are allegations that the Speaker did not carry other lawmakers along in handling the funds,” the source alleged.

Another source attributed the Speaker’s decision to remain in office to the intervention of a prominent political figure in the state. “The Speaker wanted to resign today but did not eventually do so because of political intervention. We will see what happens tomorrow,” the source added.

However, Oladiji has dismissed the allegations in their entirety. In a statement, he described reports of an impending resignation, leadership crisis and alleged mismanagement of OSOPADEC funds as “sensationalised, malicious and entirely fabricated.”

“We state unequivocally, without an atom of ambiguity, that Rt. Hon. Olamide Oladiji never contemplated resigning, nor is there any leadership crisis within the 10th Ondo State House of Assembly. The report is a total figment of the imagination of its authors and their nameless sources,” the statement read.

The Speaker further maintained that lawmakers independently determine and manage their welfare and resource allocations, insisting that he only receives what is constitutionally due to his office. It added that claims he sidelined members in the handling of the alleged N44 million OSOPADEC fund were “a manufactured lie designed to create artificial disaffection where none exists.”

Speaking with newsmen, Oladiji also denied claims that 21 lawmakers had demanded his resignation. “I’m not aware of that,” he said. He equally dismissed allegations linking him to an alleged assassination plot against a fellow lawmaker.

“I’m a law-abiding citizen. I’m a Christian; I don’t believe in all that. Let her come up with evidence to confirm such allegations,” he stated.

But even as the Speaker sought to calm the growing controversy, the crisis assumed another dimension after the member representing Ilaje Constituency II, Olawumi Fayemi-Obayelu, alleged in a Facebook post that she narrowly escaped death following threats aimed at stopping what she described as her investigation into alleged bribery, forgery and corruption involving the Speaker and OSOPADEC.

The lawmaker accused the Speaker of attempting to intimidate her and reaffirmed what she described as the position of two-thirds of the House, urging him to resign or “face the consequences” of his actions. She also alleged that funds meant for her constituency were being diverted, insisting she would not be intimidated.

Rather than easing tension, the controversy has since widened into allegations of executive interference. Chairman of the House Committee on Information and spokesperson of the Assembly, Hon. Olatunji Fabiyi, alleged that Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa had been making efforts to persuade lawmakers to abandon the impeachment process against the Speaker.

Fabiyi claimed that 21 of the 26 lawmakers had already endorsed Oladiji’s removal and insisted there was no going back on what he described as the collective decision of the House.

The spokesperson said the lawmakers had resolved not to hold plenary until a new speaker is elected. “We have resolved not to hold plenary until there is a change of Speaker.

“We still have seven days to go because I have the opinion that the government is calling some members that they should backpedal on the issue of impeachment,” Fabiyi said.

He questioned what he described as Governor Aiyedatiwa’s interest in the matter, insisting that the impeachment move was purely an internal affair of the legislature.

“Twenty-one members have signed an impeachment against Mr. Speaker. To me, I don’t know the interest of Mr. Governor. Unless the government is telling us that they have something in common,” he stated.

According to Fabiyi, lawmakers had already informed the governor that their grievances were directed solely at the leadership of the Assembly and not at his administration.

“I have spoken to Mr. Governor already and we have made it very clear to him that we don’t have anything against him. We simply don’t want our leadership again. There is no reason why somebody should continue to perpetrate himself over us when we don’t want him anymore,” he added.

The lawmaker further argued that leadership changes within the legislature fall squarely within the constitutional powers of the House and urged the governor to refrain from interfering. “It is exclusively a private affair of the House. It is not an executive affair. If there is no hidden agenda, I see no reason why Mr. Governor should be protecting one Speaker. And if there is a hidden agenda, let him say it to the whole world now,” he declared.

Fabiyi maintained that allowing the impeachment process to run its constitutional course would restore peace to the Assembly. “Mr. Governor should just allow peace to reign in the House by allowing Mr. Speaker to step aside. It is the resolution of the whole House that Mr. Speaker should go. No going back.”

He also disclosed that lawmakers initially believed the governor requested seven days to intervene but later realised the appeal was for a 14-day window. “At the initial stage, we thought it was seven days that Mr. Governor requested from us, but it is clear to us that he begged for 14 days, not seven days. The 14 days will last till next Sunday,” Fabiyi added.

Perhaps the most disturbing aspect of the crisis is not the impeachment threat itself but the allegation that legislative activities have virtually ground to a halt.

Lawmakers claim the Assembly has held only four plenary sittings in the last seven months. Should that allegation prove accurate, it would inevitably raise serious questions about compliance with Section 104 of the 1999 Constitution, which requires every State House of Assembly to sit for not less than 181 days in a legislative year. More importantly, it raises concerns about whether the Assembly is adequately performing its constitutional responsibilities of lawmaking, oversight and representation at a time when the state faces pressing economic and security challenges.

It is pertinent to state that beyond the immediate battle for the Speakership, the unfolding crisis carries significant political implications for the ruling APC ahead of the 2027 general elections. Internal wrangling within the legislature could deepen divisions within the party, weaken public confidence in its leadership and provide opposition parties with fresh political ammunition.

A prolonged impasse may also strain the relationship between the executive and legislative arms of government, slowing policy implementation and undermining governance at a period when citizens expect greater attention to infrastructure, security, healthcare and economic development.

However, a political analyst, Kehinde Ogunkorode, believes the crisis presents an opportunity for the APC leadership to demonstrate its capacity for internal conflict resolution.

“Rather than allowing the disagreement to degenerate into a prolonged institutional crisis, the party must encourage dialogue, transparency and strict adherence to constitutional procedures. Any perception of undue interference from outside the legislature, could further inflame tensions and erode public trust in democratic institutions.”

He noted that the biggest losers in any prolonged legislative crisis are not the politicians but the people of Ondo State.

“Every day consumed by political infighting is a day lost in debating bills, scrutinising government spending and addressing the pressing needs of constituents. The Assembly exists to serve the people, not to become an arena for endless power struggles.

“How the Assembly and the APC manage this crisis may ultimately shape not only the future of the 10th Assembly but also the political fortunes of the ruling party in Ondo State as the countdown to the 2027 elections gathers momentum”, he added.

Even as the political standoff persisted, the crisis took another dramatic turn on Wednesday when lawmakers convened a parliamentary meeting at the Assembly Complex in Akure and announced the constitution of a four-member panel to investigate and audit the Assembly’s accounts, including the Speaker’s alleged role in the management of its finances.

Significantly, Speaker Oladiji and his deputy, Hon. Ololade Gbegudu, were absent from the meeting, while the Majority Leader, Hon. Olatunji Oshati, presided over proceedings.

Briefing reporters after the session, Chairman of the House Committee on Information, Hon. Olatunji Ifabiyi, said the decision to constitute the probe panel underscored the lawmakers’ commitment to transparency and accountability.

He explained that members were compelled to reconvene after weeks of inactivity in order to resume their constitutional responsibilities of lawmaking and oversight.

Ifabiyi also dismissed claims that lawmakers had accepted inducements to abandon the impeachment process against the Speaker, insisting that no member had compromised. He maintained that the impeachment move remained alive but had been temporarily suspended to allow the leadership of the All Progressives Congress mediate in the dispute.

World.title: Elumelu: Firebrand Whose Voice Has Shaped Nigeria’s Parliamentary Discourse
World.content:
Jonathan Eze writes that parliamentarians with a demonstrable record of legislative engagements like Hon Ndudi Elumelu are likely to play an important role in enriching debates and strengthening oversight in the House of Representatives in the coming 11th National Assembly, as he’s set to once again get the nod of the electorate in Aniocha/Oshimili Federal Constituency.

In every democratic legislature, there are lawmakers who merely occupy seats, and there are those whose presence fundamentally shape national conversations. Over the years, Hon. Ndudi Elumelu, representing Aniocha/Oshimili Federal Constituency of Delta State in the House of Representatives, has consistently belonged to the latter category.

Through a combination of rigorous legislative engagement, fearless oversight, articulate debate, and constituency-focused representation, Elumelu has carved out a reputation as one of the National Assembly’s most influential parliamentarians.

His legislative career has been defined not by loud political theatrics but by strategic interventions on issues that touch governance, accountability, national development, and the welfare of ordinary Nigerians. Whether serving as Minority Leader of the House of Representatives or participating in critical committee assignments, Elumelu has demonstrated an uncommon ability to combine political diplomacy with principled advocacy.

As conversations gradually shift towards the composition of the 11th and subsequent National Assemblies after the 2027 general elections, many political observers argue that lawmakers with deep institutional knowledge and proven legislative competence will be indispensable to preserving the quality of parliamentary deliberations. Within that conversation, Elumelu’s name frequently emerges as one of the most experienced voices whose continued presence could strengthen legislative capacity.

A Career Built on Legislative Substance

Unlike many politicians whose public image rests primarily on electoral victories, Elumelu’s profile has largely been constructed around his performance. Throughout his years in the House of Representatives, he has developed a reputation for approaching national issues through careful analysis, constitutional interpretation, and policy-oriented debate.

His contributions at plenary have often reflected a deep understanding of legislative procedure and the broader implications of public policy.

His tenure as Minority Leader particularly elevated his national profile. At a period marked by intense political competition, Elumelu demonstrated remarkable restraint, often choosing constructive engagement over unnecessary confrontation.

While providing robust opposition where necessary, he equally supported initiatives considered beneficial to national development, reinforcing the idea that legislative effectiveness is measured by ideas rather than partisan rhetoric.

This balanced approach earned him respect across party lines, illustrating that parliamentary leadership is often built on credibility rather than volume.

Power Sector Probe Reinforces His Oversight Credentials

Among the defining moments of Elumelu’s legislative career was his leadership of one of Nigeria’s most significant investigations into the country’s troubled electricity sector.

The probe into the management of billions of dollars invested in Nigeria’s power sector attracted nationwide attention because electricity remains one of the country’s greatest developmental challenges.

For decades, successive administrations invested enormous financial resources into generation, transmission, and distribution with results that many Nigerians considered disappointing.

Serving as Chairman of the House Ad Hoc Committee investigating the power sector, Elumelu supervised extensive hearings involving government agencies, electricity operators, regulators, contractors, and other stakeholders. The investigation sought to answer critical questions surrounding project implementation, expenditure, policy consistency, institutional coordination, and the overall value obtained from massive public investments.

Regardless of differing political opinions surrounding the eventual recommendations, the exercise underscored one fundamental principle: parliament remains a critical institution for democratic accountability.

The probe demonstrated Elumelu’s willingness to confront difficult governance questions and reinforced his image as a legislator committed to strengthening oversight, the constitutional responsibility through which the National Assembly scrutinizes executive actions and public expenditure. For many analysts, the investigation remains one of the most ambitious oversight exercises undertaken by the House of Representatives in recent history.

Effective Representation of Delta State

Beyond national politics, Elumelu’s political relevance is perhaps most evident in Delta State, where he has remained closely connected to his constituents. Over his terms, he has consistently advocated and implemented critical legacy projects and interventions aimed at improving infrastructure, education, youth empowerment, healthcare delivery, and economic opportunities within Aniocha/Oshimili Federal Constituency and beyond.

His constituency engagement reflects an understanding that effective representation extends beyond legislative debates in Abuja. Town hall meetings, educational support initiatives, skills acquisition programmes, road projects, community development efforts, and youth empowerment schemes have remained central components of his political philosophy.

His accessibility to constituents has also strengthened his electoral appeal. In an era where many elected officials become increasingly distant after elections, Elumelu maintained regular interaction with community leaders, traditional institutions, youth groups, women associations, and professional bodies. Such engagement has contributed significantly to sustaining his political relevance within Delta politics.

Parliamentarian Driven by Consensus

One defining characteristic of Elumelu’s legislative style is his preference for consensus building. The Nigerian Parliament often brings together lawmakers with diverse ideological, regional, ethnic, and partisan interests. Successfully navigating such complexity requires negotiation, patience, and emotional intelligence.

Observers have frequently noted Elumelu’s ability to build bridges across political divides, facilitating cooperation on issues of national importance without sacrificing the constitutional role of legislative scrutiny. This approach became particularly evident during his leadership of the minority caucus, where balancing party interests with national responsibilities required exceptional political maturity.

Rather than reducing parliamentary debates to partisan contests, he consistently projected the legislature as an institution whose ultimate responsibility lies with the Nigerian people.

Strengthening Democratic Institutions. Perhaps Elumelu’s most enduring contribution lies in his commitment to institutional development.

Healthy democracies thrive when legislatures effectively perform three constitutional responsibilities: lawmaking, oversight, and representation. Throughout his parliamentary career, Elumelu has demonstrated appreciation for these responsibilities, frequently emphasizing transparency, accountability, constitutionalism, and responsible governance.

His interventions have often reflected concern for strengthening institutions rather than promoting personalities. This institutional mindset distinguishes experienced legislators from politicians whose influence depends solely on executive patronage or temporary political alignments.

As democratic systems mature, institutional memory becomes increasingly valuable. Legislators who understand parliamentary traditions, committee procedures, constitutional boundaries, and legislative negotiation often play important roles in mentoring newer members and preserving the effectiveness of parliamentary governance.

Looking Towards 2027

With political activities gathering momentum ahead of the 2027 elections, discussions surrounding legislative experience are expected to feature prominently.

As Elumelu gears up to secure another mandate from his constituents, the House of Representatives and of course the National Assembly would retain one of its experienced parliamentarians with extensive knowledge of legislative processes, committee oversight, and parliamentary leadership.

His presence would likely provide institutional continuity and contribute to informed legislative debates on complex national issues, particularly in areas of governance reform, public accountability, infrastructure, and economic development. Ultimately, however, that decision rests with the electorate, who will determine whether his legislative record merits renewed confidence at the polls.

Legacy Beyond Politics

Every public servant is ultimately judged not by campaign promises but by measurable contributions to democratic governance. For Elumelu, his legacy continues to be shaped by years of active participation in national lawmaking, his prominent role in high-profile oversight investigations, his leadership within the House of Representatives, and his sustained engagement with constituents in Delta State.

His parliamentary journey illustrates the enduring importance of experienced legislators in strengthening democratic institutions. It also highlights how effective representation requires more than occupying public office; it demands intellectual preparation, policy understanding, political courage, and an unwavering commitment to public service.

Elumelu’s legislative trajectory places him among those whose contributions have significantly shaped debates within Nigeria’s House of Representatives, while his future political relevance will ultimately continue to be assessed by the quality of his service and the confidence reposed in him by the electorate.

World.title: New twist in St Stithians tragedy as police open murder case
World.content:
St Stithians teenagers Cameron Waldeck-Cooks, a Grade 11 learner, and Ethan Coetzee died at a lodge in Sabie. Police have since opened a murder case. Images: St Stithians

Police have opened a murder case following postmortem findings into the deaths of St Stithians teenagers Cameron Waldeck-Cooks, a Grade 11 learner, and 19-year-old Ethan Coetzee, who were found dead at a lodge in Sabie, Mpumalanga.

Police respond to lodge

The South African Police Service (SAPS) said officers were called to the lodge on Monday, 3 August, at about 07:50 after reports that two people had been found dead.

When officers arrived, they found the bodies of a 19-year-old man and a 17-year-old girl. Both were declared dead at the scene.



Police initially registered an inquest docket.

Postmortem changes direction of investigation

The investigation took a new turn after the postmortem examination.

According to SAPS, the results suggest the 17-year-old girl may have been strangled, while the 19-year-old man may have taken his own life.



Police have since added a murder charge to the investigation.

“The postmortem results suggests that the 17-year-old female may have been strangled, while the 19-year-old male may have taken his own life,” SAPS said.

Investigation continues

Police said the investigation is ongoing to establish the full circumstances surrounding the deaths.



On Tuesday, St Stithians College shared two separate posts about the tragic deaths of Ethan Coetzee and Cameron Waldeck-Cooks.
